3.17.d: समिध्यमानः परथमानु धर्मा समक्तुभिरज्यते विश्ववारः | शोचिष्केशो घर्तनिर्णिक पावकः सुयज्ञो अग्निर्यजथाय देवान ||
3.17.e: DULY enkindled after ancient customs, bringing all treasures, he is balmed with unguents,—  Flame-haired, oil-clad, the purifying Agni, skilled in fair rites, to bring the Gods for worship.

3.17.d: यथायजो होत्रमग्ने पर्थिव्या यथा दिवो जातवेदश्चिकित्वान | एवानेन हविषा यक्षि देवान मनुष्वद यज्ञं पर तिरेममद्य ||
3.17.e: As thou, O Agni, skilful Jātavedas, hast sacrificed as Priest of Earth, of Heaven,  So with this offering bring the Gods, and prosper this sacrifice today as erst for Manu.

3.17.d: तरीण्यायूंषि तव जातवेदस्तिस्र आजानीरुषसस्ते अग्ने | ताभिर्देवानामवो यक्षि विद्वानथा भव यजमानाय शं योः ||
3.17.e: Three are thy times of life, O Jātavedas, and the three mornings are thy births, O Agni.  With these, well-knowing, grant the Gods’ kind favour, and help in stir and stress the man who worships.

3.17.d: अग्निं सुदीतिं सुद्र्शं गर्णन्तो नमस्यामस्त्वेड्यं जातवेदः | तवां दूतमरतिं हव्यवाहं देवा अक्र्ण्वन्नम्र्तस्य नाभिम ||
3.17.e: Agni most bright and fair with song we honour, yea, the adorable, O Jātavedas.  Thee, envoy, messenger, oblation-bearer, the Gods have made centre of life eternal.

3.17.d: यस्त्वद धोता पूर्वो अग्ने यजीयान दविता च सत्ता सवधया च शम्भुः तस्यानु धर्म पर यजा चिकित्वो.अथ नो धा अध्वरं देववीतौ ||
3.17.e: That Priest before thee, yet more skilled in worship, stablished of old, health-giver by his nature,—  After his custom offer, thou who knowest, and lay our sacrifice where Gods may taste it.

3.18.d: भवा नो अग्ने सुमना उपेतौ सखेव सख्ये पितरेव साधुः | पुरुद्रुहो हि कषितयो जनानां परति परतीचीर्दहतादरातीः ||
3.18.e: AGNI, be kind to us when we approach thee good as a friend to friend, as sire and mother.  The races of mankind are great oppressors burn up malignity that strives against us.

3.18.d: तपो शवग्ने अन्तरानमित्रान तपा शंसमररुषः परस्य | तपो वसो चिकितानो अचित्तान वि ते तिष्ठन्तामजरा अयासः ||
3.18.e: Agni, burn up the unfriendly who are near us, burn thou the foeman's curse who pays no worship.  Burn, Vasu, thou who markest well, the foolish: let thine eternal nimble beams surround thee.

3.18.d: इध्मेनाग्न इछमानो घर्तेन जुहोमि हव्यं तरसे बलाय | यावदीशे बरह्मणा वन्दमान इमां धियं शतसेयाय देवीम ||
3.18.e: With fuel, Agni, and with oil, desirous, mine offering I present for strength and conquest,  With prayer, so far as I have power, adoring-this hymn divine to gain a hundred treasures.

3.18.d: उच्छोचिषा सहसस पुत्र सतुतो बर्हद वयः शशमानेषु धेहि | रेवदग्ने विश्वामित्रेषु शं योर्मर्म्र्ज्मा ते तन्वं भूरि कर्त्वः ||
3.18.e: Give with thy glow, thou Son of Strength, when lauded, great vital power to those who toil to serve thee.  Give richly, Agni, to the Viśvāmitras in rest and stir. Oft have we decked thy body.

3.18.d: कर्धि रत्नं सुसनितर्धनानां स घेदग्ने भवसि यत समिद्धः | सतोतुर्दुरोणे सुभगस्य रेवत सर्प्रा करस्ना दधिषे वपूंषि ||
3.18.e: Give us, O liberal Lord, great store of riches, for, Agni, such art thou when duly kindled.  Thou in the happy singer's home bestowest, amply with arms extended, things of beauty.

3.19.d: अग्निं होतारं पर वर्णे मियेधे गर्त्सं कविं विश्वविदममूरम | स नो यक्षद देवताता यजीयान राये वाजाय वनतेमघानि ||
3.19.e: AGNI, quick, sage, infallible, all-knowing, I choose to be our Priest at this oblation.  In our Gods’ service he, best skilled, shall worship: may he obtain us boons for strength and riches.

3.19.d: पर ते अग्ने हविष्मतीमियर्म्यछा सुद्युम्नां रातिनीं घर्ताचीम | परदक्षिणिद देवतातिमुराणः सं रातिभिर्वसुभिर्यज्ञमश्रेत ||
3.19.e: Agni, to thee I lift the oil-fed ladle, bright, with an offering, bearing our oblation.  From the right hand, choosing the Gods’ attendance, he with rich presents hath arranged the worship.

3.19.d: स तेजीयसा मनसा तवोत उत शिक्ष सवपत्यस्य शिक्षोः | अग्ने रायो नर्तमस्य परभूतौ भूयाम ते सुष्टुतयश्च वस्वः ||
3.19.e: Of keenest spirit is the man thou aidest give us good offspring, thou who givest freely.  In power of wealth most rich in men. O Agni, of thee, the Good, may we sing forth fair praises.

3.19.d: भूरीणि हि तवे दधिरे अनीकाग्ने देवस्य यज्यवो जनासः | स आ वह देवतातिं यविष्ठ शर्धो यदद्य दिव्यंयजासि ||
3.19.e: Men as they worship thee the God, O Agni, have set on thee full many a brilliant, aspect.  So bring Most Youthful One, the Gods’ assembly, the Heavenly Host which thou to-day shalt honour.

3.19.d: यत तवा होतारमनजन मियेधे निषादयन्तो यजथाय देवाः | स तवं नो अग्ने.अवितेह बोध्यधि शरवांसि धेहि नस्तनूषु ||
3.19.e: When Gods anoint thee Priest at their oblation, and seat thee for thy task as Sacrificer,  O Agni, be thou here our kind defender, and to ourselves vouchsafe the gift of glory.

3.20.d: अग्निमुषसमश्विना दधिक्रां वयुष्टिषु हवते वह्निरुक्थैः | सुज्योतिषो नः शर्ण्वन्तु देवाः सजोषसो अध्वरं वावशानाः ||
3.20.e: WITH lauds at break of morn the priest invoketh Agni, Dawn, Dadhikrās, and both the Aśvins.  With one consent the Gods whose light is splendid, longing to taste our sacrifice, shall hear us.

3.20.d: अग्ने तरी ते वाजिना तरी षधस्था तिस्रस्ते जिह्वा रतजात पूर्वीः | तिस्र उ ते तन्वो देववातास्ताभिर्नः पाहि गिरो अप्रयुछन ||
3.20.e: Three are thy powers, O Agni, three thy stations, three are thy tongues, yea, many, Child of Order!  Three bodies hast thou which the Gods delight in: with these protect our hymns with care unceasing.

3.20.d: अग्ने भूरीणि तव जातवेदो देव सवधावो.अम्र्तस्य नाम | याश्च माया मायिनां विश्वमिन्व तवे पूर्वीः सन्दधुःप्र्ष्टबन्धो ||
3.20.e: O Agni, many are the names thou bearest, immortal, God, Divine, and Jātavedas.  And many charms of charmers, All-Inspirer! have they laid in thee, Lord of true attendants!

3.20.d: अग्निर्नेता भग इव कषितीनां दैवीनां देव रतुपा रतावा | स वर्त्रहा सनयो विश्ववेदाः पर्षद विश्वाति दुरिता गर्णन्तम ||
3.20.e: Agni, like Bhaga, leads the godly people, he who is true to Law and guards the seasons.  Ancient, all-knowing, he the Vṛtra-slayer shall bear the singer safe through every trouble.

3.20.d: ददहिक्रामग्निमुषसं च देवीं बर्हस्पतिं सवितारं चदेवम | अश्विना मित्रावरुणा भगं च वसून रुद्रानादित्यानिह हुवे ||
3.20.e: I call on Savitar the God, on Morning, Bṛhaspati, and Dadhikrās, and Agni,  On Varuṇa and Mitra, on the Aśvins, Bhaga, the Vasus, Rudras and Ādityas.

3.21.d: इमं नो यज्ञमम्र्तेषु धेहीमा हव्या जातवेदो जुषस्व | सतोकानामग्ने मेदसो घर्तस्य होतः पराशान परथमो निषद्य ||
3.21.e: SET this our sacrifice among the Immortals: be pleased with these our presents, Jātavedas.  O Priest, O Agni, sit thee down before us, and first enjoy the drops of oil and fatness.

3.21.d: घर्तवन्तः पावक ते सतोका शचोतन्ति मेदसः | सवधर्मन देववीतये शरेष्ठं नो धेहि वार्यम ||
3.21.e: For thee, O Purifier, flow the drops of fatness rich in oil.  After thy wont vouchsafe to us the choicest boon that Gods may feast.

3.21.d: तुभ्यं सतोका घर्तश्चुतो.अग्ने विप्राय सन्त्य | रषिः शरेष्ठः समिध्यसे यज्ञस्य पराविता भव ||
3.21.e: Agni, Most Excellent! for thee the Sage are drops that drip with oil.  Thou art enkindled as the best of Seers. Help thou the sacrifice.

3.21.d: तुभ्यं शचोतन्त्यध्रिगो शचीव सतोकासो अग्ने मेदसो घर्तस्य | कविशस्तो बर्हता भानुनागा हव्या जुषस्व मेधिर ||
3.21.e: To thee, O Agni, mighty and resistless, to thee stream forth the drops of oil and fatness.  With great light art thou come, O praised by poets! Accept our offering, O thou Sage.

3.21.d: ओजिष्ठं ते मध्यतो मेद उद्भ्र्तं पर ते वयं ददामहे | शचोतन्ति ते वसो सतोका अधि तवचि परति तान देवशो विहि ||
3.21.e: Fatness exceeding rich, extracted from the midst,—this as our gift we offer thee.  Excellent God, the drops run down upon thy skin. Deal them to each among the Gods.

3.22.d: अयं सो अग्निर्यस्मिन सोममिन्द्रः सुतं दधे जठरे वावशानः | सहस्रिणं वाजमत्यं न सप्तिं ससवान सन सतूयसे जातवेदः ||
3.22.e: THIS is that Agni whence the longing Indra took the pressed Soma deep within his body.  Winner of spoils in thousands, like a courser, with praise art thou exalted, Jātavedas.

3.22.d: अग्ने यत ते दिवि वर्चः पर्थिव्यां यदोषधीष्वप्स्वा यजत्र | येनान्तरिक्षमुर्वाततन्थ तवेषः स भानुरर्णवो नर्चक्षाः ||
3.22.e: That light of thine in heaven and earth, O Agni, in plants, O Holy One, and in the waters,  Wherewith thou hast spread wide the air's mid-region-bright is that splendour, wavy, man-beholding.

3.22.d: अग्ने दिवो अर्णमछा जिगास्यछा देवानूचिषे धिष्ण्याये | या रोचने परस्तात सूर्यस्य याश्चावस्तादुपतिष्ठण्त आपः ||
3.22.e: O Agni, to the sea of heaven thou goest: thou hast called hither Gods beheld in spirit.  The waters, too, come hither, those up yonder in the Sun's realm of light, and those beneath it.

3.22.d: पुरीष्यासो अग्नयः परावणेभिः सजोषसः | जुषन्तां यज्ञमद्रुहो.अनमीवा इषो महीः ||
3.22.e: Let fires that dwell in mist, combined with those that have their home in floods,  Guileless accept our sacrifice, great viands free from all disease.
Agni, as holy food to thine invoker give wealth in cattle, lasting, rich in marvels.  To us be born a son and spreading offspring. Agni, be this thy gracious will to us-ward.

3.23.d: निर्मथितः सुधित आ सधस्थे युवा कविरध्वरस्य परणेता | जूर्यत्स्वग्निरजरो वनेष्वत्रा दधे अम्र्तं जातवेदाः ||
3.23.e: RUBBED into life, well stablished in the dwelling, Leader of sacrifice, the Sage, the youthful,  Here in the wasting fuel Jātavedas, eternal, hath assumed immortal being.

3.23.d: अमन्थिष्टां भारता रेवदग्निं देवश्रवा देववातः सुदक्षम | अग्ने वि पश्य बर्हताभि रायेषां नो नेता भवतादनु दयून ||
3.23.e: Both Bharatas, Devaśravas, Devāvata, have strongly rubbed to life effectual Agni.  O Agni, look thou forth with ample riches: be, every day, bearer of food to feed us.

3.23.d: दश कषिपः पूर्व्यं सीमजीजनन सुजातं मात्र्षु परियम | अग्निं सतुहि दैववातं देवश्रवो यो जनानामसद वशी ||
3.23.e: Him nobly born of old the fingers ten produced, him whom his Mothers counted dear.  Praise Devāvata's Agni, thou Devaśravas, him who shall be the people's Lord.

3.23.d: नि तवा दधे वर आ पर्थिव्या इळायास पदे सुदिनत्वे अह्नाम | दर्षद्वत्यां मानुष आपयायां सरस्वत्यां रेवदग्नेदिदीहि ||
3.23.e: He set thee in the earth's most lovely station, in Iḷā's place, in days of fair bright weather.  On man, on Āpayā, Agni! on the rivers Dṛṣadvati, Sarasvatī, shine richly.
Agni, as holy food to thine invoker give wealth in cattle, lasting, rich in marvels.  To us be born a son and spreading offspring Agni, be this thy gracious will to us-ward

3.24.d: अग्ने सहस्व पर्तना अभिमातीरपास्य | दुष्टरस्तरन्नरातीर्वर्चो धा यज्ञवाहसे ||
3.24.e: AGNI, subdue opposing bands, and drive our enemies away.  Invincible, slay godless foes: give splendour to the worshipper.

3.24.d: अग्न इळा समिध्यसे वीतिहोत्रो अमर्त्यः | जुषस्व सू नो अध्वरम ||
3.24.e: Lit with libation, Agni, thou, deathless, who callest Gods to feast,  Accept our sacrifice with joy.

3.24.d: अग्ने दयुम्नेन जाग्र्वे सहसः सूनवाहुत | एदं बर्हिः सदो ||
3.24.e: With splendour, Agni, Son of Strength, thou who art worshipped, wakeful One.  Seat thee on this my sacred grass.
With all thy fires, with all the Gods, Agni, exalt the songs we sing.  And living men in holy rites.

3.24.d: अग्ने विश्वेभिरग्निभिर्देवेभिर्महया गिरः | यज्ञेषु यौ चायवः ||
3.24.e: Grant, Agni, to the worshipper wealth rich in heroes, plenteous store,  Make thou us rich with many sons.

3.24.d: अग्ने दा दाशुषे रयिं वीरवन्तं परीणसम | शिशीहि नः सूनुमतः ||

3.25.d: अगने दिवः सूनुरसि परचेतास्तना पर्थिव्या उत विश्ववेदाः | रधग देवानिह यजा चिकित्वः ||
3.25.e: THOU art the sapient Son of Dyaus, O Agni, yes and the Child of Earth, who knowest all things.  Bring the Gods specially, thou Sage, for worship.

3.25.d: अग्निः सनोति वीर्याणि विद्वान सनोति वाजमम्र्ताय भूषन | स नो देवानेह वहा पुरुक्षो ||
3.25.e: Agni the wise bestows the might of heroes grants strengthening food, preparing it for nectar.  Thou who art rich in food bring the Gods hither.

3.25.d: अग्निर्द्यावाप्र्थिवी विश्वजन्ये आ भाति देवी अम्र्ते अमूरः | कषयन वाजैः पुरुश्चन्द्रो नमोभिः ||
3.25.e: Agni, infallible, lights Earth and Heaven, immortal Goddesses gracious to all men,—  Lord through his strength, splendid through adorations.

3.25.d: अग्न इन्द्रश्च दाशुषो दुरोने सुतावतो यज्ञमिहोप यातम | अमर्धन्ता सोमपेयाय देवा ||
3.25.e: Come to the sacrifice, Agni and Indra come to the offerer's house who hath the Soma.  Come, friendly-minded, Gods, to drink the Soma.

3.25.d: अग्ने अपां समिध्यसे दुरोणे नित्यः सूनो सहसो जातवेदः | सधस्थानि महयमान ऊती ||
3.25.e: In the floods' home art thou enkindled, Agni, O Jātavedas, Son of Strength, eternal,  Exalting with thine help the gathering-places.

3.26.d: वैश्वानरं मनसाग्निं निचाय्या हविष्मन्तो अनुषत्यं सवर्विदम | सुदानुं देवं रथिरं वसूयवो गीर्भी रण्वंकुशिकासो हवामहे ||
3.26.e: REVERING in our heart Agni Vaiśvānara, the finder of the light, whose promises are true,  The liberal, gladsome, car-borne God we Kuśikas invoke him with oblation, seeking wealth with songs.

3.26.d: तं शुभ्रमग्निमवसे हवामहे वैश्वानरं मातरिश्वानमुक्थ्यम | बर्हस्पतिं मनुषो देवतातये विप्रं शरोतारमतिथिं रघुष्यदम ||
3.26.e: That Agni, bright, Vaiśvānara, we invoke for help, and Mātariśvan worthy of the song of praise;  Bṛhaspati for man's observance of the Gods, the Singer prompt to hear, the swiftly-moving guest.

3.26.d: अश्वो न करन्दञ जनिभिः समिध्यते वैश्वानरः कुशिकेभिर्युगे-युगे | स नो अग्निः सुवीर्यं सवश्व्यं दधातु रत्नमम्र्तेषु जाग्र्विः ||
3.26.e: Age after age Vaiśvānara, neighing like a horse, is kindled with the women by the Kuśikas.  May Agni, he who wakes among Immortal Gods, grant us heroic strength and wealth in noble steeds.

3.26.d: पर यन्तु वाजास्तविषीभिरग्नयः शुभे सम्मिष्लाः पर्षतीरयुक्षत | बर्हदुक्षो मरुतो विश्ववेदसः पर वेपयन्तिपर्वतानदाभ्याः ||
3.26.e: Let them go forth, the strong, as flames of fire with might. Gathered for victory they have yoked their spotted deer.  Pourers of floods, the Maruts, Masters of all wealth, they who can ne’er be conquered, make the mountains shake.

3.26.d: अग्निश्रियो मरुतो विश्वक्र्ष्टय आ तवेषमुग्रमव ईमहे वयम | ते सवानिनो रुद्रिया वर्षनिर्णिजः सिंहा न हेषक्रतवः सुदानवः ||
3.26.e: The Maruts, Friends of men, are glorious as the fire: their mighty and resplendent succour we implore.  Those storming Sons of Rudra clothed in robes of rain, boon-givers of good gifts, roar as the lions roar.

3.26.d: वरातं-वरातं गणं-गणं सुशस्तिभिरग्नेर्भामं मरुतामोज ईमहे | पर्षदश्वासो अनवभ्रराधसो गन्तारो यज्ञं विदथेषु धीराः ||
3.26.e: We, band on band and troop following troop, entreat with fair lauds Agni's splendour and the Maruts’ might,  With spotted deer for steeds, with wealth that never fails, they, wise Ones, come to sacrifice at our gatherings.

3.26.d: अग्निरस्मि जन्मना जातवेदा घर्तं मे चक्षुरम्र्तं म आसन | अर्कस्त्रिधातू रजसो विमानो.अजस्रो घर्मो हविरस्मि नाम ||
3.26.e: Agni am I who know, by birth, all creatures. Mine eye is butter, in my mouth is nectar.  I am light threefold, measurer of the region exhaustless heat am I, named burnt-oblation.

3.26.d: तरिभिः पवित्रैरपुपोद धयर्कं हर्दा मतिं जयोतिरनु परजानन | वर्षिष्ठं रत्नमक्र्त सवधाभिरादिद दयावाप्र्थिवी पर्यपश्यत ||
3.26.e: Bearing in mind a thought with light accordant, he purified the Sun with three refinings;  By his own nature gained the highest treasure, and looked abroad over the earth and heaven.

3.26.d: शतधारमुत्समक्षीयमाणं विपश्चितं पितरं वक्त्वानाम | मेळिं मदन्तं पित्रोरुपस्थे तं रोदसी पिप्र्तं सत्यवाचम ||
3.26.e: The Spring that fails not with a hundred streamlets, Father inspired of prayers that men should utter,  The Sparkler, joyous in his Parents' bosorn, -him, the Truth-speaker, sate ye, Earth and Heaven.

3.27.d: पर वो वाजा अभिद्यवो हविष्मन्तो घर्ताच्या | देवाञ जिगातिसुम्नयुः ||
3.27.e: IN ladle dropping oil your food goes in oblation up to heaven,  Goes to the Gods in search of bliss.

3.27.d: ईळे अग्निं विपश्चितं गिरा यज्ञस्य साधनम | शरुष्टीवानं धितावानम ||
3.27.e: Agni I laud, the Sage inspired, crowner of sacrifice through song,  Who listens and gives bounteous gifts.

3.27.d: अग्ने शकेम ते वयं यमं देवस्य वाजिनः | अति दवेषांसि तरेम ||
3.27.e: O Agni, if we might obtain control of thee the potent God,  Then should we overcome our foes.
Kindled at sacrifices he is Agni, hallower, meet for praise,  With flame for hair: to him we seek.

3.27.d: पर्थुपाजा अमर्त्यो घर्तनिर्णिक सवाहुतः | अग्निर्यज्ञस्य हव्यवाट ||
3.27.e: Immortal Agni, shining far, enrobed with oil, well worshipped, bears  The gifts of sacrifice away.

3.27.d: तं सबाधो यतस्रुच इत्था धिया यज्ञवन्तः | आ चक्रुरग्निमूतये ||
3.27.e: The priests with ladles lifted up, worshipping here with holy thought,  Have brought this Agni for our aid.

3.27.d: होता देवो अमर्त्यः पुरस्तादेति मायया | विदथानि परचोदयन ||
3.27.e: Immortal, Sacrificer, God, with wondrous power he leads the way,  Urging the great assembly on.

3.27.d: वाजी वाजेषु धीयते.अध्वरेषु पर णीयते | विप्रो यज्ञस्य साधनः ||
3.27.e: Strong, he is set on deeds ofstrength. In sacrifices led in front,  As Singer he completes the rite.

3.27.d: धिया चक्रे वरेण्यो भूतानां गर्भमा दधे | दक्षस्यपितरं तना ||
3.27.e: Excellent, he was made by thought. The Germ of beings have I gained,  Yea, and die Sire of active strength.

3.27.d: नि तवा दधे वरेण्यं दक्षस्येळा सहस्क्र्त | अग्ने सुदीतिमुशिजम ||
3.27.e: Thee have I stablished, Excellent, O strengthened by the sage's prayer,  Thee, Agni, longing, nobly bright.

3.27.d: अग्निं यन्तुरमप्तुरं रतस्य योगे वनुषः | विप्रा वाजैः समिन्धते ||
3.27.e: Agni, the swift and active One, singers, at time of sacrifice,  Eagerly kindle with their food.

3.27.d: ऊर्जो नपातमध्वरे दीदिवांसमुप दयवि | अग्निमीळे कविक्रतुम ||
3.27.e: Agni the Son of Strength who shines up to the heaven in solemn rites,  The wise of heart, I glorify.
Meet to be lauded and adored, showing in beauty through the dark,  Agni, the Strong, is kindled well.
Agni is kindled as a bull, like a horsebearer of the Gods:  Men with oblations worship him.

3.27.d: वर्षो अग्निः समिध्यते.अश्वो न देववाहनः | तं हविष्मन्त ईळते ||
3.27.e: Thee will we kindle as a bull, we who are Bulls ourselves, O Bull.  Thee, Agni, shining mightily.

3.27.d: वर्षणं तवा वयं वर्षन वर्षणः समिधीमहि | अग्ने दीद्यतं बर्हत ||

3.28.d: अग्ने जुषस्व नो हविः पुरोळाशं जातवेदः | परातःसावेधियावसो ||
3.28.e: AGNI who knowest all, accept our offering and the cake of meal,  At dawn's libation, rich in prayer!

3.28.d: पुरोळा अग्ने पचतस्तुभ्यं वा घा परिष्क्र्तः | तं जुषस्व यविष्ठ्य ||
3.28.e: Agni, the sacrificial cake hath been prepared and dressed for thee:  Accept it, O Most Youthful God.

3.28.d: अग्ने वीहि पुरोळाषमाहुतं तिरोह्न्यम | सहसः सूनुरस्यध्वरे हितः ||
3.28.e: Agni, enjoy the cake of meal and our oblation three days old:  Thou, Son of Strength, art stablished at our sacrifice.

3.28.d: माध्यन्दिने सवने जातवेदः पुरोळाशमिह कवे जुषस्व | अग्ने यह्वस्य तव भागधेयं न पर मिनन्ति विदथेषु धीराः ||
3.28.e: Here at the midday sacrifice enjoy thou the sacrificial cake, wise, Jātavedas!  Agni, the sages in assemblies never minish the portion due to thee the Mighty.

3.28.d: अग्ने तर्तीये सवने हि कानिषः पुरोळाशं सहसः सूनवाहुतम | अथा देवेष्वध्वरं विपन्यया धा रत्नवन्तमम्र्तेषु जाग्र्विम ||
3.28.e: O Agni, at the third libation takewith joy the offered cake of sacrifice, thou, Son of Strength.  Through skill in song bear to the Gods our sacrifice, watchful and fraught with riches, to Immortal God.

3.28.d: अग्ने वर्धान आहुतिं पुरोळाशं जातवेदः | जुषस्व तिरोह्न्यम ||
3.28.e: O waxing Agni, knower, thou, of all, accept our gifts, the cake,  And that prepared ere yesterday.

3.29.d: अस्तीदमधिमन्थनमस्ति परजननं कर्तम | एतां विश्पत्नीमा भराग्निं मन्थाम पूर्वथा ||
3.29.e: HERE is the gear for friction, here tinder made ready for the spark.  Bring thou the Matron: we will rub Agni in ancient fashion forth.

3.29.d: अरण्योर्निहितो जातवेदा गर्भ इव सुधितो गर्भिणीषु | दिवे-दिव ईड्यो जाग्र्वद्भिर्हविष्मद्भिर्मनुष्येभिरग्निः ||
3.29.e: 1n the two fire-sticks Jātavedas lieth, even as the well-set germ in pregnant women,  Agni who day by day must be exalted by men who watch and worship with oblations.

3.29.d: उत्तानायामव भरा चिकित्वान सद्यः परवीता वर्षणं जजान | अरुषस्तूपो रुशदस्य पाज इळायास पुत्रो वयुने.अजनिष्ट ||
3.29.e: Lay this with care on that which lies extended: straight hath she borne the Steer when made prolific.  With his red pillar—radiant is his splendour—in our skilled task is born the Son of Iḷā.

3.29.d: इळायास्त्वा पदे वयं नाभा पर्थिव्या अधि | जातवेदो नि धीमह्यग्ने हव्याय वोळ्हवे ||
3.29.e: In Iḷā's place we set thee down, upon the central point of earth,  That, Agni Jātavedas, thou mayst bear our offerings to the Gods.

3.29.d: मन्थता नरः कविमद्वयन्तं परचेतसमम्र्तं सुप्रतीकम | यज्ञस्य केतुं परथमं पुरस्तादग्निं नरो जनयता सुशेवम ||
3.29.e: Rub into life, ye men, the Sage, the guileless, Immortal, very wise and fair to look on.  O men, bring forth the most propitious Agni, first ensign of the sacrifice to eastward.

3.29.d: यदी मन्थन्ति बाहुभिर्वि रोचते.अश्वो न वाज्यरुषो वनेष्वा | चित्रो न यामन्नश्विनोरनिव्र्तः परि वर्णक्त्यश्मनस्त्र्णा दहन ||
3.29.e: When with their arms they rub him straight he shineth forth like a strong courser, red in colour, in the wood.  Bright, checkless, as it were upon the Aśvins' path, he passeth by the stones and burneth up the grass.

3.29.d: जातो अग्नी रोचते चेकितानो वाजी विप्रः कविशस्तः सुदानुः | यं देवास ईड्यं विश्वविदं हव्यवाहमदधुरध्वरेषु ||
3.29.e: Agni shines forth when born, observant, mighty, the bountiful, the Singer praised by sages;  Whom, as adorable and knowing all things, Gods set at solemn rites as offering-bearer.

3.29.d: सीद होतः सव उ लोके चिकित्वान सादया यज्ञं सुक्र्तस्य योनौ | देवावीर्देवान हविषा यजास्यग्ने बर्हद यजमाने वयो धाः ||
3.29.e: Set thee, O Priest, in, thine own place, observant: lay down the sacrifice in the home of worship.  Thou, dear to Gods, shalt serve them with oblation: Agni, give long life to the sacrificer.

3.29.d: कर्णोत धूमं वर्षणं सखायो.अस्रेधन्त इतन वाजमछ | अयमग्निः पर्तनाषाट सुवीरो येन देवासो असहन्त दस्यून ||
3.29.e: Raise ye a mighty smoke, my fellow-workers! Ye shall attain to wealth without obstruction.  This Agni is the battle-winning Hero by whom the Gods have overcome the Dasyus.

3.29.d: अयं ते योनिर्र्त्वियो यतो जातो अरोचथाः | तं जानन्नग्न आ सीदाथा नो वर्धया गिरः ||
3.29.e: This is thine ordered place of birth whence sprung to life thou shonest forth.  Knowing this, Agni, sit thee down, and prosper thou the songs we sing.

3.29.d: तनूनपादुच्यते गर्भ आसुरो नराशंसो भवति यद विजायते | मातरिश्वा यदमिमीत मातरि वातस्य सर्गो अभवत्सरीमणि ||
3.29.e: As Germ Celestial he is called Tanūnapāt, and Narāśaṁsa born diffused in varied shape.  Formed in his Mother he is Mātariśvan; he hath, in his course, become the rapid flight of wind.

3.29.d: सुनिर्मथा निर्मथितः सुनिधा निहितः कविः | अग्ने सवध्वरा कर्णु देवान देवयते यज ||
3.29.e: With strong attrition rubbed to life, laid down with careful hand, a Sage,  Agni, make sacrifices good, and for the pious bring the Gods.

3.29.d: अजीजनन्नम्र्तं मर्त्यासो.अस्रेमाणं तरणिं वीळुजम्भम | दश सवसारो अग्रुवः समीचीः पुमांसं जातमभि सं रभन्ते ||
3.29.e: Mortals have brought to life the God Immortal, the Conqueror with mighty jaws, unfailing.  The sisters ten, unwedded and united, together grasp the Babe, the new-born Infant.

3.29.d: पर सप्तहोता सनकादरोचत मातुरुपस्थे यदशोचदूधनि | न नि मिषति सुरणो दिवे-दिवे यदसुरस्य जठरादजायत ||
3.29.e: Served by the seven priests, he shone forth from ancient time, when in his Mother's bosom, in her lap, he glowed.  Giving delight each day he closeth not his eye, since from the Asura's body hewas brought to life.

3.29.d: अमित्रायुधो मरुतामिव परयाः परथमजा बरह्मणो विश्वमिद विदुः | दयुम्नवद बरह्म कुशिकास एरिर एक-एको दमे अग्निं समीधिरे ||
3.29.e: Even as the Maruts, onslaughts who attack the foe, those born the first of all knew the full power of prayer.  The Kuśikas have made the glorious hymn ascend, and, each one singly in his home, have kindled fire.

3.29.d: यदद्य तवा परयति यज्ञे अस्मिन होतश्चिकित्वो.अव्र्णीमहीह | धरुवमया धरुवमुताशमिष्ठाः परजानन विद्वानुप याहि सोमम ||
3.29.e: As we, O Priest observant, have elected thee this day, what time the solemn sacrifice began,  So surely hast thou worshipped, surely hast thou toiled: come thou unto the Soma, wise and knowing all.

3.30.d: इछन्ति तवा सोम्यासः सखायः सुन्वन्ति सोमं दधति परयांसि | तितिक्षन्ते अभिशस्तिं जनानामिन्द्र तवदा कश्चन हि परकेतः ||
3.30.e: THE friends who offer Soma long to find thee: they pour forth Soma and present their viands.  They bear unmoved the cursing of the people, for all our wisdom comes from thee, O Indra.

3.30.d: न ते दूरे परमा चिद रजांस्या तु पर याहि हरिवो हरिभ्याम | सथिराय वर्ष्णे सवना कर्तेमा युक्ता गरावाणः समिधाने अग्नौ ||
3.30.e: Not far for thee are mid-air's loftiest regions: start hither, Lord of Bays, with thy Bay Horses.  Made for the Firm and Strong are these libations. The pressing-stones are set and fire is kindled.

3.30.d: इन्द्रः सुशिप्रो मघवा तरुत्रो महाव्रातस्तुविकूर्मिर्र्घावान | यदुग्रो धा बाधितो मर्त्येषु कव तया ते वर्षभ वीर्याणि ||
3.30.e: Fair cheeks hath Indra, Maghavan, the Victor, Lord of a great host, Stormer, strong in action.  What once thou didst in might when mortals vexed thee,—where now, O Bull, are those thy hero exploits?

3.30.d: तवं हि षमा चयावयन्नच्युतान्येको वर्त्रा चरसि जिघ्नमानः | तव दयावाप्र्थिवी पर्वतासो.अनु वरताय निमितेव तस्थुः ||
3.30.e: For, overthrowing what hath ne’er been shaken, thou goest forth alone destroying Vṛtras.  For him who followeth thy Law the mountains and heaven and earth stand as if firmly stablished.

3.30.d: उताभये पुरुहूत शरवोभिरेको दर्ळ्हमवदो वर्त्रहा सन | इमे चिदिन्द्र रोदसी अपारे यत संग्र्भ्णा मघवन काशिरित ते ||
3.30.e: Yea, Much-invoked! in safety through thy glories alone thou speakest truth as Vṛtra's slayer.  E’en these two boundless worlds to thee, O Indra, what time thou graspest them, are but a handful.

3.30.d: पर सू त इन्द्र परवता हरिभ्यां पर ते वज्रः परम्र्णन्नेतु शत्रून | जहि परतीचो अनूचः पराचो विश्वं सत्यंक्र्णुहि विष्टमस्तु ||
3.30.e: Forthwith thy Bay steeds down the steep, O Indra, forth, crushing foemen, go thy bolt of thunder!  Slay those who meet thee, those who flee, who follow: make all thy promise true; be all completed.

3.30.d: यस्मै धायुरदधा मर्त्यायाभक्तं चिद भजते गेह्यं सः | भद्रा त इन्द्र सुमतिर्घ्र्ताची सहस्रदाना पुरुहूत रातिः ||
3.30.e: The man to whom thou givest as Provider enjoys domestic plenty undivided.  Blest, Indra, is thy favour dropping fatness: thy worship, Much-invoked! brings gifts in thousands.

3.30.d: सहदानुं पुरुहूत कषियन्तमहस्तमिन्द्र सं पिणक कुणारुम | अभि वर्त्रं वर्धमानं पियारुमपादमिन्द्र तवसा जघन्थ ||
3.30.e: Thou, Indra, Much-invoked! didst crush to pieces Kunaru handless fiend who dwelt with Danu.  Thou with might, Indra, smotest dead the scorner, the footless Vṛtra as he waxed in vigour.

3.30.d: नि सामनामिषिरामिन्द्र भूमिं महीमपारां सदने ससत्थ | अस्तभ्नाद दयां वर्षभो अन्तरिक्षमर्षन्त्वापस्त्वयेह परसूताः ||
3.30.e: Thou hast established in her seat, O Indra, the level earth, vast, vigorous, unbounded.  The Bull hath propped the heaven and air's mid-region. By thee sent onward let the floods flow hither.

3.30.d: अलात्र्णो वल इन्द्र वरजो गोः पुरा हन्तोर्भयमानो वयार | सुगान पथो अक्र्णोन निरजे गाः परावन वाणीः पुरुहूतं धमन्तीः ||
3.30.e: He who withheld the kine, in silence I yielded in fear before thy blow, O Indra.  He made paths easy to drive forth the cattle. Loud-breathing praises helped the Much-invoked One.

3.30.d: एको दवे वसुमती समीची इन्द्र आ पप्रौ पर्थिवीमुत दयाम | उतान्तरिक्षादभि नः समीक इषो रथीः सयुजः शूर वाजान ||
3.30.e: Indra alone filled full the earth and heaven, the Pair who meet together, rich in treasures.  Yea, bring thou near us from the air's mid-region strength, on thy car, and wholesome food, O Hero.

3.30.d: दिशः सूर्यो न मिनाति परदिष्टा दिवे-दिवे हर्यश्वप्रसूताः | सं यदानळ अध्वन आदिदश्वैर्विमोचनं कर्णुते तत तवस्य ||
3.30.e: Sūrya transgresses not the ordered limits set daily by the Lord of Tawny Coursers.  When to the goal he comes, his journey ended, his Steeds he looses: this is Indra's doing.

3.30.d: दिद्र्क्षन्त उषसो यामन्नक्तोर्विवस्वत्या महि चित्रमनीकम | विश्वे जानन्ति महिना यदागादिन्द्रस्य कर्म सुक्र्तापुरूणि ||
3.30.e: Men gladly in the course of night would look on the broad bright front of the refulgent Morning;  And all acknowledge, when she comes in glory, the manifold and goodly works of Indra.

3.30.d: महि जयोतिर्निहितं वक्षणास्वामा पक्वं चरति बिभ्रती गौः | विश्वं सवाद्म सम्भ्र्तमुस्रियायां यत सीमिन्द्रो अदधाद भोजनाय ||
3.30.e: A mighty splendour rests upon her bosom: bearing ripe milk the Cow, unripe, advances.  All sweetness is collected in the Heifer, sweetness which Indra made for our enjoyment.

3.30.d: इन्द्र दर्ह्य यामकोशा अभूवन यज्ञाय शिक्ष गर्णते सखिभ्यः | दुर्मायवो दुरेवा मर्त्यासो निषङगिणो रिपवो हन्त्वासः ||
3.30.e: Barring the way they come. Be firm, O Indra; aid friends to sacrifice and him who singeth.  These must be slain by thee, malignant mortals, armed with ill arts, our quiverbearing foemen.

3.30.d: सं घोषः शर्ण्वे.अवमैरमित्रैर्जही नयेष्वशनिं तपिष्ठाम | वर्श्चेमधस्ताद वि रुजा सहस्व जहि रक्षो मघवन रन्धयस्व ||
3.30.e: A cry is beard from enemies most near us: against them send thy fiercest-flaming weapon.  Rend them from under, crush them and subdue them. Slay, Maghavan, and make the fiends our booty.

3.30.d: उद वर्ह रक्षः सहमूलमिन्द्र वर्श्चा मध्यं परत्यग्रंश्र्णीहि | आ कीवतः सललूकं चकर्थ बरह्मद्विषे तपुषिं हेतिमस्य ||
3.30.e: Root up the race of Rākṣasas, O Indra rend it in front and crush it in the middle.  How long hast thou bebaved as one who wavers? Cast thy hot dart at him who hates devotion:

3.30.d: सवस्तये वाजिभिश्च परणेतः सं यन महीरिष आसत्सिपूर्वीः | रायो वन्तारो बर्हतः सयामास्मे अस्तु भग इन्द्रप्रजावान ||
3.30.e: When borne by strong Steeds for our weal, O Leader, thou seatest thee at many noble viands.  May we be winners of abundant riches. May Indra be our wealth with store of children.

3.30.d: आ नो भर भगमिन्द्र दयुमन्तं नि ते देष्णस्य धीमहि पररेके | ऊर्व इव पप्रथे कामो अस्मे तमा पर्ण वसुपते वसूनाम ||
3.30.e: Bestow on us resplendent wealth. O Indra let us enjoy thine overflow of bounty.  Wide as a sea our longing hath expanded, fulfil it, O thou Treasure-Lord of treasures.

3.30.d: इमं कामं मन्दया गोभिरश्वैश्चन्द्रवता राधसा पप्रथश्च | सवर्यवो मतिभिस्तुभ्यं विप्रा इन्द्राय वाहःकुशिकासो अक्रन ||
3.30.e: With kine and horses satisfy this longing with very splendid bounty skill extend it.  Seeking the light, with hymns to thee, O Indra, Kuśikas have brought their gift, the singers.

3.30.d: आ नो गोत्रा दर्द्र्हि गोपते गाः समस्मभ्यं सनयो यन्तु वाजाः | दिवक्षा असि वर्षभ सत्यशुष्मो.अस्मभ्यं सु मघवन बोधि गोदाः ||
3.30.e: Lord of the kine, burst the kine's stable open: cows shall be ours, and strength that wins the booty.  Hero, whose might is true, thy home is heaven: to us, O Maghavan, grant gifts of cattle.

3.30.d: शुनं हुवेम मघवानमिन्द्रमस्मिन भरे नर्तमं वाजसातौ | शर्ण्वन्तमुग्रमूतये समत्सु घनन्तं वर्त्राणि संजितं धनानाम ||
3.30.e: Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best Hero in this fight where spoil is gathered,  The Strong who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.

3.31.d: शासद वह्निर्दुहितुर्नप्त्यं गाद विद्वान रतस्य दीधितिंसपर्यन | पिता यत्र दुहितुः सेकं रञ्जन सं शग्म्येन मनसा दधन्वे ||
3.31.e: WISE, teaching, following the thought of Order, the sonless gained a grandson from his daughter.  Fain, as a sire, to see his child prolific, he sped to meet her with an eager spirit.

3.31.d: न जामये तान्वो रिक्थमारैक चकार गर्भं सनितुर्निधानम | यदी मातरो जनयन्त वह्निमन्यः कर्ता सुक्र्तोरन्य रन्धन ||
3.31.e: The Son left not his portion to the brother, he made a home to hold him who should gain, it.  What time his Parents gave the Priest his being, of the good pair one acted, one promoted.

3.31.d: अग्निर्जज्ञे जुह्वा रेजमानो महस पुत्रानरुषस्य परयक्षे | महान गर्भो मह्या जातमेषां मही परव्र्द धर्यश्वस्य यज्ञैः ||
3.31.e: Agni was born trembling with tongue that flickered, so that the Red's great children should be honoured.  Great is their germ, that born of them is mighty, great the Bays' Lord's approach through sacrifices.

3.31.d: अभि जैत्रीरसचन्त सप्र्धानं महि जयोतिस्तमसो निरजानन | तं जानतीः परत्युदायन्नुषासः पतिर्गवामभवदेक इन्द्रः ||
3.31.e: Conquering bands upon the Warrior waited: they recognized great light from out the darkness.  The conscious Dawns went forth to meet his coming, and the sole Master of the kine was Indra.

3.31.d: वीळौ सतीरभि धीरा अत्र्न्दन पराचाहिन्वन मनसा सप्तविप्राः | विश्वामविन्दन पथ्यां रतस्य परजानन्नित तानमसा विवेश ||
3.31.e: The sages freed them from their firmbuilt prison: the seven priests drove them forward with their spirit.  All holy Order's pathway they discovered he, full of knowledge, shared these deeds through worship.

3.31.d: विदद यदी सरमा रुग्णमद्रेर्महि पाथः पूर्व्यं सध्र्यक कः | अग्रं नयत सुपद्यक्षराणामछा रवं परथमा जानती गात ||
3.31.e: When Saramā had found the mountain's fissure, that vast and ancient place she plundered thoroughly.  In the floods' van she led them forth, light-footed: she who well knew came first unto their lowing.

3.31.d: अगछदु विप्रतमः सखीयन्नसूदयत सुक्र्ते गर्भमद्रिः | ससान मर्यो युवभिर्मखस्यन्नथाभवदङगिराः सद्यो अर्चन ||
3.31.e: Longing for friendship came the noblest singer: the hill poured forth its treasure for the pious.  The Hero with young followers fought and conquered, and straightway Aṅgiras was singing praises,

3.31.d: सतः-सतः परतिमानं पुरोभूर्विश्वा वेद जनिमा हन्ति शुष्णम | पर णो दिवः पदवीर्गव्युरर्चन सखा सखीन्रमुञ्चन निरवद्यात ||
3.31.e: Peer of each noble thing, yea, all excelling, all creatures doth he know, he slayeth Śuṣṇa.  Our leader, fain for war, singing from heaven, as Friend he saved his lovers from dishonour.

3.31.d: नि गव्यता मनसा सेदुरर्कैः कर्ण्वानासो अम्र्तत्वाय गातुम | इदं चिन नु सदनं भूर्येषां येन मासानसिषासन्न्र्तेन ||
3.31.e: They sate them down with spirit fain for booty, making with hymns a way to life eternal.  And this is still their place of frequent session, whereby they sought to gain the months through Order.

3.31.d: सम्पश्यमाना अमदन्नभि सवं पयः परत्नस्य रेतसो दुघानाः | वि रोदसी अतपद घोष एषां जाते निष्ठामदधुर्गोषु वीरान ||
3.31.e: Drawing the milk of ancient seed prolific, they joyed as they beheld their own possession.  Their shout of triumph heated earth and heaven. When the kine showed, they bade the heroes rouse them.

3.31.d: स जातेभिर्व्र्त्रहा सेदु हव्यैरुदुस्रिया अस्र्जदिन्द्रो अर्कैः | उरूच्यस्मै घर्तवद भरन्ती मधु सवाद्म दुदुहे जेन्या गौः ||
3.31.e: Indra drove forth the kine, that Vṛtra-slayer, while hymns of praise rose up and gifts were offered.  For him the Cow, noble and far-extending, poured pleasant juices, bringing oil and sweetness.

3.31.d: पित्रे चिच्चक्रुः सदनं समस्मै महि तविषीमत सुक्र्तो विहि खयन | विष्कभ्नन्त सकम्भनेना जनित्री आसीना ऊर्ध्वं रभसं वि मिन्वन ||
3.31.e: They made a mansion for their Father, deftly provided him a great and glorious dwelling;  With firm support parted and stayed the Parents, and, sitting, fixed him there erected, mighty.

3.31.d: मही यदि धिषणा शिश्नथे धात सद्योव्र्धं विभ्वं रोदस्योः | गिरो यस्मिन्ननवद्याः समीचीर्विश्वा इन्द्राय तविषीरनुत्ताः ||
3.31.e: What time the ample chalice had impelled him, swift waxing, vast, to pierce the earth and heaven,—  Him in whom blameless songs are all united: all powers invincible belong to Indra.

3.31.d: मह्या ते सख्यं वश्मि शक्तीरा वर्त्रघ्ने नियुतो यन्ति पूर्वीः | महि सतोत्रमव आगन्म सूरेरस्माकं सु मघवन बोधि गोपाः ||
3.31.e: I crave thy powers, I crave thy mighty friendship: full many a team goes to the Vṛtra-slayer.  Great is the laud, we seek the Princes' favour. Be thou, O Maghavan, our guard and keeper.

3.31.d: महि कषेत्रं पुरु शचन्द्रं विविद्वानादित सखिभ्यश्चरथं समैरत | इन्द्रो नर्भिरजनद दीद्यानः साकं सूर्यमुषसं गातुमग्निम ||
3.31.e: He, having found great, splendid, rich dominion, sent life and motion to his friends and lovers.  Indra who shone together with the Heroes begot the song, the fire, and Sun and Morning.

3.31.d: अपश्चिदेष विभ्वो दमूनाः पर सध्रीचीरस्र्जद विश्वश्चन्द्राः | मध्वः पुनानाः कविभिः पवित्रैर्द्युभिर्हिन्वन्त्यक्तुभिर्धनुत्रीः ||
3.31.e: Vast, the House-Friend, he set the waters flowing, all-lucid, widely spread, that move together.  By the wise cleansings of the meath made holy, through days, and nights they speed the swift streams onward.

3.31.d: अनु कर्ष्णे वसुधिती जिहाते उभे सूर्यस्य मंहना यजत्रे | परि यत ते महिमानं वर्जध्यै सखाय इन्द्र काम्या रजिप्याः ||
3.31.e: To thee proceed the dark, the treasure-holders, both of them sanctified by Sūrya's bounty.  The while thy ovely storming Friends, O Indra, fail to attain the measure of thy greatness.

3.31.d: पतिर्भव वर्त्रहन सून्र्तानां गिरां विश्वायुर्व्र्षभो वयोधाः | आ नो गहि सख्येभिः शिवेभिर्महान महीभिरूतिभिः सरण्यन ||
3.31.e: Be Lord of joyous songs, O Vṛtra-slayer, Bull dear to all, who gives the power of living.  Come unto us with thine auspicious friendship, hastening, Mighty One, with mighty succours.

3.31.d: तमङगिरस्वन नमसा सपर्यन नव्यं कर्णोमि सन्यसे पुराजाम | दरुहो वि याहि बहुला अदेवीः सवश्च नो मघवन सातये धाः ||
3.31.e: Like Aṅgiras I honour him with worship, and renovate old song for him the Ancient.  Chase thou the many godless evil creatures, and give us, Maghavan, heaven's light to help m.

3.31.d: मिहः पावकाः परतता अभूवन सवस्ति नः पिप्र्हि पारमासाम | इन्द्र तवं रथिरः पाहि नो रिषो मक्षू-मक्षू कर्णुहि गोजितो नः ||
3.31.e: Far forth are spread the purifying waters convey thou us across them unto safety.  Save us, our Charioteer, from harm, O Indra, soon, very soon, make us win spoil of cattle.

3.31.d: अदेदिष्ट वर्त्रहा गोपतिर्गा अन्तः कर्ष्णानरुषैर्धामभिर्गात | पर सून्र्ता दिशमान रतेन दुरश्च विश्वा अव्र्णोदप सवाः ||
3.31.e: His kine their Lord hath shown, e’en Vṛtra's slayer, through the black hosts he passed with red attendants.  Teaching us pleasant things by holy Order, to, us hath he thrown open all his portals.
Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best Hero in this fight where spoil is gathered.  The Strong who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.

3.32.d: इन्द्र सोमं सोमपते पिबेमं माध्यन्दिनं सवनं चारु यत ते | परप्रुथ्या शिप्रे मघवन्न्र्जीषिन विमुच्या हरी इहमादयस्व ||
3.32.e: DRINK thou this Soma, Indra, Lord of Soma; drink thou the draught of noonday which thou Iovest.  Puffing thy cheeks, impetuous, liberal Giver, here loose thy two Bay Horses and rejoice thee.

3.32.d: गवाशिरं मन्थिनमिन्द्र शुक्रं पिबा सोमं ररिमा ते मदाय | बरह्मक्र्ता मारुतेना गणेन सजोषा रुद्रैस्त्र्पदाव्र्षस्व ||
3.32.e: Quaff it pure, meal-blent, mixt with milk, O Indra; we have poured forth the Soma for thy rapture.  Knit with the prayer-fulfilling band of Maruts, yea, with the Rudras, drink till thou art sated;

3.32.d: ये ते शुष्मं ये तविषीमवर्धन्नर्चन्त इन्द्र मरुतस्तोजः | माध्यन्दिने सवने वज्रहस्त पिबा रुद्रेभिः सगणः सुशिप्र ||
3.32.e: Those who gave increase to thy strength and vigour; the Maruts singing forth thy might, O Indra.  Drink thou, O fair of cheek, whose hand wields thunder, with Rudras banded, at our noon libation.

3.32.d: त इन नवस्य मधुमद विविप्र इन्द्रस्य शर्धो मरुतो य आसन | येभिर्व्र्त्रस्येषितो विवेदामर्मणो मन्यमानस्य मर्म ||
3.32.e: They, even the Maruts who were there, excited with song the meath-created strength of Indra.  By them impelled to act he reached the vitals Of Vṛtra, though he deemed that none might wound him.

3.32.d: मनुष्वदिन्द्र सवनं जुषाणः पिबा सोमं शश्वते वीर्याय | स आ वव्र्त्स्व हर्यश्व यज्ञैः सरण्युभिरपो अर्णा सिसर्षि ||
3.32.e: Pleased, like a man, with our libation, Indra, drink, for enduring hero might, the Soma.  Lord of Bays, moved by sacrifice come hither: thou with the Swift Ones stirrest floods and waters.

3.32.d: तवमपो यद ध वर्त्रं जघन्वानत्यानिव परास्र्जः सर्तवाजौ | शयानमिन्द्र चरत वधेन वव्रिवांसं परि देवीरदेवम ||
3.32.e: When thou didst loose the streams to run like racers in the swift contest, having smitten Vṛtra  With flying weapon where he lay, O Indra, and, godless, kept the Goddesses encompassed.

3.32.d: यजाम इन नमसा वर्द्धमिन्द्रं बर्हन्तं रष्वमजरं युवानम | यस्य परिये ममतुर्यज्ञियस्य न रोदसी महिमानं ममाते ||
3.32.e: With reverence let us worship mighty Indra, great and sublime, eternal, everyouthful,  Whose greatness the dear world-halves have not measured, no, nor conceived the might of him the Holy.

3.32.d: इन्द्रस्य कर्म सुक्र्ता पुरूणि वरतानि देवा न मिनन्ति विश्वे | दाधार यः पर्थिवीं दयामुतेमां जजान सूर्यमुषसं सुदंसाः ||
3.32.e: Many are Indra's nobly wrought achievements, and none of all the Gods transgress his statutes.  He beareth up this earth and heaven, and, doer of marvels, he begot the Sun and Morning.

3.32.d: अद्रोघ सत्यं तव तन महित्वं सद्यो यज्जातो अपिबो ह सोमम | न दयाव इन्द्र तवसस्त ओजो नाहा न मासाः शरदो वरन्त ||
3.32.e: Herein, O Guileless One, is thy true greatness, that soon as born thou drankest up the Soma.  Days may not check the power of thee the Mighty, nor the nights, Indra, nor the months, nor autumns.

3.32.d: तवं सद्यो अपिबो जात इन्द्र मदाय सोमं परमे वयोमन | यद ध दयावाप्र्थिवी आविवेषीरथाभवः पूर्व्यः कारुधायाः ||
3.32.e: As soon as thou wast born in highest heaven thou drankest Soma to delight thee, Indra;  And when thou hadst pervaded earth and heaven thou wast the first supporter of the singer.

3.32.d: अहन्नहिं परिशयानमर्ण ओजायमानं तुविजात तव्यान | न ते महित्वमनु भूदध दयौर्यदन्यया सफिग्या कषामवस्थाः ||
3.32.e: Thou, puissant God, more mighty, slewest. Ahi showing his strength when couched around the waters.  The heaven itself attained not to thy greatness when with one hip of thine the earth was shadowed.

3.32.d: यज्ञो हि त इन्द्र वर्धनो भूदुत परियः सुतसोमो मियेधः | यज्ञेन यज्ञमव यज्ञियः सन यज्ञस्ते वज्रमहिहत्य आवत ||
3.32.e: Sacrifice, Indra, made thee wax so mighty, the dear oblation with the flowing Soma.  O Worshipful, with worship help our worship, for worship helped thy bolt when slaying Ahi.

3.32.d: यज्ञेनेन्द्रमवसा चक्रे अर्वागैनं सुम्नाय नव्यसे वव्र्त्याम | य सतोमेभिर्वाव्र्धे पूर्व्येभिर्यो मध्यमेभिरुत नूतनेभिः ||
3.32.e: With sacrifice and wish have I brought Indra; still for new blessings may I turn him hither,  Him magnified by ancient songs and praises, by lauds of later time and days yet recent.

3.32.d: विवेष यन मा धिषणा जजान सतवै पुरा पार्यादिन्द्रमह्नः | अंहसो यत्र पीपरद यथा नो नावेव यान्तमुभये हवन्ते ||
3.32.e: I have brought forth a song when longing seized me: ere the decisive day will I laud Indra;  Then may he safely bear us over trouble, as in a ship, when both sides invocate him.

3.32.d: आपूर्णो अस्य कलशः सवाहा सेक्तेव कोशं सिसिचे पिबध्यै | समु परिया आवव्र्त्रन मदाय परदक्षिणिदभि सोमासैन्द्रम ||
3.32.e: Full is his chalice: Glory! Like a pourer I have filled up the vessel for his drinking.  Presented on the right, dear Soma juices have brought us Indra, to rejoice him, hither.

3.32.d: न तवा गभीरः पुरुहूत सिन्धुर्नाद्रयः परि षन्तो वरन्त | इत्था सखिभ्य इषितो यदिन्द्रा दर्ळ्हं चिदरुजो गव्यमूर्वम ||
3.32.e: Not the deep-flowing flood, O Much-invoked One! not hills that compass thee about restrain thee,  Since here incited, for thy friends, O Indra, thou breakest e’en the firm built stall of cattle.
Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best Hero in this fight where spoil is gathered,  The Strong who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.

3.33.d: पर पर्वतानामुशती उपस्थादश्वे इव विषिते हासमाने | गावेव शुभ्रे मातरा रिहाणे विपाट छुतुद्री पयसाजवेते ||
3.33.e: FORTH from the bosom of the mountains, eager as two swift mares with loosened rein contending,  Like two bright mother cows who lick their youngling, Vipāś and Sutudri speed down their waters.

3.33.d: इन्द्रेषिते परसवं भिक्षमाणे अछा समुद्रं रथ्येव याथः | समाराणे ऊर्मिभिः पिन्वमाने अन्या वामन्यामप्येति शुभ्रे ||
3.33.e: Impelled by Indra whom ye pray to urge you, ye move as ’twere on chariots to the ocean.  Flowing together, swelling with your billows, O lucid Streams, each of you seeks the other.

3.33.d: अछा सिन्धुं मात्र्तमामयासं विपाशमुर्वीं सुभगामगन्म | वत्समिव मातरा संरिहाणे समानं योनिमनु संचरन्ती ||
3.33.e: I have attained the most maternal River, we have approached Vipāś, the broad, the blessed.  Licking as ’twere their calf the pair of Mothers flow onward to their common home together.

3.33.d: एन वयं पयसा पिन्वमाना अनु योनिं देवक्र्तं चरन्तीः | न वर्तवे परसवः सर्गतक्तः किंयुर्विप्रो नद्यो जोहवीति ||
3.33.e: We two who rise and swell with billowy waters move forward to the home which Gods have made us.  Our flood may not be stayed when urged to motion. What would the singer, calling to the Rivers?

3.33.d: रमध्वं मे वचसे सोम्याय रतावरीरुप मुहूर्तमेवैः | पर सिन्धुमछा बर्हती मनीषावस्युरह्वे कुशिकस्य सूनुः ||
3.33.e: Linger a little at my friendly bidding rest, Holy Ones, a moment in your journey.  With hymn sublime soliciting your favour Kuśika's son hath called unto the River.

3.33.d: इन्द्रो अस्मानरदद वज्रबाहुरपाहन वर्त्रं परिधिं नदीनाम | देवो.अनयत सवित सुपाणिस्तस्य वयं परसवे याम उर्वीः ||
3.33.e: Indra who wields the thunder dug our channels: he smote down Vṛtra, him who stayed our currents.  Savitar, God, the lovely-handed, led us, and at his sending forth we flow expanded.

3.33.d: परवाच्यं शश्वधा वीर्यं तदिन्द्रस्य कर्म यदहिंविव्र्श्चत | वि वज्रेण परिषदो जघानायन्नापो.अयनमिछमानाः ||
3.33.e: That hero deed of Indra must be lauded for ever that he rent Ahi in pieces.  He smote away the obstructors with his thunder, and eager for their course forth flowed the waters.

3.33.d: एतद वचो जरितर्मापि मर्ष्ठा आ यत ते घोषानुत्तरा युगानि | उक्थेषु कारो परति नो जुषस्व मा नो नि कः पुरुषत्रा नमस्ते ||
3.33.e: Never forget this word of thine, O singer, which future generations shall reecho.  In hymns, O bard, show us thy loving kindness. Humble us not mid men. To thee be honour!

3.33.d: ओ षु सवसारः कारवे शर्णोत ययौ वो दूरादनसा रथेन | नि षू नमध्वं भवता सुपारा अधोक्षाः सिन्धवःस्रोत्याभिः ||
3.33.e: List quickly, Sisters, to the bard who cometh to you from far away with car and wagon.  Bow lowly down; be easy to be traversed stay, Rivers, with your floods below our axles.

3.33.d: आ ते कारो शर्णवामा वचांसि ययाथ दूरादनसा रथेन | नि ते नंसै पीप्यानेव योषा मर्यायेव कन्या शश्वचै ते ||
3.33.e: Yea, we will listen to thy words, O singer. With wain and car from far away thou comest.  Low, like a nursing mother, will I bend me, and yield me as a maiden to her lover.

3.33.d: यदङग तवा भरताः सन्तरेयुर्गव्यन गराम इषित इन्द्रजूतः | अर्षादह परसवः सर्गतक्त आ वो वर्णे सुमतिं यज्ञियानाम ||
3.33.e: Soon as the Bharatas have fared across thee, the warrior band, urged on and sped by Indra,  Then let your streams flow on in rapid motion. I crave your favour who deserve our worship.

3.33.d: अतारिषुर्भरता गव्यवः समभक्त विप्रः सुमतिं नदीनाम | पर पिन्वध्वमिषयन्तीः सुराधा आ वक्षणाः पर्णध्वं यात शीभम ||
3.33.e: The warrior host, the Bharatas, fared over the singer won the favour of the Rivers.  Swell with your billows, hasting, pouring riches. Fill full your channels, and roll swiftly onward.

3.33.d: उद व ऊर्मिः शम्या हन्त्वापो योक्त्राणि मुञ्चत | मादुष्क्र्तौ वयेनसाघ्न्यौ शूनमारताम ||
3.33.e: So let your wave bear up the pins, and ye, O Waters, spare the thongs;  And never may the pair of Bulls, harmless and sinless, waste away.

3.34.d: इन्द्रः पूर्भिदातिरद दासमर्कैर्विदद्वसुर्दयमानो विशत्रून | बरह्मजूतस्तन्वा वाव्र्धानो भूरिदात्र आप्र्णद रोदसी उभे ||
3.34.e: FORT-RENDER, Lord of Wealth, dispelling foemen, Indra with lightnings hath o’ercome the Dāsa.  Impelled by prayer and waxen great in body, he hath filled earth and heaven, the Bounteous Giver.

3.34.d: मखस्य ते तविषस्य पर जूतिमियर्मि वाचमम्र्ताय भूषन | इन्द्र कषितीनामसि मानुषीणां विशां दैवीनामुत पूर्वयावा ||
3.34.e: I stimulate thy zeal, the Strong, the Hero decking my song of praise forth; Immortal.  O Indra, thou art equally the Leader of heavenly hosts and human generations.

3.34.d: इन्द्रो वर्त्रमव्र्णोच्छर्धनीतिः पर मायिनाममिनाद वर्पणीतिः | अहन वयंसमुशधग वनेष्वाविर्धेना अक्र्णोद राम्याणाम ||
3.34.e: Leading, his band Indra encompassed Vṛtra; weak grew the wily leader of enchanters.  He who burns fierce in forests slaughtered Vyaṁsa, and made the Milch-kine of the nights apparent.

3.34.d: इन्द्रः सवर्षा जनयन्नहानि जिगायोशिग्भिः पर्तना अभिष्टिः | परारोचयन मनवे केतुमह्नामविन्दज्ज्योतिर्ब्र्हतेरणाय ||
3.34.e: Indra, light-winner, days' Creator, conquered, victorious, hostile bands with those who loved him.  For man the days' bright ensign he illumined, and found the light for his joy and gladness.

3.34.d: इन्द्रस्तुजो बर्हणा आ विवेश नर्वद दधानो नर्या पुरूणि | अचेतयद धिय इमा जरित्रे परेमं वर्णमतिरच्छुक्रमासाम ||
3.34.e: Forward to fiercely falling blows pressed Indra, herolike doing many hero exploits.  These holy songs he taught the bard who gaised him, and widely spread these Dawns' resplendent colour.

3.34.d: महो महानि पनयन्त्यस्येन्द्रस्य कर्म सुक्र्ता पुरूणि | वर्जनेन वर्जिनान सं पिपेष मायाभिर्दस्यून्रभिभूत्योजाः ||
3.34.e: They laud the mighty acts of him the Mighty, the many glorious deeds performed by Indra.  He in his strength, with all-surpassing prowess, through wondrous arts crushed the malignant Dasyus.

3.34.d: युधेन्द्रो मह्ना वरिवश्चकार देवेभ्यः सत्पतिश्चर्षणिप्राः | विवस्वतः सदने अस्य तानि विप्रा उक्थेभिः कवयोग्र्णन्ति ||
3.34.e: Lord of the brave, Indra who rules the people gave freedom to the Gods by might and battle.  Wise singers glorify with chanted praises these his achievements in Vivasvān's dwelling.

3.34.d: सत्रासाहं वरेण्यं सहोदां ससवांसं सवरपश्च देवीः | ससान यः पर्थिवीं दयामुतेमामिन्द्रं मदन्त्यनु धीरणासः ||
3.34.e: Excellent, Conqueror, the victory-giver, the winner of the light and Godlike Waters,  He who hath won this broad earth and this heaven, -in Indra they rejoice who love devotions.

3.34.d: ससानात्यानुत सूर्यं ससानेन्द्रः ससान पुरुभोजसं गाम | हिरण्ययमुत भोगं ससान हत्वी दस्यून परार्यंवर्णमावत ||
3.34.e: He gained possession of the Sun and Horses, Indra obtained the Cow who feedeth many.  Treasure of gold he won; he smote the Dasyus, and gave protection to the Āryan colour.

3.34.d: इन्द्र ओषधीरसनोदहानि वनस्पतीन्रसनोदन्तरिक्षम | बिभेद वलं नुनुदे विवाचो.अथाभवद दमितद्भिक्रतूनाम ||
3.34.e: He took the plants and days for his possession; he gained the forest trees and air's mid-region.  Vala he cleft, and chased away opponents: thus was he tamer of the overweening.
Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best Hero in the fight where spoil is gathered,  The Strong, who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers treasures.

3.35.d: तिष्ठा हरी रथ आ युज्यमाना याहि वायुर्न नियुतो नो अछ | पिबास्यन्धो अभिस्र्ष्टो अस्मे इन्द्र सवाहा ररिमाते मदाय ||
3.35.e: MOUNT the Bay Horses to thy chariot harnessed, and come to us like Vāyu with his coursers.  Thou, hastening to us, shalt drink the Soma. Hail, Indra. We have poured it for thy rapture.

3.35.d: उपाजिरा पुरुहूताय सप्ती हरी रथस्य धूर्ष्वा युनज्मि | दरवद यथा सम्भ्र्तं विश्वतश्चिदुपेमं यज्ञमावहात इन्द्रम ||
3.35.e: For him, the God who is invoked by many, the two swift Bay Steeds to the pole I harness,  That they in fleet course may bring Indra hither, e’en to this sacrifice arranged completely.

3.35.d: उपो नयस्व वर्षणा तपुष्पोतेमव तवं वर्षभ सवधावः | गरसेतामश्वा वि मुचेह शोणा दिवे-दिवे सद्र्शीरद्धिधानाः ||
3.35.e: Bring the strong Steeds who drink the warm libation, and, Bull of Godlike nature, be thou gracious.  Let thy Steeds eat; set free thy Tawny Horses, and roasted grain like this consume thou daily.

3.35.d: बरह्मणा ते बरह्मयुजा युनज्मि हरी सखाया सधमाद आशू | सथिरं रथं सुखमिन्द्राधितिष्ठन परजानन विद्वानुप याहि सोमम ||
3.35.e: Those who are yoked by prayer I harness, fleet friendly Bays who take their joy together.  Mounting thy firm and easy car, O Indra, wise and all-knowing come thou to the Soma.

3.35.d: मा ते हरी वर्षणा वीतप्र्ष्ठा नि रीरमन यजमानासो अन्ये | अत्यायाहि शश्वतो वयं ते.अरं सुतेभिः कर्णवामसोमैः ||
3.35.e: No other worshippers must stay beside them thy Bays, thy vigorous and smooth-backed Coursers.  Pass by them all and hasten onward hither: with Soma pressed we will prepare to feast thee.

3.35.d: तवायं सोमस्त्वमेह्यर्वां छश्वत्तमं सुमना अस्यपाहि | अस्मिन यज्ञे बर्हिष्या निषद्या दधिष्वेमं जठर इन्दुमिन्द्र ||
3.35.e: Thine is this Soma: hasten to approach it. Drink thou thereof, benevolent, and cease not.  Sit on the sacred grass at this our worship, and take these drops into thy belly, Indra.

3.35.d: सतीर्णं ते बर्हिः सुत इन्द्र सोमः कर्ता धाना अत्तवे तेहरिभ्याम | तदोकसे पुरुशाकाय वर्ष्णे मरुत्वते तुभ्यंराता हवींषि ||
3.35.e: The grass is strewn for thee, pressed is the Soma; the grain is ready for thy Bays to feed on.  To thee who lovest them, the very mighty, strong, girt by Maruts, are these gifts presented.

3.35.d: इमं नरः पर्वतास्तुभ्यमापः समिन्द्र गोभिर्मधुमन्तमक्रन | तस्यागत्या सुमना रष्व पाहि परजानन विद्वान पथ्या अनु सवाः ||
3.35.e: This the sweet draught, with cows, the men, the mountains, the waters, Indra, have for thee made ready.  Come, drink thereof, Sublime One, friendly-minded, foreseeing, knowing well the ways thou goest.

3.35.d: यानाभजो मरुत इन्द्र सोमे ये तवामवर्धन्नभवन गणस्ते | तेभिरेतं सजोषा वावशानो.अग्नेः पिब जिह्वयासोममिन्द्र ||
3.35.e: The Maruts, they with whom thou sharedst Soma, Indra, who made thee strong and were thine army,—  With these accordant, eagerly desirous drink thou this Soma with the tongue of Agni.

3.35.d: इन्द्र पिब सवधया चित सुतस्याग्नेर्वा पाहि जिह्वया यजत्र | अध्वर्योर्वा परयतं शक्र हस्ताद धोतुर्वा यज्ञं हविषो जुषस्व ||
3.35.e: Drink, Indra, of the juice by thine own nature, or by the tongue of Agni, O thou Holy.  Accept the sacrificial gift, O Śakra, from the Adhvaryu's hand or from the Hotar's.
Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best Hero in the fight where spoil is gathered,  The Strong, who listens, who.gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.

3.36.d: इमामू षु परभ्र्तिं सातये धाः शश्वचः छश्वदूतिभिर्यादमानः | सुते-सुते वाव्र्धे वर्धनेभिर्यः कर्मभिर्महद्भिः सुश्रुतो भूत ||
3.36.e: WITH constant succours, fain thyself to share it, make this oblation which we bring effective.  Grown great through strengthening gifts at each libation, he hath become renowned by mighty exploits.

3.36.d: इन्द्राय सोमाः परदिवो विदाना रभुर्येभिर्व्र्षपर्वा विहायाः | परयम्यमानान परति षू गर्भायेन्द्र पिब वर्षधूतस्य वर्ष्णः ||
3.36.e: For Indra were the Somas erst- discovered, whereby he grew strong-jointed, vast, and skilful.  Indra , take quickly these presented juices: drink of the strong, that which the strong have shaken.

3.36.d: पिबा वर्धस्व तव घा सुतास इन्द्र सोमासः परथमा उतेमे | यथापिबः पूर्व्यानिन्द्र सोमानेवा पाहि पन्यो अद्या नवीयान ||
3.36.e: Drink and wax great. Thine are the juices, Indra, both Somas of old time and these we bring thee.  Even as thou drankest, Indra, earlier Somas, so drink to-day, a new guest, meet for praises.

3.36.d: महानमत्रो वर्जने विरप्श्युग्रं शवः पत्यते धर्ष्ण्वोजः | नाह विव्याच पर्थिवी चनैनं यत सोमासो हर्यश्वममन्दन ||
3.36.e: Great and impetuous, mighty-voiced in battle, surpassing power is his, and strength resistless.  Him the broad earth hath never comprehended when Somas cheered the Lord of Tawny Coursers.

3.36.d: महानुग्रो वाव्र्धे वीर्याय समाचक्रे वर्षभः काव्येन | इन्द्रो भगो वाजदा अस्य गावः पर जायन्ते दक्षिणा अस्य पूर्वीः ||
3.36.e: Mighty and strong he waxed for hero exploit: the Bull was furnished a Sage's wisdom.  Indra is our kind Lord; his steers have vigour; his cows are many with abundant offspring.

3.36.d: पर यत सिन्धवः परसवं यथायन्नापः समुद्रं रथ्येव जग्मुः | अतश्चिदिन्द्रः सदसो वरीयान यदीं सोमः पर्णति दुग्धो अंशुः ||
3.36.e: As floods according to their stream flow onward, so to the sea, as borne on cars, the waters.  Vaster is Indra even than his dwelling, what time the stalk milked out, the Soma, fills him.

3.36.d: समुद्रेण सिन्धवो यादमाना इन्द्राय सोमं सुषुतं भरन्तः | अंशुं दुहन्ति हस्तिनो भरित्रैर्मध्वः पुनन्ति धारया पवित्रैः ||
3.36.e: Eager to mingle with the sea, the rivers carry the well-pressed Soma juice to Indra.  They drain the stalk out with their arms, quick-banded, and cleanse it with a stream of mead and filters.

3.36.d: हरदा इव कुक्षयः सोमधानाः समी विव्याच सवना पुरूणि | अन्ना यदिन्द्रः परथमा वयाश वर्त्रं जघन्वानव्र्णीत सोमम ||
3.36.e: Like lakes appear his flanks filled full with Soma: yea, he contains libations in abundance.  When Indra had consumed the first sweet viands, he, after slaying Vṛtra, claimed the Soma.

3.36.d: आ तू भर माकिरेतत परि षठाद विद्मा हि तवा वसुपतिं वसूनाम | इन्द्र यत ते माहिनं दत्रमस्त्यस्मभ्यं तद धर्यश्व पर यन्धि ||
3.36.e: Then bring thou hither, and let none prevent it: we know thee well, the Lord of wealth and treasure.  That splendid gift which is thine own, O Indra, vouchsafe to us, Lord of the Tawny Coursers.

3.36.d: अस्मे पर यन्धि मघवन्न्र्जीषिन्निन्द्र रायो विश्ववारस्य भूरेः | अस्मे शतं शरदो जीवसे धा अस्मे वीरान छश्वत इन्द्र शिप्रिन ||
3.36.e: O Indra, Maghavan, impetuous mover, grant us abundant wealth that brings all blessings.  Give us a hundred autumns for our lifetime: give us, O fair-checked Indra, store of heroes.
Call we on Indra, Maghavan, auspicious, best Hero in the fight where spoil is gathered,  The Strong, who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.

3.37.d: वार्त्रहत्याय शवसे पर्तनाषाह्याय च | इन्द्र तवा वर्तयामसि ||
3.37.e: O INDRA, for the strength that slays Vṛtra and conquers in the fight,  We turn thee hitherward to us.

3.37.d: अर्वाचीनं सु ते मन उत चक्षुः शतक्रतो | इन्द्र कर्ण्वन्तु वाघतः ||
3.37.e: O Indra, Lord of Hundred Powers, may those who praise thee hitherward.  Direct thy spirit and thine eye.
O Indra, Lord of Hundred Powers, with all our songs we invocate  Thy names for triumph over foes.

3.37.d: पुरुष्टुतस्य धामभिः शतेन महयामसि | इन्द्रस्य चर्षणीध्र्तः ||
3.37.e: We strive for glory through the powers immense of him whom many praise,  Of Indra who supports mankind.

3.37.d: इन्द्रं वर्त्राय हन्तवे पुरुहूतमुप बरुवे | भरेषु वाजसातये ||
3.37.e: For Vṛtra's slaughter I address Indra whom many invocate,  To win us booty in the wars.

3.37.d: वाजेषु सासहिर्भव तवामीमहे शतक्रतो | इन्द्र वर्त्रायहन्तवे ||
3.37.e: In battles be victorious. We seek thee, Lord of Hundred Powers,  Indra, that Vṛtra may be slain.

3.37.d: दयुम्नेषु पर्तनाज्ये पर्त्सुतूर्षु शरवस्सु च | इन्द्र साक्ष्वाभिमातिषु ||
3.37.e: In splendid combats of the hosts, in glories where the fight is won.  Indra, be victor over foes.

3.37.d: शुष्मिन्तमं न ऊतये दयुम्निनं पाहि जाग्र्विम | इन्द्र सोमंशतक्रतो ||
3.37.e: Drink thou the Soma for our help, bright, vigilant, exceeding strong,  O Indra, Lord of Hundred Powers.

3.37.d: इन्द्रियाणि शतक्रतो या ते जनेषु पञ्चसु | इन्द्र तानि ता वर्णे ||
3.37.e: O Śatakratu, powers which thou mid the Five Races hast displayed-  These, Indra, do I claim of thee.

3.37.d: अगन्निन्द्र शरवो बर्हद दयुम्नं दधिष्व दुष्टरम | उत ते शुष्मं तिरामसि ||
3.37.e: Indra, great glory hast thou gained. Win splendid fame which none may mar  We make thy might perpetual.

3.37.d: अर्वावतो न आ गह्यथो शक्र परावतः | उ लोको यस्ते अद्रिव इन्द्रेह तत आ गहि ||
3.37.e: Come to us either from anear, Or, Śakra, come from far away.  Indra, wherever be thy home, come to us thence, O Thunder-armed.

3.38.d: अभि तष्टेव दीधया मनीषामत्यो न वाजी सुधुरो जिहानः | अभि परियाणि मर्म्र्शत पराणि कवीन्रिछामि सन्द्र्शे सुमेधाः ||
3.38.e: HASTING like some strong courser good at drawing, a thought have I imagined like a workman.  Pondering what is dearest and most noble, I long to see the sages full of wisdom.

3.38.d: इनोत पर्छ जनिमा कवीनां मनोध्र्तः सुक्र्तस्तक्षत दयाम | इमा उ ते परण्यो वर्धमाना मनोवाता अध नु धर्मणिग्मन ||
3.38.e: Ask of the sages' mighty generations firm-minded and devout they framed the heaven.  These are thy heart-sought strengthening directions, and they have come to be sky's upholders.

3.38.d: नि षीमिदत्र गुह्या दधाना उत कषत्राय रोदसी समञ्जन | सं मात्राभिर्ममिरे येमुर उर्वी अन्तर मही सम्र्ते धायसे धुः ||
3.38.e: Assuming in this world mysterious natures, they decked the heaven and earth for high dominion,  Measured with measures, fixed their broad expanses, set the great worlds apart held firm for safety.

3.38.d: आतिष्ठन्तं परि विश्वे अभूषञ्छ्रियो वसानश्चरति सवरोचिः | महत तद वर्ष्णो असुरस्य नामा विश्वरूपो अम्र्तानि तस्थौ ||
3.38.e: Even as he mounted up they all adorned him: self-luminous he travels clothed in splendour.  That is the Bull's, the Asura's mighty figure: he, omniform, hath reached the eternal waters.

3.38.d: असूत पूर्वो वर्षभो जयायानिमा अस्य शुरुधः सन्ति पूर्वीः | दिवो नपाता विदथस्य धीभिः कषत्रं राजाना परदिवो दधाथे ||
3.38.e: First the more ancient Bull engendered offspring; these are his many draughts that lent him vigour.  From days of old ye Kings, two Sons of Heaven, by hymns of sacrifice have won dominion.

3.38.d: तरीणि राजाना विदथे पुरूणि परि विश्वानि भूषथः सदांसि | अपश्यमत्र मनसा जगन्वान वरते गन्धर्वानपि वायुकेशान ||
3.38.e: Three seats ye Sovrans, in the Holy synod, many, yea, all, ye honour with your presence.  There saw I, going thither in the spirit, Gandharvas in their course with wind-blown tresses.

3.38.d: तदिन नवस्य वर्षभस्य धेनोरा नामभिर्ममिरे सक्म्यंगोः | अन्यद-अन्यदसुर्यं वसाना नि मायिनो ममिरे रूपमस्मिन ||
3.38.e: That same companionship of her, the Milch-cow, here with the strong Bull's divers forms they stablished.  Enduing still some new celestial figure, the skilful workers shaped a form around him.

3.38.d: तदिन नवस्य सवितुर्नकिर्मे हिरण्ययीममतिं यामशिश्रेत | आ सुष्टुती रोदसी विश्वमिन्वे अपीव योषा जनिमानि वव्रे ||
3.38.e: Let no one here debar me from enjoying the golden light which Savitar diffuses.  He covers both all-fostering worlds with praises even as a woman cherishes her children.

3.38.d: युवं परत्नस्य साधथो महो यद दैवी सवस्तिः परि णः सयातम | गोपाजिह्वस्य तस्थुषो विरूपा विश्वे पश्यन्ति मायिनः कर्तानि ||
3.38.e: Fulfil, ye twain, his work, the Great, the Ancient: as heavenly blessing keep your guard around us.  All the wise Gods behold his varied actions who stands erect, whose voice is like a herdsman's.
Call we on Indra, Maghavan, auspicious, best Hero in the fight where spoil is gathered,  The Strong, who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.

3.39.d: इन्द्रं मतिर्ह्र्द आ वच्यमानाछा पतिं सतोमतष्टा जिगाति | या जाग्र्विर्विदथे शस्यमानेन्द्र यत ते जायते विद्धि तस्य ||
3.39.e: To Indra from the heart the hymn proceedeth, to him the Lord, recited, built with praises;  The wakening song sung forth in holy synod: that which is born for thee, O Indra, notice.

3.39.d: दिवश्चिदा पूर्व्या जायमाना वि जाग्र्विर्विदथे शस्यमाना | भद्रा वस्त्राण्यर्जुना वसाना सेयमस्मे सनजापित्र्या धीः ||
3.39.e: Born from the heaven e’en in the days aforetime, wakening, sting aloud in holy synod,  Auspicious, clad in white and shining raiment, this is the ancient hymn of our forefathers.

3.39.d: यमा चिदत्र यमसूरसूत जिह्वाया अग्रं पतदा हयस्थात | वपूंषि जाता मिथुना सचेते तमोहना तपुषो बुध्न एता ||
3.39.e: The Mother of the Twins hath borne Twin Children: my tongue's tip raised itself and rested silent.  Killing the darkness at the light's foundation, the Couple newly born attain their beauty.

3.39.d: नकिरेषां निन्दिता मर्त्येषु ये अस्माकं पितरो गोषु योधाः | इन्द्र एषां दरंहिता माहिनावानुद गोत्राणि सस्र्जे दंसनावान ||
3.39.e: Not one is found among them, none of mortals, to blame our sires who fought to win the cattle.  Their strengthener was Indra the Majestic he spread their stalls of kine the Wonder-Worker.

3.39.d: सखा ह यत्र सखिभिर्नवग्वैरभिज्ञ्वा सत्वभिर्गा अनुग्मन | सत्यं तदिन्द्रो दसभिर्दशग्भिः सूर्यं विवेदतमसि कषियन्तम ||
3.39.e: Where as a Friend with friendly men, Navagvas, with heroes, on his knees he sought the cattle.  There, verily with ten Daśagvas Indra found the Sun lying hidden in the darkness.

3.39.d: इन्द्रो मधु सम्भ्र्तमुस्रियायां पद्वद विवेद शफवन नमेगोः | गुहा हितं गुह्यं गूळ्हमप्सु हस्ते दधे दक्षिणे दक्षिणावान ||
3.39.e: Indra found meath collected in the milch-cow, by foot and hoof, in the cow's place of pasture.  That which lay secret, hidden in the waters, he held in his right hand, the rich rewarder.

3.39.d: जयोतिर्व्र्णीत तमसो विजानन्नारे सयाम दुरितादभीके | इमा गिरः सोमपाः सोमव्र्द्ध जुषस्वेन्द्र पुरुतमस्य कारोः ||
3.39.e: He took the light, discerning it from darkness: may we be far removed from all misfortune.  These songs, O Soma-drinker, cheered by Soma, Indra, accept from thy most zealous poet.

3.39.d: जयोतिर्यज्ञाय रोदसी अनु षयादारे सयाम दुरितस्य भूरेः | भूरि चिद धि तुजतो मर्त्यस्य सुपारासो वसवो बर्हणावत ||
3.39.e: Let there be light through both the worlds for worship: may we be far from most overwhelming evil.  Great woe comes even from the hostile mortal, piled up; but good at rescue are the Vasus.
Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best Hero in the fight where spoil is gathered,  The Strong, who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.

3.40.d: इन्द्र तवा वर्षभं वयं सुते सोमे हवामहे | स पाहि मध्वो अन्धसः ||
3.40.e: THEE, Indra, we invoke, the Bull, what time the Soma is expressed.  So drink thou of the savoury juice.

3.40.d: इन्द्र करतुविदं सुतं सोमं हर्य पुरुष्टुत | पिबा वर्षस्व तात्र्पिम ||
3.40.e: Indra, whom many laud, accept the strength-conferring Soma juice:  Quaff, pour down drink that satisfies.

3.40.d: इन्द्र पर णो धितावानं यज्ञं विश्वेभिर्देवेभिः | तिर सतवान विश्पते ||
3.40.e: Indra, with all the Gods promote our wealth-bestowing sacrifice,  Thou highly-lauded Lord of men.

3.40.d: इन्द्र सोमाः सुता इमे तव पर यन्ति सत्पते | कषयं चन्द्रास इन्दवः ||
3.40.e: Lord of the brave, to thee proceed these drops of Soma juice expressed,  The bright drops to thy dwelling-place.

3.40.d: दधिष्वा जठरे सुतं सोममिन्द्र वरेण्यम | तव दयुक्षास इन्दवः ||
3.40.e: Within thy belly, Indra, take juice, Soma the most excellent: Thine are the drops celestial.

3.40.d: गिर्वणः पाहि नः सुतं मधोर्धाराभिरज्यसे | इन्द्र तवादातमिद यशः ||
3.40.e: Drink our libation, Lord of hymns: with streams of meath thou art bedewed  Our glory, Indra, is thy gift.

3.40.d: अभि दयुम्नानि वनिन इन्द्रं सचन्ते अक्षिता | पीत्वी सोमस्य वाव्र्धे ||
3.40.e: To Indra go the treasures of the worshipper, which never fail:  He drinks the Soma and is strong

3.40.d: अर्वावतो न आ गहि परावतश्च वर्त्रहन | इमा जुषस्व नो गिरः ||
3.40.e: From far away, from near at hand, O Vṛtra-slayer, come to us:  Accept the songs we sing to thee.

3.40.d: यदन्तरा परावतमर्वावतं च हूयसे | इन्द्रेह तत आ गहि ||
3.40.e: When from the space between the near and far thou art invoked by us,  Thence, Indra. come thou hitherward.

3.41.d: आ तू न इन्द्र मद्र्यग घुवानः सोमपीतये | हरिभ्यां याह्यद्रिवः ||
3.41.e: INVOKED to drink the Soma juice, come with thy Bay Steeds, Thunder-armed  Come, Indra, hitherward to me.

3.41.d: सत्तो होता न रत्वियस्तिस्तिरे बर्हिरानुषक | अयुज्रन परातरद्रयः ||
3.41.e: Our priest is seated, true to time; the grass is regularly strewn;  The pressing-stones were set at morn.

3.41.d: इमा बरह्म बरह्मवाहः करियन्त आ बर्हिः सीद | वीहि शूर पुरोळाशम ||
3.41.e: These prayers, O thou who hearest prayer are offered: seat thee on the grass.  Hero, enjoy the offered cake.

3.41.d: रारन्धि सवनेषु ण एषु सतोमेषु वर्त्रहन | उक्थेष्विन्द्र गिर्वणः ||
3.41.e: O Vṛtra-slayer, be thou pleased with these libations, with these hymns,  Song-loving Indra, with our lauds.

3.41.d: मतयः सोमपामुरुं रिहन्ति शवसस पतिम | इन्द्रं वत्सं न मातरः ||
3.41.e: Our hymns caress the Lord of Strength, vast, drinker of the Soma's juice,  Indra, as mother-cows their calf.

3.41.d: स मन्दस्वा हयन्धसो राधसे तन्वा महे | न सतोतारं निदे करः ||
3.41.e: Delight thee with the juice we pour for thine own great munificence:  Yield not thy singer to reproach.

3.41.d: वयमिन्द्र तवायवो हविष्मन्तो जरामहे | उत तवमस्मयुर्वसो ||
3.41.e: We, Indra, dearly loving thee, bearing oblation, sing thee hymns  Thou, Vasu, dearly lovest us.

3.41.d: मारे अस्मद वि मुमुचो हरिप्रियार्वां याहि | इन्द्र सवधावोमत्स्वेह ||
3.41.e: O thou to whom thy Bays are dear, loose not thy Horses far from us:  Here glad thee, Indra, Lord divine.

3.41.d: अर्वाञ्चं तवा सुखे रथे वहतामिन्द्र केशिना | घर्तस्नूबर्हिरासदे ||
3.41.e: May long-maned Coursers, dropping oil, bring thee on swift car hitherward,  Indra, to seat thee on the grass.

3.42.d: उप नः सुतमा गहि सोममिन्द्र गवाशिरम | हरिभ्यां यस्ते अस्मयुः ||
3.42.e: COME to the juice that we have pressed, to Soma, Indra, bleat with milk:  Come, favouring us, thy Bay-drawn car!

3.42.d: तमिन्द्र मदमा गहि बर्हिष्ठां गरावभिः सुतम | कुविन नवस्य तर्प्णवः ||
3.42.e: Come, Indra, to this gladdening drink, placed on the grass, pressed out with stones:  Wilt thou not drink thy fill thereof?

3.42.d: इन्द्रमित्था गिरो ममाछागुरिषिता इतः | आव्र्ते सोमपीतये ||
3.42.e: To Indra have my songs of praise gone forth, thus rapidly sent hence,  To turn him to the Soma-draught.

3.42.d: इन्द्रं सोमस्य पीतये सतोमैरिह हवामहे | उक्थेभिः कुविदागमत ||
3.42.e: Hither with songs of praise we call Indra to drink the Soma juice:  Will he not come to us by lauds?

3.42.d: इन्द्र सोमाः सुता इमे तान दधिष्व शतक्रतो | जठरे वाजिनीवसो ||
3.42.e: Indra, these Somas are expressed. Take them within thy belly, Lord  Of Hundred Powers, thou Prince of Wealth.

3.42.d: विद्मा हि तवा धनंजयं वाजेषु दध्र्षं कवे | अधा तेसुम्नमीमहे ||
3.42.e: We know thee winner of the spoil, and resolute in battles, Sage!  Therefore thy blessing we implore.

3.42.d: इममिन्द्र गवाशिरं यवाशिरं च नः पिब | आगत्या वर्षभिः सुतम ||
3.42.e: Borne hither by thy Stallions, drink, Indra, this juice which we have pressed,  Mingled with barley and with milk.

3.42.d: तुभ्येदिन्द्र सव ओक्ये सोमं चोदामि पीतये | एष रारन्तु ते हर्दि ||
3.42.e: Indra, for thee, in thine own place, I urge the Soma for thy draught:  Deep in thy heart let it remain,

3.42.d: तवां सुतस्य पीतये परत्नमिन्द्र हवामहे | कुशिकासो अवस्यवः ||
3.42.e: We call on thee, the Ancient One, Indra, to drink the Soma juice,  We Kuśikas who seek thine aid.

3.43.d: आ याह्यर्वां उप वन्धुरेष्ठास्तवेदनु परदिवः सोमपेयम | परिया सखाया वि मुचोप बर्हिस्त्वामिमे हव्यवाहो हवन्ते ||
3.43.e: MOUNTED upon thy chariot-seat approach us: thine is the Soma-draught from days aforetime.  Loose for the sacred grass thy dear companions. These men who bring oblation call thee hither.

3.43.d: आ याहि पूर्वीरति चर्षणीरानर्य आशिष उप नो हरिभ्याम | इमा हि तवा मतय सतोमतष्टा इन्द्र हवन्ते सख्यं जुषाणाः ||
3.43.e: Come our true Friend, passing by many people; come with thy two Bay Steeds to our devotions;  For these our hymns are calling thee, O Indra, hymns formed for praise, soliciting thy friendship.

3.43.d: आ नो यज्ञं नमोव्र्धं सजोषा इन्द्र देव हरिभिर्याहि तूयम | अहं हि तवा मतिभिर्जोहवीमि घर्तप्रयाः सधमादे मधूनाम ||
3.43.e: Pleased, with thy Bay Steeds, Indra, God, come quickly to this our sacrifice that heightens worship;  For with my thoughts, presenting oil to feed thee, I call thee to the feast of sweet libations.

3.43.d: आ च तवामेता वर्षणा वहातो हरी सखाया सुधुरा सवङगा | धानावदिन्द्रः सवनं जुषाणः सखा सख्युः शर्णवद वन्दनानि ||
3.43.e: Yea, let thy two Bay Stallions bear thee hither, well limbed and good to draw, thy dear companions.  Pleased with the corn-blent offering which we bring thee, may Indra, Friend, hear his friend's adoration.

3.43.d: कुविन मा गोपां करसे जनस्य कुविद राजानं मघवन्न्र्जीषिन | कुविन म रषिं पपिवांसं सुतस्य कुविन मे वस्वो अम्र्तस्य शिक्षाः ||
3.43.e: Wilt thou not make me guardian of the people, make me, impetuous Maghavan, their ruler?  Make me a Ṛṣi having drunk of Soma? Wilt thou not give me wealth that lasts for ever?

3.43.d: आ तवा बर्हन्तो हरयो युजाना अर्वागिन्द्र सधमादो वहन्तु | पर ये दविता दिव रञ्जन्त्याताः सुसम्म्र्ष्टासो वर्षभस्य मूराः ||
3.43.e: Yoked to thy chariot, led thy tall Bays, Indra, companions of thy banquet, bear thee hither,  Who from of old press to heaven's farthest limits, the Bull's impetuous and well-groomed Horses.

3.43.d: इन्द्र पिब वर्षधूतस्य वर्ष्ण आ यं ते शयेन उशते जभार | यस्य मदे चयावयसि पर कर्ष्टीर्यस्य मदे अप गोत्रा ववर्थ ||
3.43.e: Drink of the strong pressed out by strong ones, Indra, that which the Falcon brought thee when thou longedst;  In whose wild joy thou stirrest up the people, in whose wild joy thou didst unbar the cow-stalls.
Call we on Indra, Makhavan, auspicious, best Hero in the fight where spoil is gathered;  The Strong, who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.

3.44.d: अयं ते अस्तु हर्यतः सोम आ हरिभिः सुतः | जुषाण इन्द्र हरिभिर्न आ गह्या तिष्ठ हरितं रथम ||
3.44.e: May this delightsome Soma be expressed for thee by tawny stones.  Joying thereat, O Indra, with thy Bay Steeds come:. ascend thy golden-coloured car.

3.44.d: हर्यन्नुषसमर्चयः सूर्यं हर्यन्नरोचयः | विद्वांष्चिकित्वान हर्यश्व वर्धस इन्द्र विश्वा अभि शरियः ||
3.44.e: In love thou madest Uṣas glow, in love thou madest Sūrya shine.  Thou, Indra, knowing, thinking, Lord of Tawny Steeds, above all glories waxest great.

3.44.d: दयामिन्द्रो हरिधायसं पर्थिवीं हरिवर्पसम | अधारयद धरितोर्भूरि भोजनं ययोरन्तर्हरिश्चरत ||
3.44.e: The heaven with streams of golden hue, earth with her tints of green and gold-  The golden Pair yield Indra plenteous nourishment: between them moves the golden One.

3.44.d: जज्ञानो हरितो वर्षा विश्वमा भाति रोचनम | हर्यश्वो हरितं धत्त आयुधमा वज्रं बाह्वोर्हरिम ||
3.44.e: When born to life the golden Bull illumines all the realm of light.  He takes his golden weapon, Lord of Tawny Steeds, the golden thunder in his arms.

3.44.d: इन्द्रो हर्यन्तमर्जुनं वज्रं शुक्रैरभीव्र्तम | अपाव्र्णोद धरिभिरद्रिभिः सुतमुद गा हरिभिराजत ||
3.44.e: The bright, the well-loved thunderbolt, girt with the bright, Indra disclosed,  Disclosed the Soma juice pressed out by tawny stones, with tawny steeds drave forth the kine.

3.45.d: आ मन्द्रैरिन्द्र हरिभिर्याहि मयूररोमभिः | मा तवा केचिन नि यमन विं न पाशिनो.अति धन्वेव तानिहि ||
3.45.e: COME hither, Indra, with Bay Steeds, joyous, with tails like peacocks' plumes.  Let no men cheek thy course as fowlers stay the bird: pass o’er them as o’er desert lands.

3.45.d: वर्त्रखादो वलंरुजः पुरां दर्मो अपामजः | सथाता रथस्य हर्योरभिस्वर इन्द्रो दर्ळ्हा चिदारुजः ||
3.45.e: He who slew Vṛtra, burst the cloud, brake the strongholds and drave the floods,  Indra who mounts his chariot at his Bay Steeds' cry, shatters e’en things that stand most firm.

3.45.d: गम्भीरानुदधीन्रिव करतुं पुष्यसि गा इव | पर सुगोपायवसं धेनवो यथा हरदं कुल्या इवाशत ||
3.45.e: Like pools of water deep and full, like kine thou cherishest thy might;  Like the milch-cows that go well-guarded to the mead, like water-brooks that reach the lake.

3.45.d: आ नस्तुजं रयिं भरांशं न परतिजानते | वर्क्षं पक्वं फलमङकीव धूनुहीन्द्र सम्पारणं वसु ||
3.45.e: Bring thou us wealth with power to strike, our share, 'gainst him who calls it his.  Shake, Indra, as with hooks, the tree for ripened fruit, for wealth to satisfy our wish.

3.45.d: सवयुरिन्द्र सवराळ असि समद्दिष्टिः सवयशस्तरः | स वाव्र्धान ओजसा पुरुष्टुत भवा नः सुश्रवस्तमः ||
3.45.e: Indra, self-ruling Lord art thou, good Leader, of most glorious fame.  So, waxen in thy strength, O thou whom many praise, be thou most swift to hear our call.

3.46.d: युध्मस्य ते वर्षभस्य सवराज उग्रस्य यून सथविरस्य घर्ष्वेः | अजूर्यतो वज्रिणो वीर्याणीन्द्र शरुतस्य महतो महानि ||
3.46.e: OF thee, the Bull, the Warrior, Sovran Ruler, joyous and fierce, ancient and ever youthful,  The undecaying One who wields the thunder, renowned and great, great are the exploits, Indra.

3.46.d: महानसि महिष वर्ष्ण्येभिर्धनस्प्र्दुग्र सहमानो अन्यान | एको विश्वस्य भुवनस्य राजा स योधया च कषयया च जनान ||
3.46.e: Great art thou, Mighty Lord, through manly vigour, O fierce One, gathering spoil, subduing others,  Thyself alone the universe's Sovran: so send forth men to combat and to rest them.

3.46.d: पर मात्राभी रिरिचे रोचमानः पर देवेभिर्विश्वतो अप्रतीतः | पर मज्मना दिव इन्द्रः पर्थिव्याः परोरोर्महो अन्तरिक्षाद रजीषी ||
3.46.e: He hath surpassed all measure in his brightness, yea, and the Gods, for none may be his equal.  Impetuous Indra in his might cxccedcth wide vast mid-air and heaven and earth together.

3.46.d: उरुं गभीरं जनुषाभ्युग्रं विश्वव्यचसमवतं मतीनाम | इन्द्रं सोमासः परदिवि सुतासः समुद्रं न सरवता विशन्ति ||
3.46.e: To Indra, even as rivers to the ocean, flow forth from days of old the Soma juices;  To him wide deep and mighty from his birth-time, the well of holy thoughts, aIl-comprehending.

3.46.d: यं सोममिन्द्र पर्थिवीद्यावा गर्भं न माता बिभ्र्तस्त्वाया | तं ते हिन्वन्ति तमु ते मर्जन्त्यध्वर्यवो वर्षभ पातवा उ ||
3.46.e: The Soma, Indra, which the earth and heaven bear for thee as a mother bears her infant,  This they send forth to thee, this, vigorous Hero! Adhvaryus purify for thee to drink of.

3.47.d: मरुत्वानिन्द्र वर्षभो रणाय पिबा सोममनुष्वधं मदाय | आ सिञ्चस्व जठरे मध्व ऊर्मिं तवं राजासि परदिवः सुतानाम ||
3.47.e: DRINK, Indra, Marut-girt, as Bull, the Soma, for joy, for rapture even as thou listest.  Pour down the flood of meath within thy belly: thou from of old art King of Soma juices.

3.47.d: सजोषा इन्द्र सगणो मरुद्भिः सोमं पिब वर्त्रहा शूर विद्वान | जहि शत्रून्रप मर्धो नुदस्वाथाभयं कर्णुहि विश्वतो नः ||
3.47.e: Indra, accordant, with the banded Maruts, drink Soma, Hero, as wise Vṛtra-slayer.  Slay thou our foemen, drive away assailants and make us safe on every side from danger.

3.47.d: उत रतुभिर्र्तुपाः पाहि सोममिन्द्र देवेभिः सखिभिः सुतं नः | यानाभजो मरुतो ये तवान्वहन वर्त्रमदधुस्तुभ्यमोजः ||
3.47.e: And, drinker at due seasons, drink in season, Indra, with friendly Gods, our pressed-out Soma.  The Maruts following, whom thou madest sharers, gave thee the victory, and thou slewest Vṛtra.

3.47.d: ये तवाहिहत्ये मघवन्नवर्धन ये शाम्बरे हरिवो ये गविष्टौ | ये तवा नूनमनुमदन्ति विप्राः पिबेन्द्र सोमं सगणो मरुद्भिः ||
3.47.e: Drink Soma, Indra, banded with the Maruts who, Maghavan, strengthened thee at Ahi's slaughter,  'Gainst Śambara, Lord of Bays! in winning cattle, and now rejoice in thee, the holy Singers.

3.47.d: मरुत्वन्तं वर्षभं वाव्र्धानमकवारिं दिव्यं शासमिन्द्रम | विश्वासाहमवसे नूतनायोग्रं सहोदामिह तंहुवेम ||
3.47.e: The Bull whose strength hath waxed, whom Maruts follow, free-giving Indra, the celestial Ruler,  Mighty, all-conquering, the victory-giver, him let us call to grant us new protection.

3.48.d: सद्यो ह जातो वर्षभः कनीनः परभर्तुमावदन्धसः सुतस्य | साधोः पिब परतिकामं यथा ते रसाशिरः परथमं सोम्यस्य ||
3.48.e: SOON as the young Bull sprang into existence he longed to taste the pressed-out Soma's liquor.  Drink thou thy fill, according to thy longing, first, of the goodly mixture blent with Soma.

3.48.d: यज्जायथास्तदहरस्य कामे.अंशोः पीयूषमपिबो गिरिष्ठाम | तं ते माता परि योषा जनित्री महः पितुर्दम आसिञ्चदग्रे ||
3.48.e: That day when thou wast born thou, fain to taste it, drankest the plant's milk which the mountains nourish.  That milk thy Mother first, the Dame who bare thee, poured for thee in thy mighty Father's dwelling.

3.48.d: उपस्थाय मातरमन्नमैट्ट तिग्ममपश्यदभि सोममूधः | परयावयन्नचरद गर्त्सो अन्यान महानि चक्रे पुरुधप्रतीकः ||
3.48.e: Desiring food he came unto his Mother, and on her breast beheld the pungent Soma.  Wise, he moved on, keeping aloof the others, and wrought great exploits in his varied aspects.

3.48.d: उग्रस्तुराषाळ अभिभूत्योजा यथावशं तन्वं चक्र एषः | तवष्टारमिन्द्रो जनुषाभिभूयामुष्या सोममपिबच्चमूषु ||
3.48.e: Fierce, quickly conquering, of surpassing vigour, he framed his body even as he listed.  E’en from his birth-time Indra conquered Tvaṣṭar, bore off the Soma and in beakers drank it.
Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best Hero in the fight where spoil is gathered;  The Strong, who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.

3.49.d: शंसा महामिन्द्रं यस्मिन विश्वा आ कर्ष्टयः सोमपाः काममव्यन | यं सुक्रतुं धिषणे विभ्वतष्टं घनं वर्त्राणां जनयन्त देवाः ||
3.49.e: GREAT Indra will I laud, in whom all people who drink the Soma have attained their longing;  Whom, passing wise, Gods, Heaven and Earth, engendered, formed by a Master's hand, to crush the Vṛtras.

3.49.d: यं नु नकिः पर्तनासु सवराजं दविता तरति नर्तमं हरिष्ठाम | इनतमः सत्वभिर्यो ह शूषैः पर्थुज्रया अमिनादायुर्दस्योः ||
