3.49.e: Whom, most heroic, borne by Tawny Coursers, verily none subdueth in the battle;  Who, reaching far, most vigorous, hath shortened the Dasyu's life with Warriors bold of spirit.

3.49.d: सहावा पर्त्सु तरणिर्नार्वा वयानशी रोदसी मेहनावान | भगो न कारे हव्यो मतीनां पितेव चारुः सुहवो वयोधाः ||
3.49.e: Victor in fight, swift mover like a warhorse, pervading both worlds, rainer down of blessings,  To he invoked in war like Bhaga, Father, as ’twere, of hymns, fair, prompt to hear, strength-giver.

3.49.d: धर्ता दिवो रजसस पर्ष्ट ऊर्ध्वो रथो न वायुर्वसुभिर्नियुत्वान | कषपां वस्ता जनिता सूर्यस्य विभक्ता भागं धिषणेव वाजम ||
3.49.e: Supporting heaven, the high back of the region, his car is Vāyu with his team of Vasus.  Illumining the nights, the Sun's creator, like Dhiṣaṇā he deals forth strength and riches.
Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best Hero in the fight where spoil is gathered;  The Strong, who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers treasure.

3.50.d: इन्द्रः सवाहा पिबतु यस्य सोम आगत्या तुम्रो वर्षभो मरुत्वान | ओरुव्यचाः पर्णतामेभिरन्नैरास्य हविस्तन्वःकामं रध्याः ||
3.50.e: LET Indra drink, All-hail! for his is Soma,—the mighty Bull come, girt by Maruts, hither.  Far-reaching, let him fill him with these viands, and let our offering sate his body's longing.

3.50.d: आ ते सपर्यू जवसे युनज्मि ययोरनु परदिवः शरुष्टिमावः | इह तवा धेयुर्हरयः सुशिप्र पिबा तवस्य सुषुतस्य चारोः ||
3.50.e: I yoke thy pair of trusty Steeds for swiftness, whose faithful service from of old thou lovest.  Here, fair of cheek! let thy Bay Coursers place thee: drink of this lovely welleffused libation.

3.50.d: गोभिर्मिमिक्षुं दधिरे सुपारमिन्द्रं जयैष्ठ्याय धायसे गर्णानाः | मन्दानः सोमं पपिवान रजीषिन समस्मभ्यं पुरुधा गा इषण्य ||
3.50.e: With milk they made Indra their good Preserver, lauding for help and rule the bounteous rainer.  Impetuous God, when thou hast drunk the Soma, enraptured send us cattle in abundance.
With kine and horses satisfy this longing with very splendid bounty still extend it.  Seeking the light, with hymns to thee, O Indra, the Kuśikas have brought their gift, the singers.
Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best Hero in the fight where spoil is gathered;  The Strong, who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.

3.51.d: चर्षणीध्र्तं मघवानमुक्थ्यमिन्द्रं गिरो बर्हतीरभ्यनूषत | वाव्र्धानं पुरुहूतं सुव्र्क्तिभिरमर्त्यं जरमाणं दिवे-दिवे ||
3.51.e: HIGH hymns have sounded forth the praise of Maghavan, supporter of mankind, of Indra meet for lauds;  Him who hath waxen great, invoked with beauteous songs, Immortal One, whose praise each day is sung aloud.

3.51.d: शतक्रतुमर्णवं शाकिनं नरं गिरो म इन्द्रमुप यन्ति विश्वतः | वाजसनिं पूर्भिदं तूर्णिमप्तुरं धामसाचमभिषाचं सवर्विदम ||
3.51.e: To Indra from all sides go forth my songs of praise, the Lord of Hundred Powers, strong, Hero, like the sea,  Swift, winner of the booty, breaker-down of forts, faithful and ever-glorious, finder of the light.

3.51.d: आकरे वसोर्जरिता पनस्यते.अनेहस सतुभ इन्द्रो दुवस्यति | विवस्वतः सदन आ हि पिप्रिये सत्रासाहमभिमातिहनं सतुहि ||
3.51.e: Where battle's spoil is piled the singer winneth praise, for Indra taketh care of matchless worshippers.  He in Vivasvān's dwelling findeth his delight: praise thou the ever-conquering slayer of the foe.

3.51.d: नर्णामु तवा नर्तमं गीर्भिरुक्थैरभि पर वीरमर्चता सबाधः | सं सहसे पुरुमायो जिहीते नमो अस्य परदिव एक ईशे ||
3.51.e: Thee, valorous, most heroic of the heroes, shall the priests glorify with songg and praises.  Full of all wondrous power he goes to conquest: worship is his, sole Lord from days aforetime.

3.51.d: पूर्वीरस्य निष्षिधो मर्त्येषु पुरू वसूनि पर्थिवी बिभर्ति | इन्द्राय दयाव ओषधीरुतापो रयिं रक्षन्ति जीरयो वनानि ||
3.51.e: Abundant are the gifts he gives to mortals: for him the earth bears a rich store of treasures.  The heavens, the growing plants, the living waters, the forest trees preserve their wealth for Indra.

3.51.d: तुभ्यं बरह्माणि गिर इन्द्र तुभ्यं सत्रा दधिरे हरिवो जुषस्व | बोध्यापिरवसो नूतनस्य सखे वसो जरित्र्भ्यो वयोधाः ||
3.51.e: To thee, O Indra, Lord of Bays, for ever are offered prayers and songs: accept them gladly.  As Kinsman think thou of some fresh assistance; good Friend, give strength and life to those who praise thee.

3.51.d: इन्द्र मरुत्व इह पाहि सोमं यथा शार्याते अपिबः सुतस्य | तव परणीती तव शूर शर्मन्ना विवासन्ति कवयःसुयज्ञाः ||
3.51.e: Here, Indra, drink thou Soma with the Maruts, as thou didst drink the juice beside Śāryāta.  Under thy guidance, in thy keeping, Hero, the singers serve, skilled in fair sacrifices.

3.51.d: स वावशान इह पाहि सोमं मरुद्भिरिन्द्र सखिभिः सुतं नः | जातं यत तवा परि देवा अभूषन महे भराय पुरुहूत विश्वे ||
3.51.e: So eagerly desirous drink the Soma, our juice, O Indra, with thy friends the Maruts,  Since at thy birth all Deities adorned thee for the great fight, O thou invoked of many.

3.51.d: अप्तूर्ये मरुत आपिरेषो.अमन्दन्निन्द्रमनु दातिवाराः | तेभिः साकं पिबतु वर्त्रखादः सुतं सोमं दाशुषः सवे सधस्थे ||
3.51.e: He was your comrade in your zeal, O Maruts: they, rich in noble gifts, rejoiced in Indra.  With them together let the Vṛtra-slayer drink in his home the worshipper's libation.

3.51.d: इदं हयन्वोजसा सुतं राधानां पते | पिबा तवस्य गिर्वणः ||
3.51.e: So, Lord of affluent gifts, this juice hath been pressed for thee with strength  Drink of it, thou who lovest song.

3.51.d: यस्ते अनु सवधामसत सुते नि यछ तन्वम | स तवा ममत्तु सोम्यम ||
3.51.e: Incline thy body to this juice which suits thy Godlike nature well:  May it cheer thee who lovest it.

3.51.d: पर ते अश्नोतु कुक्ष्योः परेन्द्र बरह्मणा शिरः | पर बाहू शूर राधसे ||
3.51.e: Brave Indra, let it work through both thy flanks, and through thy head by prayer,  And through thine arms, to prosper us.

3.52.e: INDRA, accept at break of day our Soma mixt with roasted corn,  With groats with cake, with eulogies.

3.52.d: पुरोळाशं पचत्यं जुषस्वेन्द्रा गुरस्व च | तुभ्यं हव्यानि सिस्रते ||
3.52.e: Accept, O Indra, and enjoy the well-dressed sacrificial cake: Oblations are poured forth to thee.

3.52.d: पुरोळाशं च नो घसो जोषयासे गिरश्च नः | वधूयुरिव योषणाम ||
3.52.e: Consume our sacrificial cake, accept the songs of praise we sing,  As he who woes accepts his bride.

3.52.d: पुरोळाशं सनश्रुत परातःसावे जुषस्व नः | इन्द्र करतुर्हि ते बर्हन ||
3.52.e: Famed from of old, accept the cake at our libation poured at dawn,  Forgreat, O Indra, is thy power.

3.52.d: माध्यन्दिनस्य सवनस्य धानाः पुरोळाशमिन्द्र कर्ष्वेहचारुम | पर यत सतोता जरिता तूर्ण्यर्थो वर्षायमाण उप गीर्भिरीट्टे ||
3.52.e: Let roasted corn of our midday libation, and sacrificial cake here please thee, Indra,  What time the lauding singer, keen of purpose and eager as a bull, with hymns implores thee.

3.52.d: तर्तीये धानाः सवने पुरुष्टुत पुरोळाशमाहुतं मामहस्व नः | रभुमन्तं वाजवन्तं तवा कवे परयस्वन्त उप शिक्षेम धीतिभिः ||
3.52.e: At the third sacrifice, O thou whom many praise, give glory to the roasted corn and holy cake.  With offered viands and with songs may we assist thee, Sage, whom Vāja and the Ṛbhus wait upon.

3.52.d: पूषण्वते ते चक्र्मा करम्भं हरिवते हर्यश्वाय धानाः | अपूपमद्धि सगणो मरुद्भिः सोमं पिब वर्त्रहा शूर विद्वान ||
3.52.e: The groats have we prepared for thee with Pūṣan, corn for thee, Lord of Bay Steeds, with thy horses.  Eat thou the meal-cake, banded with the Maruts, wise Hero, Vṛtra-slayer, drink the Soma.

3.52.d: परति धाना भरत तूयमस्मै पुरोळाशं वीरतमाय नर्णाम | दिवे-दिवे सद्र्शीरिन्द्र तुभ्यं वर्धन्तु तवा सोमपेयाय धर्ष्णो ||
3.52.e: Bring forth the roasted corn to meet him quickly, cake for the bravest Hero mid the heroes.  Indra, may hymns accordant with thee daily strengthen thee, Bold One, for the draught of Soma.

3.53.d: इन्द्रापर्वता बर्हता रथेन वामीरिष आ वहतं सुवीराः | वीतं हव्यान्यध्वरेषु देवा वर्धेथां गीर्भीरिळया मदन्ता ||
3.53.e: ON a high car, O Parvata and Indra, bring pleasant viands, with brave heroes, hither.  Enjoy the gifts, Gods, at our sacrifices wax strong by hymns, rejoice in our oblation.

3.53.d: तिष्ठा सु कं मघवन मा परा गाः सोमस्य नु तवा सुषुतस्य यक्षि | पितुर्न पुत्रः सिचमा रभे त इन्द्र सवादिष्ठया गिरा शचीवः ||
3.53.e: Stay still, O Maghavan, advance no farther. a draught of well-pressed Soma will I give thee.  With sweetest song I grasp, O Mighty Indra, thy garment's hem as a child grasps his father's.

3.53.d: शंसावाध्वर्यो परति मे गर्णीहीन्द्राय वाहः कर्णवाव जुष्टम | एदं बर्हिर्यजमानस्य सीदाथा च भूदुक्थमिन्द्राय शस्तम ||
3.53.e: Adhvaryu, sing we both; sing thou in answer: make we a laud acceptable to Indra.  Upon this sacrificer's grass he seated: to Indra shall our eulogy be uttered.

3.53.d: जायेदस्तं मघवन सेदु योनिस्तदित तवा युक्ता हरयो वहन्तु | यदा कदा च सुनवाम सोममग्निष टवा दूतो धन्वात्यछ ||
3.53.e: A wife, O Maghavan is home and dwelling: so let thy Bay Steeds yoked convey thee hither.  Whenever we press out for thee the Soma, let Agni as our Herald speed to call thee.

3.53.d: परा याहि मघवन्ना च याहीन्द्र भरातरुभयत्रा ते अर्थम | यत्रा रथस्य बर्हतो निधानं विमोचनं वाजिनो रासभस्य ||
3.53.e: Depart, O Maghavan;again come hither: both there and here thy goat is Indra, Brother,  Where thy tall chariot hath a place to rest in, and where thqu loosest thy loud-neighing Courser.

3.53.d: अपाः सोममस्तमिन्द्र पर याहि कल्याणीर्जया सुरणंग्र्हे ते | यत्रा रथस्य बर्हतो निधानं विमोचनं वाजिनोदक्षिणावत ||
3.53.e: Thou hast drunk Soma, Indra, turn thee homeward; thy joy is in thy home, thy racious Consort;  Where thy tall chariot hath a place to rest in, and thy strong Courser is set free with guerdon.

3.53.d: इमे भोजा अङगिरसो विरूपा दिवस पुत्रासो असुरस्य वीराः | विश्वामित्राय ददतो मघानि सहस्रसावे पर तिरन्त आयुः ||
3.53.e: Bounteous are these, Aṅgirases, Virupas: the Asura's Heroes and the Sons of Heaven.  They, giving store of wealth to Viśvāmitra, prolong his life through countless Soma-pressings.

3.53.d: रूपं-रूपं मघवा बोभवीति मायाः कर्ण्वानस्तन्वं परि सवाम | तरिर्यद दिवः परि मुहूर्तमागात सवैर्मन्त्रैरन्र्तुपा रतावा ||
3.53.e: Maghavan weareth every shape at pleasure, effecting magic changes in his body,  Holy One, drinker out of season, coming thrice, in a moment, through fit prayers, from heaven.

3.53.d: महान रषिर्देवजा देवजूतो.अस्तभ्नात सिन्धुमर्णवं नर्चक्षाः | विश्वामित्रो यदवहत सुदासमप्रियायत कुशिकेभिरिन्द्रः ||
3.53.e: The mighty sage, God-born and God-incited, who looks on men, restrained the billowy river.  When Viśvāmitra was Sudās's escort, then Indra through the Kuśikas grew friendly.

3.53.d: हंसा इव कर्णुथ शलोकमद्रिभिर्मदन्तो गीर्भिरध्वरे सुते सचा | देवेभिर्विप्रा रषयो नर्चक्षसो वि पिबध्वं कुशिकाः सोम्यं मधु ||
3.53.e: Like swans, prepare a song of praise with pressing-stones, glad in your hymns with juice poured forth in sacrifice.  Ye singers, with the Gods, sages who look on men, ye Kutikas drink up the Soma's savoury meath.

3.53.d: उप परेत कुशिकाश्चेतयध्वमश्वं राये पर मुञ्चता सुदासः | राजा वर्त्रं जङघनत परागपागुदगथा यजाते वर आ पर्थिव्याः ||
3.53.e: Come forward, Kuśikas, and be attentive; let loose Sudās's horse to win him riches.  East, west, and north, let the King slay the foeman, then at earth's choicest place perform his worship.

3.53.d: य इमे रोदसी उभे अहमिन्द्रमतुष्टवम | विश्वामित्रस्यरक्षति बरह्मेदं भारतं जनम ||
3.53.e: Praises to Indra have I sung, sustainer of this earth and heaven. This prayer of Viśvāmitra keeps secure the race of Bharatas.

3.53.d: विश्वामित्रा अरासत बरह्मेन्द्राय वज्रिणे | करदिन नः सुराधसः ||
3.53.e: The Viśvāmitras have sung forth this prayer to Indra Thunder-aimed:  So let him make us prosperous.

3.53.d: किं ते कर्ण्वन्ति कीकटेषु गावो नाशिरं दुह्रे न तपन्तिघर्मम | आ नो भर परमगन्दस्य वेदो नैचाशाखं मघवन्रन्धया नः ||
3.53.e: Among the Kikatas what do thy cattle? They pour no milky draught, they heat no caldron.  Bring thou to us the wealth of Pramaganda;give up to us, O Maghavan, the low-born.

3.53.d: ससर्परीरमतिं बाधमाना बर्हन मिमाय जमदग्निदत्ता | आ सूर्यस्य दुहिता ततान शरवो देवेष्वम्र्तमजुर्यम ||
3.53.e: Sasarpari, the gift of Jamadagnis, hath lowed with mighty voice dispelling famine.  The Daughter of the Sun hath spread our glory among the Gods, imperishable, deathless.

3.53.d: ससर्परीरभरत तूयमेभ्यो.अधि शरवः पाञ्चजन्यासु कर्ष्टिषु | सा पक्ष्या नव्यमायुर्दधाना यां मे पलस्तिजमदग्नयो ददुः ||
3.53.e: Sasarpari brought glory speedily to these, over the generations of the Fivefold Race;  Daughter of Paksa, she bestows new vital power, she whom the ancient Jamadagnis gave to me.

3.53.d: सथिरौ गावौ भवतां वीळुरक्षो मेषा वि वर्हि मा युगं वि शारि | इन्द्रः पातल्ये ददतां शरीतोररिष्टनेमे अभि नः सचस्व ||
3.53.e: Strong be the pair of oxen, firm the axles, let not the pole slip nor the yoke be broken.  May Indra, keep the yoke-pins from decaying: attend us, thou whose fellies are uninjured.

3.53.d: बलं धेहि तनूषु नो बलमिन्द्रानळुत्सु नः | बलं तोकाय तनयाय जीवसे तवं हि बलदा असि ||
3.53.e: O Indra, give our bodies strength, strength to the bulls who draw the wains,  Strength to our seed and progeny that they may live, for thou art he who giveth strength.

3.53.d: अभि वययस्व खदिरस्य सारमोजो धेहि सपन्दने शिंशपायाम | अक्ष वीळो वीळित वीळयस्व मा यामादस्मादव जीहिपो नः ||
3.53.e: Enclose thee in the heart of Khayar timber, in the car wrought of Sinsapa put firmness.  Show thyself strong, O Axle, fixed and strengthened: throw us not from the car whereon we travel.

3.53.d: अयमस्मान वनस्पतिर्मा च हा मा च रीरिषत | सवस्त्याग्र्हेभ्य आवसा आ विमोचनात ||
3.53.e: Let not this sovran of the wood leave us forlorn or injure us.  Safe may we be until we reach our homes and rest us and unyoke.

3.53.d: इन्द्रोतिभिर्बहुलाभिर्नो अद्य याच्छ्रेष्ठाभिर्मघवञ्छूर जिन्व | यो नो दवेष्ट्यधरः सस पदीष्ट यमु दविष्मस्तमु पराणो जहातु ||
3.53.e: With various aids this day come to us, Indra, with best aids speed us, Maghavan, thou Hero.  Let him who hatcth us fall headlong downward: him whom we hate let vital breath abandon.

3.53.d: परशुं चिद वि तपति शिम्बलं चिद वि वर्श्चति | उखा चिदिन्द्र येषन्ती परयस्ता फेनमस्यति ||
3.53.e: He heats his very axe, and then cuts a mere Semal blossom off.  O Indra, like a caldron cracked and seething, so he pours out foam.

3.53.d: न सायकस्य चिकिते जनासो लोधं नयन्ति पशु मन्यमानाः | नावाजिनं वाजिना हासयन्ति न गर्दभं पुरो अश्वान नयन्ति ||
3.53.e: Men notice not the arrow, O ye people; they bring the red beast deeming it a bullock.  A sluggish steed men run not with the courser, nor ever lead an ass before a charger.

3.53.d: इम इन्द्र भरतस्य पुत्रा अपपित्वं चिकितुर्न परपित्वम | हिन्वन्त्यश्वमरणं न नित्यं जयावाजं परि णयन्त्याजौ ||
3.53.e: These men, the sons of Bhārata, O Indra, regard not severance or close connexion.  They urge their own steed as it were another's, and take him, swift as the bow's string, to battle.

3.54.d: इमं महे विदथ्याय शूषं शश्वत कर्त्व ईड्यय पर जभ्रुः | शर्णोतु नो दम्येभिरनीकैः शर्णोत्वग्निर्दिव्यैरजस्रः ||
3.54.e: To him adorable, mighty, meet for synods, this strengthening hymn, unceasing, have they offered.  May Agni hear us with his homely splendours, hear us, Eternal One, with heavenly lustre.

3.54.d: महि महे दिवे अर्चा पर्थिव्यै कामो म इछञ्चरति परजानन | ययोर्ह सतोमे विदथेषु देवाः सपर्यवो मादयन्ते सचायोः ||
3.54.e: To mighty Heaven and Earth I sing forth loudly: my wish goes out desirous and well knowing  Both, at whose laud in synods, showing favour, the Gods rejoice them with the living mortal.

3.54.d: युवोर्र्तं रोदसी सत्यमस्तु महे षु णः सुविताय पर भूतम | इदं दिवे नमो अग्ने पर्थिव्यै सपर्यामि परयसा यामि रत्नम ||
3.54.e: O Heaven and Earth, may your great law he faithful: he ye our leaders for our high advantage.  To Heaven and Earth I offer this my homage, with food, O Agni, as I pray for riches.

3.54.d: उतो हि वां पूर्व्या आविविद्र रतावरी रोदसी सत्यवाचः | नरश्चिद वां समिथे शूरसातौ ववन्दिरे पर्थिवि वेविदानाः ||
3.54.e: Yea, holy Heaven and Earth, the ancient sages whose word was ever true had power to find you;  And brave men in the fightwhere heroes conquer, O Earth, have known you well and paid you honour.

3.54.d: को अद्धा वेद क इह पर वोचद देवानछा पथ्या का समेति | दद्र्श्र एषामवमा सदांसि परेषु या गुह्येषु वरतेषु ||
3.54.e: What pathway leadeth to the Gods? Who knoweth this of a truth, and who will now declare it?  Seen are their lowest dwelling-places only, but they are in remote and secret regions.

3.54.d: कविर्न्र्चक्षा अभि षीमचष्ट रतस्य योना विघ्र्ते मदन्ती | नाना चक्राते सदनं यथा वः समानेन करतुना संविदाने ||
3.54.e: The Sage who looketh on mankind hath viewed them bedewed, rejoicing in the seat of Order.  They make a home as for a bird, though parted, with one same will finding themselves together.

3.54.d: समान्या वियुते दूरेन्ते धरुवे पदे तस्थतुर्जागरूके | उत सवसारा युवती भवन्ती आदु बरुवाते मिथुनानि नाम ||
3.54.e: Partners though parted, with far-distant limits, on one firm place both stand for ever watchful,  And, being young for evermore, as sisters, speak to each other names that are united.

3.54.d: विश्वेदेते जनिमा सं विविक्तो महो देवान बिभ्रती न वयथेते | एजद धरुवं पत्यते विश्वमेकं चरत पतत्रि विषुणं वि जातम ||
3.54.e: All living things they part and keep asunder; though bearing up the mighty Gods they reel not.  One All is Lord of what is fixed and moving, that walks, that flies, this multiform creation.

3.54.d: सना पुराणमध्येम्यारान महः पितुर्जनितुर्जामि तन नः | देवासो यत्र पनितार एवैरुरौ पथि वयुते तस्थुरन्तः ||
3.54.e: Afar the Ancient from of old I ponder, our kinship with our mighty Sire and Father,—  Singing the praise whereof the Gods by custom stand on the spacious far-extended pathway.

3.54.d: इमं सतोमं रोदसी पर बरवीम्य रदूदराः शर्णवन्नग्निजिह्वाः | मित्रः सम्राजो वरुणो युवान आदित्यासः कवयः पप्रथानाः ||
3.54.e: This laud, O Heaven and Earth, to you I utter: let the kind-hearted hear, whose tongue is Agni,  Young, Sovran Rulers, Varuṇa and Mitra, the wise and very glorious Ādityas.

3.54.d: हिरण्यपाणिः सविता सुजिह्वस्त्रिरा दिवो विदथे पत्यमानः | देवेषु च सवितः शलोकमश्रेरादस्मभ्यमा सुवसर्वतातिम ||
3.54.e: The fair-tongued Savitar, the golden-handed, comes thrice from heaven as Lord in our assembly.  Bear to the Gods this song of praise, and send us, then, Savitar, complete and perfect safety.

3.54.d: सुक्र्त सुपाणिः सववान रतावा देवस्त्वष्टावसे तानि नोधात | पूषण्वन्त रभवो मादयध्वमूर्ध्वग्रावाणो अध्वरमतष्ट ||
3.54.e: Deft worker, skiful-handed, helpful, holy, may Tvaṣṭar, God, give us these things to aid us,  Take your delight, Ye Ṛbhus joined with Pūṣan: ye have prepared the rite with stones adjusted.

3.54.d: विद्युद्रथा मरुत रष्टिमन्तो दिवो मर्या रतजाता अयासः | सरस्वती शर्णवन यज्ञियासो धाता रयिं सहवीरं तुरासः ||
3.54.e: Borne on their flashing car, the spear-armed Maruts, the nimble Youths of Heaven, the Sons of Order,  The Holy, and Sarasvatī, shall hear us: ye Mighty, give us wealth with noble offspring.

3.54.d: विष्णुं सतोमासः पुरुदस्ममर्का भगस्येव कारिणो यामनि गमन | उरुक्रमः ककुहो यस्य पूर्विर्न मर्धन्ति युवतयोजनित्रीः ||
3.54.e: To Viṣṇu rich in marvels, songs And praises shall go as singers on the road of Bhaga,—  The Chieftain of the Mighty Stride, whose Mothers, the many young Dames, never disregard him.

3.54.d: इन्द्रो विश्वैर्वीर्यैः पत्यमान उभे आ पप्रौ रोदसी महित्वा | पुरन्दरो वर्त्रहा धर्ष्णुषेणः संग्र्भ्या न आ भरा भूरि पश्वः ||
3.54.e: Indra, who rules through all his powers heroic, hath with his majesty filled earth and heaven.  Lord of brave hosts, Fort-crusher, Vṛtra-slayer, gather thou up and bring us store of cattle.

3.54.d: नासत्या मे पितरा बन्धुप्र्छा सजात्यमश्विनोश्चारु नाम | युवं हि सथो रयिदौ नो रयीणां दात्रं रक्षेथे अकवैरदब्धा ||
3.54.e: My Sires are the Nāsatyas, kind tokinsmen: the Aśvins' kinship is a glorious title.  For ye are they who give us store of riches: ye guard your gift uncheated by the bounteous.

3.54.d: महत तद वः कवयश्चारु नाम यद ध देव भवथ विश्व इन्द्रे | सख रभुभिः पुरुहूत परियेभिरिमां धियं सातये तक्षता नः ||
3.54.e: This is, ye Wise, your great and glorious title, that all ye Deities abide in Indra.  Friend, Much-invoked! art thou with thy dear Ṛbhus: fashion ye this our hymn for our advantage.

3.54.d: अर्यमा णो अदितिर्यज्ञियासो.अदब्धानि वरुणस्य वरतानि | युयोत नो अनपत्यानि गन्तोः परजावान नः पशुमानस्तु गातुः ||
3.54.e: Aryaman, Aditi deserve our worship: the laws of Varuṇa remain unbroken.  The lot of childlessness remove ye from us, and let our course be rich in kine and offspring.

3.54.d: देवानां दूतः पुरुध परसूतो.अनागान नो वोचतु सर्वताता | शर्णोतु नः पर्थिवी दयौरुतापः सूर्यो नक्षत्रैरुर्वन्तरिक्षम ||
3.54.e: May the Gods’ envoy, sent to many a quarter, proclaim us sinless for our perfect safety.  May Earth and Heaven, the Sun, the waters, hear us, and the wide firmament and constellations.

3.54.d: शर्ण्वन्तु नो वर्षणः पर्वतासो धरुवक्षेमास इळया मदन्तः | आदित्यैर्नो अदितिः शर्णोतु यछन्तु नो मरुतः शर्मभद्रम ||
3.54.e: Hear us the mouatains which distil the rain-drops, and, resting firm, rejoice in freshening moisture.  May Aditi with the Ādityas hear us, and Maruts grant us their auspicious shelter.

3.54.d: सदा सुगः पितुमानस्तु पन्था मध्व देवा ओषधीः सम्पिप्र्क्त | भगो मे अग्ने सख्ये न मर्ध्या उद रायो अश्यां सदनं पुरुक्षोः ||
3.54.e: Soft be our path for ever, well-provisioned: with pleasant meath, O Gods, the herbs besprinkle.  Safe be my bliss, O Agni, in thy friendship: may I attain the seat of foodful. riches,

3.54.d: सवदस्व हव्या समिषो दिदीह्यस्मद्र्यक सं मिमीहि शरवांसि | विश्वानग्ने पर्त्सु तञ जेषि शत्रूनहा विश्वा सुमना दीदिही नः ||
3.54.e: Enjoy the offering: beam thou strength upon us; combine thou for our good all kinds of glory.  Conquer in battle, Agni, all those foemen, and light us every day with loving kindness.

3.55.d: उषसः पूर्वा अध यद वयूषुर्महद वि जज्ञे अक्षरं पदे गोः | वरता देवानामुप नु परभूषन महद देवानामसुरत्वमेकम ||
3.55.e: AT the first shining of the earliest Mornings, in the Cow's home was born the Great Eternal.  Now shall the statutes of the Gods be valid. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion -

3.55.d: मो षू णो अत्र जुहुरन्त देवा मा पूर्वे अग्ने पितरः पदज्ञाः | पुराण्योः सद्मनोः केतुरन्तर्म... ||
3.55.e: Let not the Gods here injure us, O Agni, nor Fathers of old time who know the region,  Nor the sign set between two ancient dwellings. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: वि मे पुरुत्रा पतयन्ति कामाः शम्यछा दीद्ये पूर्व्याणि | समिद्धे अग्नाव रतमिद वदेम म... ||
3.55.e: My wishes fly abroad to many places: I glance back to the ancient sacrifices.  Let us declare the truth when fire is kindled. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: समानो राजा विभ्र्तः पुरुत्रा शये शयासु परयुतो वनानु | अन्या वत्सं भरति कषेति माता म... ||
3.55.e: King Universal, born to sundry quarters, extended through the wood be lies on couches.  One Mother rests: another feeds the Infant. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: आक्षित पूर्वास्वपरा अनूरुत सद्यो जातासु तरुणीष्वन्तः | अन्तर्वतीः सुवते अप्रवीता म... ||
3.55.e: Lodged in old plants, he grows again in younger, swiftly within the newly-born and tender.  Though they are unimpregned, he makes them fruitful. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: शयुः परस्तादध नु दविमाताबन्धनश्चरति वत्स एकः | मित्रस्य ता वरुणस्य वरतानि म... ||
3.55.e: Now lying far away, Child of two Mothers, he wanders unrestrained, the single youngling.  These are the laws of Varuṇa and Mitra. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: दविमाता होता विदथेषु सम्राळ अन्वग्रं चरति कषेति बुध्नः | पर रण्यानि रण्यवाचो भरन्ते म... ||
3.55.e: Child of two Mothers, Priest, sole Lord in synods, he still precedes while resting as foundation.  They who speak sweetly bring him sweet addresses. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: शूरस्येव युध्यतो अन्तमस्य परतीचीनं दद्र्शे विश्वमायत | अन्तर्मतिश्चरति निष्षिधं गोर्म... ||
3.55.e: As to a friendly warrior when he battles, each thing that comes anear is seen to meet him.  The hymn commingles with the cow's oblation. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: नि वेवेति पलितो दूत आस्वन्तर्महांश्चरति रोचनेन | वपूंषि बिभ्रदभि नो वि चष्टे म... ||
3.55.e: Deep within these the hoary envoy pierceth; mighty, he goeth to the realm of splendour,  And looketh on us, clad in wondrous beauty. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: विष्णुर्गोपाः परमं पाति पाथः परिया धामान्यम्र्तादधानः | अग्निष टा विश्वा भुवनानि वेद म... ||
3.55.e: Viṣṇu, the guardian, keeps the loftiest station, upholding dear, immortal dwelling-places.  Agni knows well all these created beings. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: नाना चक्राते यम्या वपूंषि तयोरन्यद रोचते कर्ष्णमन्यत | शयावी च यदरुषी च सवसारौ म... ||
3.55.e: Ye, variant Pair, have made yourselves twin beauties: one of the Twain is dark, bright shines the other;  And yet these two, the dark, the red, are Sisters. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: माता च यत्र दुहिता च धेनू सबर्दुघे धापयेते समीची | रतस्य ते सदसीळे अन्तर्म... ||
3.55.e: Where the two Cows, the Mother and the Daughter, meet and give suck yielding their lordly nectar,  I praise them at the seat of law eternal. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: अन्यस्या वत्सं रिहती मिमाय कया भुवा नि दधे धेनुरूधः | रतस्य सा पयसापिन्वतेळा म... ||
3.55.e: Loud hath she lowed, licking the other's youngling. On what world hath the Milch-cow laid her udder?  This Iḷā streameth with the milk of Order. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: पद्या वस्ते पुरुरूपा वपूंष्यूर्ध्वा तस्थौ तर्यविं रेरिहाणा | रतस्य सद्म वि चरामि विद्वान म... ||
3.55.e: Earth weareth beauties manifold: uplifted, licking her Calf of eighteen months, she standeth.  Well-skilled I seek the seat of law eternal. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: पदे इव निहिते दस्मे अन्तस्तयोरन्यद गुह्यमाविरन्यत | सध्रीचीना पथ्या सा विषूची म... ||
3.55.e: Within a wondrous place the Twain are treasured: the one is manifest, the other hidden.  One common pathway leads in two directions. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: आ धेनवो धुनयन्तामशिश्वीः सबर्दुघाः शशया अप्रदुग्धाः | नव्या-नव्या युवतयो भवन्तीर्म... ||
3.55.e: Let the milch-kine that have no calves storm downward, yielding rich nectar, streaming, unexhausted,  These who are ever new and fresh and youthful. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: यदन्यासु वर्षभो रोरवीति सो अन्यस्मिन यूथे नि दधातिरेतः | स हि कषपावान स भगः स राजा म... ||
3.55.e: What time the Bull bellows in other regions, another herd receives the genial moisture;  For he is Bhaga, King, the earth's Protector. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: वीरस्य नु सवश्व्यं जनासः पर नु वोचाम विदुरस्य देवाः | षोळ्हा युक्ताः पञ्च-पञ्चा वहन्ति म... ||
3.55.e: Let us declare the Hero's wealth in horses, O all ye folk: of this the Gods have knowledge.  Sixfold they bear him, or by fives are harnessed. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: देवस्त्वष्टा सविता विश्वरूपः पुपोष परजाः पुरुधाजजान | इमा च विश्वा भुवनान्यस्य म... ||
3.55.e: Tvaṣṭar the God, the omniform. Creator, begets and feeds mankind in various manner.  His, verily, arc all these living creatures. Great is the Gods’ supreme dominion.

3.55.d: मही समैरच्चम्वा समीची उभे ते अस्य वसुना नय्र्ष्टे | शर्ण्वे वीरो विन्दमानो वसूनि म... ||
3.55.e: The two great meeting Bowls hath he united: each of the Pair is laden with histreasure.  The Hero is renowned for gathering riches. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: इमां च नः पर्थिवीं विश्वधाया उप कषेति हितमित्रो नराजा | पुरःसदः शर्मसदो न वीरा म... ||
3.55.e: Yea, and on this our earth the All-Sustainer dwells like a King with noble friends about him.  In his protection heroes rest in safety. Great is the Cods' supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: निष्षिध्वरीस्त ओषधीरुतापो रयिं त इन्द्र पर्थिवी बिभर्ति | सखायस्ते वामभाजः सयाम म... ||
3.55.e: Rich in their gifts for thee are herbs and waters, and earth brings all her wealth for thee, O Indra.  May we as friends of thine share goodly treasures. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.56.d: न ता मिनन्ति मायिनो न धीरा वरता देवानां परथमा धरुवाणि | न रोदसी अद्रुहा वेद्याभिर्न पर्वता निनमे तस्थिवांसः ||
3.56.e: NOT men of magic skill, not men of wisdom impair the Gods’ first steadfast ordinances.  Ne’er may the earth and heaven which know not malice, nor the fixed hills, be bowed by sage devices.

3.56.d: षड भारानेको अचरन बिभर्त्य रतं वर्षिष्ठमुप गाव आगुः तिस्रो महीरुपरास्तस्थुरत्या गुहा दवे निहितेदर्श्येका ||
3.56.e: One, moving not away, supports six burthens: the Cows proceed to him the true, the Highest.  Near stand three Mighty Ones who travel swiftly: two are concealed from sight, one is apparent.

3.56.d: तरिपाजस्यो वर्षभो विश्वरूप उत तर्युधा पुरुध परजावान | तर्यनीकः पत्यते माहिनावान स रेतोधा वर्षभः शश्वतीनाम ||
3.56.e: The Bull who wears all shapes, the triple-breasted, three-uddered, with a brood in many places,  Ruleth majestic with his triple aspect, the Bull, the Everlasting Ones' impregner.

3.56.d: अभीक आसां पदवीरबोध्यादित्यानामह्वे चारु नाम | आपश्चिदस्मा अरमन्त देवीः पर्थग वरजन्तीः परि षीमव्र्ञ्जन ||
3.56.e: When nigh them, as their tracer he observed them: he called aloud the dear name of Ādityas.  The Goddesses, the Waters, stayed to meet him: they who were wandering separate enclosed him.

3.56.d: तरी षधस्था सिन्धवस्त्रिः कवीनामुत तरिमाता विदथेषु सम्राट | रतावरीर्योषणास्तिस्रो अप्यास्त्रिरा दिवो विदथे पत्यमानाः ||
3.56.e: Streams! the wise Gods have thrice three habitations. Child of three Mothers, he is Lord in synods.  Three are the holy Ladies of the Waters, thrice here from heaven supreme in our assembly.

3.56.d: तरिरा दिवः सवितर्वार्याणि दिवे-दिव आ सुव तरिर्नो अह्नः | तरिधातु राय आ सुवा वसूनि भग तरातर्धिषणे सातये धाः ||
3.56.e: Do thou, O Savitar, from heaven thrice hither, three times a day, send down thy blessings daily.  Send us, O Bhaga, triple wealth and treasure; cause the two worlds to prosper us, Preserver!

3.56.d: तरिरा दिवः सविता सोषवीति राजाना मित्रावरुणा सुपाणी | आपश्चिदस्य रोदसी चिदुर्वी रत्नं भिक्षन्त सवितुः सवाय ||
3.56.e: Savitar thrice from heaven pours down abundance, and the fair-handed Kings Varuṇa, Mitra;  And spacious Heaven and Earth, yea, and the Waters, solicit wealth that Savitar may send us.

3.56.d: तरिरुत्तमा दूणशा रोचनानि तरयो राजन्त्यसुरस्य वीराः | रतावान इषिरा दूळभासस्त्रिरा दिवो विदथे सन्तु देवाः ||
3.56.e: Three are the bright realms, best, beyond attainment, and three, the Asura's Heroes, rule as Sovrans,  Holy and vigorous, never to be injured. Thrice may the Gods from heaven attend our synod.

3.57.d: पर मे विविक्वानविदन मनीषां धेनुं चरन्तीं परयुतामगोपाम | सद्यश्चिद या दुदुहे भूरि धासेरिन्द्रस्तदग्निः पनितारो अस्याः ||
3.57.e: MY thought with fine discernment hath discovered the Cow who wanders free without a herdsman,  Her who hath straightway poured me food in plenty: Indra and Agni therefore are her praisers.

3.57.d: इन्द्रः सु पूषा वर्षणा सुहस्ता दिवो न परीताः शशयं दुदुह्रे | विश्वे यदस्यां रणयन्त देवाः पर वो.अत्र वसवः सुम्नमश्याम ||
3.57.e: Indra and Pūṣan, deft of hand and mighty, well-pleased have drained the heaven's exhaustless udder.  As in this praise the Gods have all delighted, may I win blessing here from you, O Vasus.

3.57.d: या जामयो वर्ष्ण इछन्ति शक्तिं नमस्यन्तीर्जानते गर्भमस्मिन | अछा पुत्रं धेनवो वावशाना महश्चरन्ति बिभ्रतं वपूंषि ||
3.57.e: Fain to lend vigour to the Bull, the siste.. with reverence recognize the germ within him.  The Cows come lowing hither to the Youngling, to him endued with great and wondrous beauties.

3.57.d: अछा विवक्मि रोदसी सुमेके गराव्णो युजानो अध्वरे मनीषा | इमा उ ते मनवे भूरिवारा ऊर्ध्वा भवन्ति दर्शता यजत्राः ||
3.57.e: Fixing with thought, at sacrifice, the press-stones, I bid the well-formed Heaven and Earth come hither;  For these thy flames, which give men boons in plenty, rise up on high, the beautiful, the holy.

3.57.d: या ते जिह्वा मधुमती सुमेधा अग्ने देवेषूच्यत उरूची | तयेह विश्वानवसे यजत्राना सादय पायया चा मधूनि ||
3.57.e: Agni, thy meath-sweet tongue that tastes fair viands, which among Gods is called the far-extended,—  Therewith make all the Holy Odes be seated here for our help, and feed them with sweet juices.

3.57.d: या ते अग्ने पर्वतस्येव धारासश्चन्ती पीपयद देव चित्रा | तामस्मभ्यं परमतिं जातवेदो वसो रास्व सुमतिं विश्वजन्याम ||
3.57.e: Let thy stream give us drink, O God, O Agni, wonderful and exhaustless like the rain-clouds.  Thus care for us, O Vasu Jātavedas, show us thy loving-kindness, reaching all men.

3.58.d: धेनुः परत्नस्य काम्यं दुहानान्तः पुत्रश्चरति दक्षिणायाः | आ दयोतनिं वहति शुभ्रयामोषस सतोमो अश्विनावजीगः ||
3.58.e: THE Ancient's Milch-cow yields the things we long for: the Son of Dakṣiṇā travels between them.  She with the splendid chariot brings refulgence. The praise of Uṣas hath awoke the Aśvins.

3.58.d: सुयुग वहन्ति परति वां रतेनोर्ध्वा भवन्ति पितरेव मेधाः | जरेथामस्मद वि पणेर्महीषां युवोरवश्चक्र्मा यातमर्वाक ||
3.58.e: They bear you hither by well-orderd statute: our sacred offerings rise as if to parents.  Destroy in us the counsel of the niggard come hitherward, for we have shown you favour.

3.58.d: सुयुग्भिरश्वैः सुव्र्ता रथेन दस्राविमं शर्णुतं शलोकमद्रेः | किमङग वां परत्यवर्तिं गमिष्ठाहुर्विप्रासो अश्विना पुराजाः ||
3.58.e: With lightly-rolling car and well-yoked horses hear this, the press-stone's song, ye Wonder-Workers.  Have not the sages of old time, ye Aśvins, called you most prompt to come and stay misfortune?

3.58.d: आ मन्येथामा गतं कच्चिदेवैर्विश्वे जनासो अश्विना हवन्ते | इमा हि वां गोर्जीका मधूनि पर मित्रासो न ददुरुस्रो अग्रे ||
3.58.e: Remember us, and come to us, for ever men, as their wont is, invocate the Aśvins.  Friends as it were have offered you these juices, sweet, blent with milk at the first break of morning.

3.58.d: तिरः पुरू चिदश्विना रजांस्याङगूषो वां मघवाना जनेषु | एह यातं पथिभिर्देवयानैर्दस्राविमे वां निधयो मधूनाम ||
3.58.e: Even through many regions, O ye Aśvins high praise is yours among mankind, ye Mighty-  Come, helpers, on the paths which Gods have travelled: here your libations of sweet meath are ready.

3.58.d: पुराणमोकः सख्यं शिवं वां युवोर्नरा दरविणं जह्नाव्याम | पुनः कर्ण्वानाः सख्या शिवानि मध्वा मदेमसह नू समानाः ||
3.58.e: Ancient your home, auspicious is your friendship: Heroes, your wealth is with the house of Jahnu.  Forming again with you auspicious friendship, let us rejoice with draughts of meath together.

3.58.d: अश्विना वायुना युवं सुदक्षा नियुद्भिष च सजोषसा युवाना | नासत्या तिरोह्न्यं जुषाणा सोमं पिबतमस्रिधा सुदानू ||
3.58.e: O Aśvins, Very Mighty ones, with Vāyu and with his steeds, one-minded, ever-youthful,  Nāsatyas, joying in the third day's Soma, drink it, not hostile, Very Bounteous Givers.

3.58.d: अश्विना परि वामिषः पुरूचीरीयुर्गीर्भिर्यतमाना अम्र्ध्राः | रथो ह वां रतजा अद्रिजूतः परि दयावाप्र्थिवी याति सद्यः ||
3.58.e: Aśvins, to you are brought abundant viands in rivalry with sacred songs, unceasing.  Sprung from high Law your car, urged on by press-stones, goes round the earth and heaven in one brief moment.

3.58.d: अश्विना मधुषुत्तमो युवाकुः सोमस्तं पातमा गतं दुरोणे | रथो ह वां भूरि वर्पः करिक्रत सुतावतो निष्क्र्तमागमिष्ठः ||
3.58.e: Aśvins, your Soma sheds delicious sweetness: drink ye thereof and come unto our dwelling.  Your car, assuming many a shape, most often goes to the Soma-presser's place of meeting.

3.59.d: मित्रो जनान यातयति बरुवाणो मित्रो दाधार पर्थिवीमुत दयाम | मित्रः कर्ष्टीरनिमिषाभि चष्टे मित्राय हव्यंघ्र्तवज्जुहोत ||
3.59.e: MITRA, when speaking, stirreth men to labour: Mitra sustaineth both the earth and heaven.  Mitra beholdeth men with eyes that close not. To Mitra bring, with holy oil, oblation.

3.59.d: पर स मित्र मर्तो अस्तु परयस्वान यस्त आदित्य शिक्षति वरतेन | न हन्यते न जीयते तवोतो नैनमंहो अश्नोत्यन्तितो न दूरात ||
3.59.e: Foremost be he who brings thee food, O Mitra, who strives to keep thy sacred Law, Āditya.  He whom thou helpest ne’er is slain or conquered, on him, from near or far, falls no affliction.

3.59.d: अनमीवास इळया मदन्तो मितज्ञवो वरिमन्ना पर्थिव्याः | आदित्यस्य वरतमुपक्षियन्तो वयं मित्रस्य सुमतौ सयाम ||
3.59.e: joying in sacred food and free from sickness, with knees bent lowly on the earth's broad surface,  Following closely the Āditya's statute, may we remain in Mitra's gracious favour.

3.59.d: अयं मित्रो नमस्यः सुशेवो राजा सुक्षत्रो अजनिष्ट वेधाः | तस्य वयं ... ||
3.59.e: Auspicious and adorable, this Mitra was born with fair dominion, King, Disposer.  May we enjoy the grace of him the Holy, yea, rest in his propitious loving-kindness.

3.59.d: महानादित्यो नमसोपसद्यो यातयज्जनो गर्णते सुशेवः | तस्मा एतत पन्यतमाय जुष्टमग्नौ मित्राय हविरा जुहोत ||
3.59.e: The great Āditya, to be served with wor. ship, who stirreth men, is gracious to the singer.  To Mitra, him most highly to be lauded, offer in fire oblation that he loveth.

3.59.d: मित्रस्य चर्षणीध्र्तो.अवो देवस्य सानसि | दयुम्नं चित्रश्रवस्तमम ||
3.59.e: The gainful grace of Mitra,. God, supporter of the race of man,  Gives splendour of most.glorious fame.

3.59.d: अभि यो महिना दिवं मित्रो बभूव सप्रथाः | अभि शरवोभिः पर्थिवीम ||
3.59.e: Mitra whose glory spreads afar, he who in might surpasses heaven,  Surpasses earth in his renown.

3.59.d: मित्राय पञ्च येमिरे जना अभिष्टिशवसे | स देवान विश्वान बिभर्ति ||
3.59.e: All the Five Races have repaired to Mitra, ever strong to aid,  For he sustaineth all the Gods.

3.59.d: मित्रो देवेष्वायुषु जनाय वर्क्तबर्हिषे | इष इष्टव्रताकः ||
3.59.e: Mitra to Gods, to living men, to him who strews the holy grass,  Gives food fulfilling sacred Law.

3.60.d: इहेह वो मनसा बन्धुता नर उशिजो जग्मुरभि तानि वेदसा | याभिर्मायाभिः परतिजूतिवर्पसः सौधन्वना यज्ञियं भागमानश ||
3.60.e: HERE is your ghostly kinship, here, O Men: they came desirous to these holy rites with store of wealth,  With wondrous arts, whereby, with schemes to meet each need, Ye gained, Sudhanvan's Sons! your share in sacrifice.

3.60.d: याभिः शचीभिश्चमसानपिंशत यया धिया गामरिणीत चर्मणः | येन हरी मनसा निरतक्षत तेन देवत्वं रभवः समानश ||
3.60.e: The mighty powers wherewith. ye formed the chalices, the thought by which ye drew the cow from out the hide,  The intellect wherewith ye wrought the two Bay Steeds,—through these, O Ṛbhus, ye attained divinity.

3.60.d: इन्द्रस्य सख्यं रभवः समानशुर्मनोर्नपातो अपसो दधन्विरे | सौधन्वनासो अम्र्तत्वमेरिरे विष्ट्वी शमीभिः सुक्र्तः सुक्र्त्यया ||
3.60.e: Friendship with Indra have the Ṛbhus, fully gained: grandsons of Manu, they skilfully urged the work.  Sudhanvan's Children won them everlasting life, serving with holy rites, pious with noble acts.  4:In company with Indra come ye to the juice, then gloriously shall your wishes be fulfilled.  Not to be paragoned, ye Priests, are your good deeds, nor your heroic acts, Ṛbhus, Sudhanvan's Sons.

3.60.d: इन्द्रेण याथ सरथं सुते सचानथो वशानां भवथासह शरिया | न वः परतिमै सुक्र्तानि वाघतः सौधन्वना रभवो वीर्याणि च ||
3.60.e: O Indra, with the Ṛbhus, Mighty Ones, pour down the Soma juice effused, well-blent, from both thy hands.  Maghalan, urged by song, in the drink-offerer's house rejoice thee with the Heroes, with Sudhanvan's Sons.

3.60.d: इन्द्र रभुभिर्वाजवद्भिः समुक्षितं सुतं सोममा वर्षस्वा गभस्त्योः | धियेषितो मघवन दाशुषो गर्हे सौधन्वनेभिः सह मत्स्वा नर्भिः ||
3.60.e: With Ṛbhu near, and Vāja, Indra, here exult, with Saci, praised of many, in the juice we pour.  These homes wherein we dwell have turned themselves to thee, -devotions to the Gods, as laws of men ordain.

3.60.d: इन्द्र रभुमान वाजवान मत्स्वेह नो.अस्मिन सवने शच्या पुरुष्टुत | इमानि तुभ्यं सवसराणि येमिरे वरता देवानां मनुषश्च धर्मभिः ||
3.60.e: Come with the mighty Ṛbhus, Indra, come to us, strengthening with thy help the singer's holy praise;  At hundred eager calls come to the living man, with thousand arts attend the act of sacrifice.

3.60.d: इन्द्र रभुभिर्वाजिभिर्वाजयन्निह सतोमं जरितुरुप याहि यज्ञियम | शतं केतेभिरिषिरेभिरायवे सहस्रणीथोध्वरस्य होमनि ||

3.61.d: उषो वाजेन वाजिनि परचेता सतोमं जुषस्व गर्णतो मघोनि | पुराणी देवि युवतिः पुरन्धिरनु वरतं चरसि विश्ववारे ||
3.61.e: O Uṣas, strong with strength, endowed witli knowledge, accept the singer's praise, O wealthy Lady.  Thou, Goddess, ancient, young, and full of wisdom, movest, all-bounteous! as the Law ordaineth.

3.61.d: उषो देव्यमर्त्या वि भाहि चन्द्ररथा सून्र्ता ईरयन्ती | आ तवा वहन्तु सुयमासो अश्वा हिरण्यवर्णां पर्थुपाजसो ये ||
3.61.e: Shine forth, O Morning, thou auspicious Goddess, on thy bright car awaking pleasant voices.  Let docile horses of far-reaching splendour convey thee hitherward, the goldencoloured.

3.61.d: उषः परतीची भुवनानि विश्वोर्ध्वा तिष्ठस्यम्र्तस्य केतुः | समानमर्थं चरणीयमाना चक्रमिव नव्यस्या वव्र्त्स्व ||
3.61.e: Thou, Morning, turning thee to every creature, standest on high as ensign of the Immortal,  To one same goal ever and ever wending now, like a wheel, O newly-born, roll hi ther.

3.61.d: अव सयूमेव चिन्वती मघोन्युषा याति सवसरस्य पत्नी | सवर्जनन्ती सुभगा सुदंसा आन्ताद दिवः पप्रथ आ पर्थिव्याः ||
3.61.e: Letting her reins drop downward, Morning cometh, the wealthy Dame, the Lady of the dwelling;  Bringing forth light, the Wonderful, the Blessed hath spread her from the bounds of earth and heaven.

3.61.d: अछा वो देवीमुषसं विभातीं पर वो भरध्वं नमसा सुव्र्क्तिम | ऊर्ध्वं मधुधा दिवि पाजो अश्रेत पर रोचना रुरुचे रण्वसन्द्र्क ||
3.61.e: Hither invoke the radiant Goddess Morning, and bring with reverence your hymn to praise her.  She, dropping sweets, hath set in heaven her brightness, and, fair to look on, hath beamed forth her splendour.

3.61.d: रतावरी दिवो अर्कैरबोध्या रेवती रोदसी चित्रमस्थात | आयतीमग्न उषसं विभातीं वाममेषि दरविणं भिक्षमाणः ||
3.61.e: From heaven, with hymns, the Holy One was wakened: brightly to both worlds came the wealthy Lady.  To Morning, Agni, when she comes refulgent, thou goest forth soliciting fair riches.

3.61.d: रतस्य बुध्न उषसामिषण्यन वर्षा मही रोदसी आ विवेश | मही मित्रस्य वरुणस्य माया चन्द्रेव भानुं वि दधे पुरुत्रा ||
3.61.e: On Law's firm base the speeder of the Mornings, the Bull, hath entered mighty earth and heaven.  Great is the power of Varuṇa and Mitra, which, bright, hath spread in every place its splendour.

3.62.d: इमा उ वां भर्मयो मन्यमाना युवावते न तुज्या अभूवन | कव तयदिन्द्रावरुणा यशो वां येन समा सिनं भरथः सखिभ्यः ||
3.62.e: YOUR well-known prompt activities aforetime needed no impulse from your faithful servant.  Where, Indra-Varuṇa, is now that glory wherewith ye brought support to those who loved you?

3.62.d: अयमु वां पुरुतमो रयीयञ्छश्वत्तममवसे जोहवीति | सजोषाविन्द्रावरुणा मरुद्भिर्दिवा पर्थिव्या शर्णुतं हवम्मे ||
3.62.e: This man, most diligent, seeking after riches, incessantly invokes you for your favour.  Accordant, Indra-Varuṇa, with Maruts, with Heaven and Earth, hear ye mine invocation.

3.62.d: अस्मे तदिन्द्रावरुणा वसु षयादस्मे रयिर्मरुतः सर्ववीरः | अस्मान वरूत्रीः शरणैरवन्त्वस्मान होत्रा भारती दक्षिणाभिः ||
3.62.e: O Indra-Varuṇa, ours be this treasure ours be wealth, Maruts, with full store of heroes.  May the Varūtrīs with their shelter aid us, and Bhāratī and Hotrā with the Mornings.

3.62.d: बर्हस्पते जुषस्व नो हव्यानि विश्वदेव्य | रास्व रत्नानि दाशुषे ||
3.62.e: Be pleased! with our oblations, thou loved of all Gods, Bṛhaspati:  Give wealth to him who brings thee gifts.
At sacrifices, with your hymns worship the pure Bṛhaspati—  I pray for power which none may bend—
The Bull of men, whom none deceive, the wearer of each shape at will,  Bṛhaspati Most Excellent.

3.62.d: इयं ते पूषन्नाघ्र्णे सुष्टुतिर्देव नव्यसी | अस्माभिस्तुभ्यं शस्यते ||
3.62.e: Divine, resplendent Pūṣan, this our newest hymn of eulogy,  By us is chanted forth to thee.

3.62.d: तां जुषस्व गिरं मम वाजयन्तीमवा धियम | वधूयुरिव योषणाम ||
3.62.e: Accept with favour this my song, be gracious to the earnest thought,  Even as a bridegroom to his bride.

3.62.d: यो विश्वाभि विपश्यति भुवना सं च पश्यति | स नः पूषाविता भुवत ||
3.62.e: May he who sees all living things, see, them together at a glance,—  May he, may Pūṣan be our help.

3.62.d: तत सवितुर्वरेण्यं भर्गो देवस्य धीमहि | धियो यो नः परचोदयात ||
3.62.e: May we attain that excellent glory of Savitar the God:  So May he stimulate our prayers.

3.62.d: देवस्य सवितुर्वयं वाजयन्तः पुरन्ध्या | भगस्य रातिमीमहे ||
3.62.e: With understanding, earnestly, of Savitar the God we crave  Our portion of prosperity.

3.62.d: देवं नरः सवितारं विप्रा यज्ञैः सुव्र्क्तिभिः | नमस्यन्ति धियेषिताः ||
3.62.e: Men, singers worship Savitar the God with hymn and holy rites,  Urged by the impulse of their thoughts.

3.62.d: सोमो जिगाति गातुविद देवानामेति निष्क्र्तम | रतस्य योनिमासदम ||
3.62.e: Soma who gives success goes forth, goes to the gathering place of Gods,  To seat him at the seat of Law.

3.62.d: सोमो अस्मभ्यं दविपदे चतुष्पदे च पशवे | अनमीवा इषस करत ||
3.62.e: To us and to our cattle may Soma give salutary food,  To biped and to quadruped.
May Soma, strengthening our power of life, and conquering our foes,  In our assembly take his seat.

3.62.d: आ नो मित्रावरुणा घर्तैर्गव्यूतिमुक्षतम | मध्वा रजांसि सुक्रतू ||
3.62.e: May Mitra-Varuṇa, sapient Pair, bedew our pasturage with oil,  With meatb the regions of the air.

3.62.d: उरुशंसा नमोव्र्धा मह्ना दक्षस्य राजथः | दराघिष्ठाभिः शुचिव्रता ||
3.62.e: Far-ruling, joyful when adored, ye reign through majesty of might,  With pure laws everlastingly.

3.62.d: गर्णाना जमदग्निना योनाव रतस्य सीदतम | पातं सोमं रताव्र्धा ||
3.62.e: Lauded by Jamadagni's song, sit in the place of holy Law:

4.1.d: तवां हय अग्ने सदम इत समन्यवो देवासो देवम अरतिं नयेरिर इति करत्वा नयेरिरे | अमर्त्यं यजत मर्त्येष्व आ देवम आदेवं जनत परचेतसं विश्वम आदेवं जनत परचेतसम ||
4.1.e: 1, THEE Agni, have the Gods, ever of one accord, sent hither down, a God, appointed messenger, yea, with their wisdom sent thee down.  The Immortal, O thou Holy One, mid mortal men, the God-devoted God, the wise, have they brought forth, brought forth the omnipresent God-devoted Sage.

4.1.d: स भरातरं वरुणम अग्न आ वव्र्त्स्व देवां अछा सुमती यज्ञवनसं जयेष्ठं यज्ञवनसम | रतावानम आदित्यं चर्षणीध्र्तं राजानं चर्षणीध्र्तम ||
4.1.e: As such, O Agni, bring with favour to the Gods thy Brother Varuṇa who loveth sacrifice,  True to the Law, the Āditya who supporteth men, the King, supporter of mankind.

4.1.d: सखे सखायम अभ्य आ वव्र्त्स्वाशुं न चक्रं रथ्येव रंह्यास्मभ्यं दस्म रंह्या | अग्ने मर्ळीकं वरुणे सचा विदो मरुत्सु विश्वभानुषु तोकाय तुजे शुशुचान शं कर्ध्य अस्मभ्यं दस्म शं कर्धि ||
4.1.e: Do thou, O Friend, turn hither him who is our Friend, swift as a wheel, like two car-steeds in rapid course, Wondrous! to us in rapid course.  O Agni, find thou grace for us with Varuṇa, with Maruts who illumine all.  Bless us, thou Radiant One, for seed and progeny, yea, bless us, O thou Wondrous God.

4.1.d: तवं नो अग्ने वरुणस्य विद्वान देवस्य हेळो ऽव यासिसीष्ठाः | यजिष्ठो वह्नितमः शोशुचानो विश्वा दवेषांसि पर मुमुग्ध्य अस्मत ||
4.1.e: Do thou who knowest Varuṇa, O Agni, put far away from us the God's displeasure.  Best Sacrificer, brightest One, refulgent remove thou far from us all those who hate us.

4.1.d: स तवं नो अग्ने ऽवमो भवोती नेदिष्ठो अस्या उषसो वयुष्टौ | अव यक्ष्व नो वरुणं रराणो वीहि मर्ळीकं सुहवो न एधि ||
4.1.e: Be thou, O Agni, nearest us with succour, our closest Friend while now this Morn is breaking.  Reconcile to us Varuṇa, be bounteous enjoy the gracious juice; be swift to hear us.

4.1.d: अस्य शरेष्ठा सुभगस्य संद्र्ग देवस्य चित्रतमा मर्त्येषु | शुचि घर्तं न तप्तम अघ्न्याया सपार्हा देवस्य मंहनेव धेनोः ||
4.1.e: Excellent is the glance, of brightest splendour, which the auspicious God bestows on mortals-  The God's glance, longed-for even as the butter, pure, heated, of the cow, the milch-cow's bounty.

4.1.d: तरिर अस्य ता परमा सन्ति सत्या सपार्हा देवस्य जनिमान्य अग्नेः | अनन्ते अन्तः परिवीत आगाच छुचिः शुक्रो अर्यो रोरुचानः ||
4.1.e: Three are those births, the true, the most exalted, eagerly longed-for, of the God, of Agni.  He came invested in the boundless region, pure, radiant, friendly, mightily resplendent.

4.1.d: स दूतो विश्वेद अभि वष्टि सद्मा होता हिरण्यरथो रंसुजिह्वः रोहिदश्वो वपुष्यो विभावा सदा रण्वः पितुमतीव संसत ||
4.1.e: This envoy joyeth in all seats of worship, borne on his golden car, sweet-tongued Invoker:  Lovely to look on, with red steeds, effulgent, like a feast rich in food, joyous for ever.

4.1.d: स चेतयन मनुषो यज्ञबन्धुः पर तम मह्या रशनया नयन्ति स कषेत्य अस्य दुर्यासु साधन देवो मर्तस्य सधनित्वम आप ||
4.1.e: Allied by worship, let him give man knowledge: by an extended cord they lead him onward.  He stays, effectual in this mortal's dwelling, and the God wins a share in his possessions.

4.1.d: स तू नो अग्निर नयतु परजानन्न अछा रत्नं देवभक्तं यद अस्य | धिया यद विश्वे अम्र्ता अक्र्ण्वन दयौष पिता जनिता सत्यम उक्षन ||
4.1.e: Let Agni -for he knows the way- conduct us to all that he enjoys of God-sent riches,  What all the Immortals have prepared with wisdom, Dyaus, Sire, Begetter, raining down true blessings.

4.1.d: स जायत परथमः पस्त्यासु महो बुध्ने रजसो अस्य योनौ | पर शर्ध आर्त परथमं विपन्यं रतस्य योना वर्षभस्य नीळे | सपार्हो युवा वपुष्यो विभावा सप्त परियासो ऽजनयन्त वर्ष्णे ||
4.1.e: In houses first he sprang into existence, at great heaven's base, and in this region's bosom;  Footless and headless, both his ends concealing, in his Bull's lair drawing himself together.

4.1.d: अस्माकम अत्र पितरो मनुष्या अभि पर सेदुर रतम आशुषाणाः | अश्मव्रजाः सुदुघा वव्रे अन्तर उद उस्रा आजन्न उषसो हुवानाः ||
4.1.e: Wondrously first he rose aloft, defiant, in the Bull's lair, the homeof holy Order,  Longed-for, young, beautiful, and far-resplendent: and sevendear frieuds sprang up unto the Mighty.

4.1.d: ते मर्म्र्जत दद्र्वांसो अद्रिं तद एषाम अन्ये अभितो वि वोचन | पश्वयन्त्रासो अभि कारम अर्चन विदन्त जयोतिश चक्र्पन्त धीभिः ||
4.1.e: Here did our human fathers take their places, fain to fulfil the sacred Law of worship.  Forth drave they, with loud call, Dawn's teeming Milch-kine bid in the mountainstable, in the cavern.

4.1.d: ते गव्यता मनसा दर्ध्रम उब्धं गा येमानम परि षन्तम अद्रिम | दर्ळ्हं नरो वचसा दैव्येन वरजं गोमन्तम उशिजो वि वव्रुः ||
4.1.e: Splendid were they when they had rent the mountain: others, around, shall tell forth this their exploit.  They sang their song, prepared to free the cattle: they found the light; with holy hymns they worshipped.

4.1.d: ते मन्वत परथमं नाम धेनोस तरिः सप्त मातुः परमाणि विन्दन | तज जानतीर अभ्य अनूषत वरा आविर भुवद अरुणीर यशसा गोः ||
4.1.e: Eager, with thought intent upon the booty, the men with their celestial speech threw open,  The solid mountain firm, compact, enclosing, confining Cows, the stable full of cattle.

4.1.d: नेशत तमो दुधितं रोचत दयौर उद देव्या उषसो भानुर अर्त | आ सूर्यो बर्हतस तिष्ठद अज्रां रजु मर्तेषु वर्जिना च पश्यन ||
4.1.e: The Milch-cow's earliest name they comprehended: they found the Mother's thrice-seven noblest titles.  This the bands knew, and sent forth acclamation:with the Bull's sheen the Red One was apparent.

4.1.d: आद इत पश्चा बुबुधाना वय अख्यन्न आद इद रत्नं धारयन्त दयुभक्तम | विश्वे विश्वासु दुर्यासु देवा मित्र धिये वरुण सत्यम अस्तु ||
4.1.e: The turbid darkness fled, the heaven was sp, endid! up rose the bright beam of celestial Morning.  Sūrya ascended to the wide expanses, beholding deeds of men both good and evil.

4.1.d: अछा वोचेय शुशुचानम अग्निं होतारं विश्वभरसं यजिष्ठम | शुच्य ऊधो अत्र्णन न गवाम अन्धो न पूतम परिषिक्तम अंशोः ||
4.1.e: Then, afterwards they looked around, awakened, when first they held that Heaven allotted treasure.  Now all the Gods abide in all their dwellings. Varuṇa, Mitra, be the prayer effective.

4.1.d: विश्वेषाम अदितिर यज्ञियानां विश्वेषाम अतिथिर मानुषाणाम | अग्निर देवानाम अव आव्र्णानः सुम्र्ळीको भवतु जातवेदाः ||
4.1.e: I will call hither brightly-beaming Agni, the Herald, all-supporting, best at worship.  He hath disclosed, like the milch cows' pure udder, the Sorria's juice when cleansed and poured from beakers.

4.2.d: यो मर्त्येष्व अम्र्त रतावा देवो देवेष्व अरतिर निधायि | होता यजिष्ठो मह्ना शुचध्यै हव्यैर अग्निर मनुष ईरयध्यै ||
4.2.e: THE, Faithful One, Immortal among mortals, a God among the Gods, appointed envoy,  Priest, best at worship, must shine forth in glory . Agni shall be raised high with man's oblations.

4.2.d: इह तवं सूनो सहसो नो अद्य जातो जातां उभयां अन्तर अग्ने | दूत ईयसे युयुजान रष्व रजुमुष्कान वर्षणः शुक्रांश च ||
4.2.e: Born for us here this day, O Son of Vigour, between both races of born beings, Agni,  Thou farest as an envoy, having harnessed, Sublime One! thy strong-muscled radiant stallions.

4.2.d: अत्या वर्धस्नू रोहिता घर्तस्नू रतस्य मन्ये मनसा जविष्ठा | अन्तर ईयसे अरुषा युजानो युष्मांश च देवान विश आ च मर्तान ||
4.2.e: I laud the ruddy steeds who pour down blessing, dropping oil, flectest through the thoualit of Order.  Yoking red horses to and fro thou goest between you Deities and mortal races.

4.2.d: अर्यमणं वरुणम मित्रम एषाम इन्द्राविष्णू मरुतो अश्विनोत | सवश्वो अग्ने सुरथः सुराधा एद उ वह सुहविषे जनाय ||
4.2.e: Aryaman, Mitra, Varuṇa, and Indra with Viṣṇu, of the Gods, Maruts and Aśvins-  These, Agni, with good car and steeds, bring hither, most bountiful, to folk with fair oblations.

4.2.d: गोमां अग्ने ऽविमां अश्वी यज्ञो नर्वत्सखा सदम इद अप्रम्र्ष्यः | इळावां एषो असुर परजावान दीर्घो रयिः पर्थुबुध्नः सभावान ||
4.2.e: Agni, be this our sacrifice eternal, with brave friends, rich in kine and sheep and horses,  Rich, Asura! in sacred food and children, in full assembly, wealth broad-based and during.

4.2.d: यस त इध्मं जभरत सिष्विदानो मूर्धानं वा ततपते तवाया | भुवस तस्य सवतवांः पायुर अग्ने विश्वस्मात सीम अघायत उरुष्य ||
4.2.e: The man who, sweating, brings for thee the fuel, and makes his head to ache, thy faithful servant,—  Agni, to him be a self-strong Protector guard him from all who seek to do him mischief.

4.2.d: यस ते भराद अन्नियते चिद अन्नं निशिषन मन्द्रम अतिथिम उदीरत | आ देवयुर इनधते दुरोणे तस्मिन रयिर धरुवो अस्तु दास्वान ||
4.2.e: Who brings thee food, though thou hast food in plenty, welcomes his cheerful guest and speeds him onward,  Who kindles thee devoutly in his dwelling,to him be wealth secure and freely giving.

4.2.d: यस तवा दोषा य उषसि परशंसात परियं वा तवा कर्णवते हविष्मान | अश्वो न सवे दम आ हेम्यावान तम अंहसः पीपरो दाश्वांसम ||
4.2.e: Whoso sings praise to thee at eve or morning, and, with oblation, doth the thing thou lovest,—  In his own home, even as a goId-girt courser, rescue him from distress, the bounteous giver.

4.2.d: यस तुभ्यम अग्ने अम्र्ताय दाशद दुवस तवे कर्णवते यतस्रुक | न स राया शशमानो वि योषन नैनम अंहः परि वरद अघायोः ||
4.2.e: Whoso brings gifts to thee Immortal, Agni, and doth thee service with uplifted ladle,—  Let him not, sorely toiling, lose his riches; let not the sinner's wickedness enclose him.

4.2.d: यस्य तवम अग्ने अध्वरं जुजोषो देवो मर्तस्य सुधितं रराणः | परीतेद असद धोत्रा सा यविष्ठासाम यस्य विधतो वर्धासः ||
4.2.e: Whose well-wrought worship thou acceptest, Agni, thou God a mortal's gift, thou liberal Giver,—  Dear be his sacrifice to thee, Most Youthful! and may we strengthen him when he adores thee.

4.2.d: चित्तिम अचित्तिं चिनवद वि विद्वान पर्ष्ठेव वीता वर्जिना च मर्तान | राये च नः सवपत्याय देव दितिं च रास्वादितिम उरुष्य ||
4.2.e: May he who knows distinguish sense and folly of men, like straight and crooked backs of horses.  Lead us, O God, to wealth and noble offspring: keep penury afar and grant us plenty.

4.2.d: कविं शशासुः कवयो ऽदब्धा निधारयन्तो दुर्यास्व आयोः | अतस तवं दर्श्यां अग्न एतान पड्भिः पश्येर अद्भुतां अर्य एवैः ||
4.2.e: This Sage the Sages, ne’er deceived, commanded, setting him down in dwellings of the living.  Hence mayst thou, friendly God, with rapid footsteps behold the Gods, wonderful, fair to look on.

4.2.d: तवम अग्ने वाघते सुप्रणीतिः सुतसोमाय विधते यविष्ठ | रत्नम भर शशमानाय घर्ष्वे पर्थु शचन्द्रम अवसे चर्षणिप्राः ||
4.2.e: Good guidance hast thou for the priest, O Agni, who, Youngest God! with outpoured Soma serves thee.  Ruler of men, thou joyous God, bring treasure splendid and plentiful to aid the toiler.

4.2.d: अधा ह यद वयम अग्ने तवाया पड्भिर हस्तेभिश चक्र्मा तनूभिः | रथं न करन्तो अपसा भुरिजोर रतं येमुः सुध्य आशुषाणाः ||
4.2.e: Now all that we, thy faithful servants, Agni, have done with feet, with hands, and with our bodies,  The wise, with toil, the holy rite have guided, as those who frame a car with manual cunning.

4.2.d: अधा मातुर उषसः सप्त विप्रा जायेमहि परथमा वेधसो नॄन | दिवस पुत्रा अङगिरसो भवेमाद्रिं रुजेम धनिनं शुचन्तः ||
4.2.e: May we, seven sages first in rank, engender, from Dawn the Mother, men to be ordainers.  May we, Aṅgirases, be sons of Heaven, and, radiant, burst the wealth-containing mountain.

4.2.d: अधा यथा नः पितरः परासः परत्नासो अग्न रतम आशुषाणाः | शुचीद अयन दीधितिम उक्थशासः कषामा भिन्दन्तो अरुणीर अप वरन ||
4.2.e: As in the days of old our ancient Fathers, speeding the work of holy worship, Agni,  Sought pure light and devotion, singing praises; they cleft the ground and made red Dawns apparent.

4.2.d: सुकर्माणः सुरुचो देवयन्तो ऽयो न देवा जनिमा धमन्तः | शुचन्तो अग्निं वव्र्धन्त इन्द्रम ऊर्वं गव्यम परिषदन्तो अग्मन ||
4.2.e: Gods, doing holy acts, devout, resplendent, smelting like ore their human generations.  Enkindling Agni and exalting Indra, they came encompassing the stall of cattle.

4.2.d: आ यूथेव कषुमति पश्वो अख्यद देवानां यज जनिमान्त्य उग्र | मर्तानां चिद उर्वशीर अक्र्प्रन वर्धे चिद अर्य उपरस्यायोः ||
4.2.e: Strong One! he marked them-and the Gods before them-like herds of cattle in a foodful pasture.  There they moaned forth their strong desire for mortals, to aid the True, the nearest One, the Living.

4.2.d: अकर्म ते सवपसो अभूम रतम अवस्रन्न उषसो विभातीः | अनूनम अग्निम पुरुधा सुश्चन्द्रं देवस्य मर्म्र्जतश चारु चक्षुः ||
4.2.e: We have worked for thee, we have laboured nobly-bright Dawns have shed their light upon our worship-  Adding a beauty to the perfect Agni, and the God's beauteous eye that shines for ever.

4.2.d: एता ते अग्न उचथानि वेधो ऽवोचाम कवये ता जुषस्व | उच छोचस्व कर्णुहि वस्यसो नो महो रायः पुरुवार पर यन्धि ||
4.2.e: Agni, Disposer, we have sung these praises to thee the Wise: do thou accept them gladly.  Blaze up on high and ever make us richer. Give us great wealth, O thou whose boons are many.

4.3.d: आ वो राजानम अध्वरस्य रुद्रं होतारं सत्ययजं रोदस्योः | अग्निम पुरा तनयित्नोर अचित्ताद धिरण्यरूपम अवसे कर्णुध्वम ||
4.3.e: WIN, to assist you, Rudra, Lord of worship, Priest of both worlds, effectual  Sacrificer,  Agni, invested with his golden colours, before the thunder strike and lay you senseless.

4.3.d: अयं योनिश चक्र्मा यं वयं ते जायेव पत्य उशती सुवासाः | अर्वाचीनः परिवीतो नि षीदेमा उ ते सवपाक परतीचीः ||
4.3.e: This shrine have we made ready for thy coming, as the fond dame attires her for her husband.  Performer of good work, sit down before us, invested while these flames incline to meet thee.

4.3.d: आश्र्ण्वते अद्र्पिताय मन्म नर्चक्षसे सुम्र्ळीकाय वेधः | देवाय शस्तिम अम्र्ताय शंस गरावेव सोता मधुषुद यम ईळे ||
4.3.e: A hymn, O Priest, to him who hears, the gentle, to him who looks on men, exceeding gracious,  A song of praise sing to the God Immortal, whom the stone, presser of the sweet juice, worships.

4.3.d: तवं चिन नः शम्या अग्ने अस्या रतस्य बोध्य रतचित सवाधीः | कदा त उक्था सधमाद्यानि कदा भवन्ति सख्या गर्हे ते ||
4.3.e: Even as true knower of the Law, O Agni, to this our solemn rite he thou attentive.  When shall thy songs of festival be sung thee? When is thy friendship shown within our dwelling?

4.3.d: कथा ह तद वरुणाय तवम अग्ने कथा दिवे गर्हसे कन न आगः | कथा मित्राय मीळ्हुषे पर्थिव्यै बरवः कद अर्यम्णे कद भगाय ||
4.3.e: Why this complaint to Varuṇa, O Agni? And why to Heaven? for what is our transgression?  How wilt thou speak to Earth and bounteous Mitra? What wilt thou say to Aryaman and Bhaga?

4.3.d: कद धिष्ण्यासु वर्धसानो अग्ने कद वाताय परतवसे शुभंये | परिज्मने नासत्याय कषे बरवः कद अग्ने रुद्राय नर्घ्ने ||
4.3.e: What, when thou blazest on the lesser altars, what to the mighty Wind who comes to bless us,  True, circumambient? what to Earth, O Agni, what wilt thou say to man-destroying Rudra?

4.3.d: कथा महे पुष्टिम्भराय पूष्णे कद रुद्राय सुमखाय हविर्दे | कद विष्णव उरुगायाय रेतो बरवः कद अग्ने शरवे बर्हत्यै ||
4.3.e: How to great Pūṣan who promotes our welfare,—to honoured Rudra what, who gives oblations?  What sin of ours to the far-striding Viṣṇu, what, Agni, wilt thou tell the Lofty Arrow.

4.3.d: कथा शर्धाय मरुताम रताय कथा सूरे बर्हते पर्छ्यमानः | परति बरवो ऽदितये तुराय साधा दिवो जातवेदश चिकित्वान ||
4.3.e: What wilt thou tell the truthful band of Maruts, how answer the great Sun when thou art questioned?  Before the Free, before the Swift, defend us: fulfil heaven's work, all-knowing Jātavedas.

4.3.d: रतेन रतं नियतम ईळ आ गोर आमा सचा मधुमत पक्वम अग्ने | कर्ष्णा सती रुशता धासिनैषा जामर्येण पयसा पीपाय ||
4.3.e: I crave the cow's true gift arranged by Order: though raw, she hath the sweet ripe juice, O Agni.  Though she is black of hue with milk she teemeth, nutritious, brightly shining, all-sustaining.

4.3.d: रतेन हि षमा वर्षभश चिद अक्तः पुमां अग्निः पयसा पर्ष्ठ्य्न | अस्पन्दमानो अचरद वयोधा वर्षा शुक्रं दुदुहे पर्श्निर ऊधः ||
4.3.e: Agni the Bull, the manly, hath been sprinkled with oil upon his back, by Law eternal.  He who gives vital power goes on unswerving. Pṛśni the Bull hath milked the pure wiiite udder.

4.3.d: रतेनाद्रिं वय असन भिदन्तः सम अङगिरसो नवन्त गोभिः | शुनं नरः परि षदन्न उषासम आविः सवर अभवज जाते अग्नौ ||
4.3.e: By Law the Aṅgirases cleft the rock asunder, and sang their hymns together with the cattle.  Bringing great bliss the men encompassed Morning: light was apparent at the birth of Agni.

4.3.d: रतेन देवीर अम्र्ता अम्र्क्ता अर्णोभिर आपो मधुमद्भिर अग्ने | वाजी न सर्गेषु परस्तुभानः पर सदम इत सरवितवे दधन्युः ||
4.3.e: By Law the Immortal Goddesses the Waters, with meath-rich waves, O Agni, and uninjured,  Like a strong courser lauded in his running, sped to flow onward swiftly and for ever.

4.3.d: मा कस्य यक्षं सदम इद धुरो गा मा वेशस्य परमिनतो मापेः | मा भरातुर अग्ने अन्र्जोर रणं वेर मा सख्युर दक्षं रिपोर भुजेम ||
4.3.e: Go never to the feast of one who harms us, the treacherous neighbour or unworthy kinsman.  Punish us not for a false brother's trespass. Let us not feel the might of friend or foeman.

4.3.d: रक्षा णो अग्ने तव रक्षणेभी रारक्षाणः सुमख परीणानः | परति षफुर वि रुज वीड्व अंहो जहि रक्षो महि चिद वाव्र्धानम ||
4.3.e: O Agni, keep us safe with thy protection, loving us, honoured God! and ever guarding.  Beat thou away,  destroy  severe affliction slay e’en the demon when he waxes mighty.

4.3.d: एभिर भव सुमना अग्ने अर्कैर इमान सप्र्श मन्मभिः शूर वाजान | उत बरह्माण्य अङगिरो जुषस्व सं ते शस्तिर देववाता जरेत ||
4.3.e: Through these our songs of praise be gracious, Agni; moved by our prayers, O Hero, touch our viands.  Accept, O Aṅgiras, these our devotions, and let the praise which Gods desire address thee.

4.3.d: एता विश्वा विदुषे तुभ्यं वेधो नीथान्य अग्ने निण्या वचांसि | निवचना कवये काव्यान्य अशंसिषम मतिभिर विप्र उक्थैः ||
4.3.e: To thee who knowest, Agni, thou Disposer, all these wise secret speeches have I uttered,  Sung to thee, Sage, the charming words of wisdom, to thee, O Singer, with. my thoughts and Praises.

4.4.d: कर्णुष्व पाजः परसितिं न पर्थ्वीं याहि राजेवामवां इभेन | तर्ष्वीम अनु परसितिं दरूणानो ऽसतासि विध्य रक्षसस तपिष्ठैः ||
4.4.e: PUT forth like a wide-spreading net thy vigour; go like a mighty King with his attendants.  Thou, following thy swift net, shootest arrows: transfix the fiends with darts that burn most fiercely.

4.4.d: तव भरमास आशुया पतन्त्य अनु सप्र्श धर्षता शोशुचानः | तपूंष्य अग्ने जुह्वा पतंगान असंदितो वि सर्ज विष्वग उल्काः ||
4.4.e: Forth go in rapid flight thy whirling weapons: follow them closely, glowing in thy fury.  Spread with thy tongue the winged flames, O Agni; unfettered, cast thy firebrands all around thee.

4.4.d: परति सपशो वि सर्ज तूर्णितमो भवा पायुर विशो अस्या अदब्धः | यो नो दूरे अघशंसो यो अन्त्य अग्ने माकिष टे वयथिर आ दधर्षीत ||
4.4.e: Send thy spies forward, fleetest in thy motion; be, ne’er deceived, the guardian of this people  From him who, near or far, is bent on evil, and let no trouble sent from thee o’ercome us.

4.4.d: उद अग्ने तिष्ठ परत्य आ तनुष्व नय अमित्रां ओषतात तिग्महेते | यो नो अरातिं समिधान चक्रे नीचा तं धक्ष्य अतसं न शुष्कम ||
4.4.e: Rise up, O Agni, spread thee out before us: burn down our foes, thou who hast sharpened arrows.  Him, blazing Agni! who hath worked us mischief, consume thou utterly like dried-up stubble.

4.4.d: ऊर्ध्वो भव परति विध्याध्य अस्मद आविष कर्णुष्व दैव्यान्य अग्ने | अव सथिरा तनुहि यातुजूनां जामिम अजामिम पर मर्णीहि शत्रून ||
4.4.e: Rise, Agni, drive off those who fight against us: make manifest thine own celestial vigour.  Slacken the strong bows of the demon-driven: destroy our foemen whether kin or stranger.

4.4.d: स ते जानाति सुमतिं यविष्ठ य ईवते बरह्मणे गातुम ऐरत | विश्वान्य अस्मै सुदिनानि रायो दयुम्नान्य अर्यो वि दुरो अभि दयौत ||
4.4.e: Most Youthful God, he knoweth well thy favour who gave an impulse to this high devotion.  All fair days and magnificence of riches hast thou beamed forth upon the good man's portals.

4.4.d: सेद अग्ने अस्तु सुभगः सुदानुर यस तवा नित्येन हविषा य उक्थैः | पिप्रीषति सव आयुषि दुरोणे विश्वेद अस्मै सुदिना सासद इष्टिः ||
4.4.e: Blest, Agni, be the man, the liberal giver, who with his lauds and regular oblation  Is fain to please thee for his life and dwelling. May all his days be bright: be this his longing.

4.4.d: अर्चामि ते सुमतिं घोष्य अर्वाक सं ते वावाता जरताम इयं गीः | सवश्वास तवा सुरथा मर्जयेमास्मे कषत्राणि धारयेर अनु दयून ||
4.4.e: I praise thy gracious favour: sing in answer. May this my song sing like a loved one with thee.  Lords of good steeds and cars may we adorn thee, and day by day vouchsafe thou us dominion.

4.4.d: इह तवा भूर्य आ चरेद उप तमन दोषावस्तर दीदिवांसम अनु दयून | करीळन्तस तवा सुमनसः सपेमाभि दयुम्ना तस्थिवांसो जनानाम ||
4.4.e: Here of free choice let each one serve thee richly, resplendent day by day at eve and morning.  So may we honour thee, content and joyous, passing beyond the glories of the people.

4.4.d: यस तवा सवश्वः सुहिरण्यो अग्न उपयाति वसुमता रथेन | तस्य तराता भवसि तस्य सखा यस त आतिथ्यम आनुषग जुजोषत ||
4.4.e: Whoso with good steeds and fine gold, O Agni, comes nigh thee on a car laden with treasure,  His Friend art thou, yea, thou art his Protector whose joy it is to entertain thee duly.

4.4.d: महो रुजामि बन्धुता वचोभिस तन मा पितुर गोतमाद अन्व इयाय | तवं नो अस्य वचसश चिकिद्धि होतर यविष्ठ सुक्रतो दमूनाः ||
4.4.e: Through words and kinship I destroy the mighty: this power I have from Gotama my father.  Mark thou this speech of ours, O thou Most Youthful, Friend of the House, exceeding wise, Invoker.

4.4.d: अस्वप्नजस तरणयः सुशेवा अतन्द्रासो ऽवर्का अश्रमिष्ठाः | ते पायवः सध्र्यञ्चो निषद्याग्ने तव नः पान्त्व अमूर ||
4.4.e: Knowing no slumber, speedy and propitious, alert and ever friendly, most unwearied,  May thy protecting powers, unerring Agni, taking their places here, combined, preserve us.

4.4.d: ये पायवो मामतेयं ते अग्ने पश्यन्तो अन्धं दुरिताद अरक्षन | ररक्ष तान सुक्र्तो विश्ववेदा दिप्सन्त इद रिपवो नाह देभुः ||
4.4.e: Thy guardian rays, O Agni, when they saw him, preserved blind Māmateya from affliction.  Lord of all riches, he preserved the pious: the fees who fain would harm them did no mischief

4.4.d: तवया वयं सधन्यस तवोतास तव परणीत्य अश्याम वाजान | उभा शंसा सूदय सत्यताते ऽनुष्ठुया कर्णुह्य अह्रयाण ||
4.4.e: Aided by thee with thee may we be wealthy, may we gain strength with thee to guide us onward.  Fulfil the words of both, O Ever Truthful: straightway do this, thou God whom power emboldens.

4.4.d: अया ते अग्ने समिधा विधेम परति सतोमं शस्यमानं गर्भाय | दहाशसो रक्षसः पाह्य अस्मान दरुहो निदो मित्रमहो अवद्यात ||
4.4.e: O Agni, with this fuel will we serve thee; accept the laud we sing to thee with favour  Destroy the cursing Rākṣasas: preserve us, O rich in friends, from guile and scorn and slander.

4.5.d: वैश्वानराय मीळ्हुषे सजोषाः कथा दाशेमाग्नये बर्हद भाः | अनूनेन बर्हता वक्षथेनोप सतभायद उपमिन न रोधः ||
4.5.e: How shall we give with one accord oblation to Agni, to Vaiśvānara the Bounteous?  Great light, with full high growth hath he uplifted, and, as a pillar bears the roof, sustains it.

4.5.d: मा निन्दत य इमाम मह्यं रातिं देवो ददौ मर्त्याय सवधावान | पाकाय गर्त्सो अम्र्तो विचेता वैश्वानरो नर्तमो यह्वो अग्निः ||
4.5.e: Reproach not him who, God and self-reliant, vouchsafed this bounty unto me a mortal,—  Deathless, discerner, wise, to me the simple, Vaiśvānara most manly, youthful Agni.

4.5.d: साम दविबर्हा महि तिग्मभ्र्ष्टिः सहस्ररेता वर्षभस तुविष्मान | पदं न गोर अपगूळ्हं विविद्वान अग्निर मह्यम परेद उ वोचन मनीषाम ||
4.5.e: Sharp-pointed, powerful, strong, of boundless vigour, Agni who knows the lofty hymn, kept secret  As the lost milch-cow's track, the doubly Mighty,—he hath declared to me this hidden knowledge.

4.5.d: पर तां अग्निर बभसत तिग्मजम्भस तपिष्ठेन शोचिषा यः सुराधाः | पर ये मिनन्ति वरुणस्य धाम परिया मित्रस्य चेततो धरुवाणि ||
4.5.e: May he with sharpened teeth, the Bounteous Giver, Agni, consume with flame most fiercely glowing.  Those who regard not Varuṇa's commandments and the dear stedfast laws of sapient Mitra.

4.5.d: अभ्रातरो न योषणो वयन्तः पतिरिपो न जनयो दुरेवाः | पापासः सन्तो अन्र्ता असत्या इदम पदम अजनता गभीरम ||
4.5.e: Like youthful women without brothers, straying, like dames who hate their lords, of evil conduct,  They who are full of sin, untrue, unfaithful, they have engendered this abysmal station.

4.5.d: इदम मे अग्ने कियते पावकामिनते गुरुम भारं न मन्म | बर्हद दधाथ धर्षता गभीरं यह्वम पर्ष्ठम परयसा सप्तधातु ||
4.5.e: To me, weak, innocent, thou, luminous Agni, hast boldly given as ’twere a heavy burthen,  This Pṛṣṭha hymn, profound and strong and mighty, of seven elements, and with offered dainties.

4.5.d: तम इन नव एव समना समानम अभि करत्वा पुनती धीतिर अश्याः | ससस्य चर्मन्न अधि चारु पर्श्नेर अग्रे रुप आरुपितं जबारु ||
4.5.e: So may our song that purifies, through wisdom reach in a moment him the Universal,  Established on the height, on earth's best station, above the beauteous grassy skin of Pṛśni.

4.5.d: परवाच्यं वचसः किम मे अस्य गुहा हितम उप निणिग वदन्ति | यद उस्रियाणाम अप वार इव वरन पाति परियं रुपो अग्रम पदं वेः ||
4.5.e: Of this my speech what shall I utter further? They indicate the milk stored up in secret  When they have thrown as ’twere the cows' stalls open. The Bird protects earths’ best and well-loved station.

4.5.d: इदम उ तयन महि महाम अनीकं यद उस्रिया सचत पूर्व्यं गौः | रतस्य पदे अधि दीद्यानं गुहा रघुष्यद रघुयद विवेद ||
4.5.e: This is the Great Ones’ mighty apparition which from of old the radiant Cow hath followed.  This, shining brightly in the place of Order, swift, hasting on in secret, she discovered.

4.5.d: अध दयुतानः पित्रोः सचासामनुत गुह्यं चारु पर्श्नेः | मातुष पदे परमे अन्ति षद गोर वर्ष्णः शोचिषः परयतस्य जिह्वा ||
4.5.e: He then who shone together with his Parents remembered Pṛśni's fair and secret treasure,  Which, in the Mother Cow's most lofty station, the Bull's tongue, of the flame bent forward, tasted.

4.5.d: रतं वोचे नमसा पर्छ्यमानस तवाशसा जातवेदो यदीदम | तवम अस्य कषयसि यद ध विश्वं दिवि यद उ दरविणं यत पर्थिव्याम ||
4.5.e: With reverence I declare the Law, O Agni; what is, comes by thine order, Jātavedas.  Of this, whate’er it be, thou art the Sovran, yea, all the wealth that is in earth or  heaven.

4.5.d: किं नो अस्य दरविणं कद ध रत्नं वि नो वोचो जातवेदश चिकित्वान | गुहाध्वनः परमं यन नो अस्य रेकु पदं न निदाना अगन्म ||
4.5.e: What is our wealth therefrom, and what our treasure? Tell us O Jātavedas, for thou  knowest,  What is our best course in this secret passage: we, unreproached, have reached a place far distant.

4.5.d: का मर्यादा वयुना कद ध वामम अछा गमेम रघवो न वाजम | कदा नो देवीर अम्र्तस्य पत्नीः सूरो वर्णेन ततनन्न उषासः ||
4.5.e: What is the limit, what the rules, the guerdon? Like fleet-foot coursers speed we to the contest.  When will the Goddesses, the Immortal's Spouses, the Dawns, spread over us the Sun-God's splendour?

4.5.d: अनिरेण वचसा फल्ग्वेन परतीत्येन कर्धुनात्र्पासः | अधा ते अग्ने किम इहा वदन्त्य अनायुधास आसता सचन्ताम ||
4.5.e: Unsatisfied, with speech devoid of vigour, scanty and frivolous and inconclusive,  Wherefore do they address thee here, O Agni? Let these who have no weapons suffer sorrow.

4.5.d: अस्य शरिये समिधानस्य वर्ष्णो वसोर अनीकं दम आ रुरोच | रुशद वसानः सुद्र्शीकरूपः कषितिर न राया पुरुवारो अद्यौत ||
4.5.e: The majesty of him the Good, the Mighty, aflame, hath shone for glory in the dwelling.  He, clothed in light, hath shone most fair to look on, wealthy in boons, as a home shines with riches.

4.6.d: ऊर्ध्व ऊ षु णो अध्वरस्य होतर अग्ने तिष्ठ देवताता यजीयान | तवं हि विश्वम अभ्य असि मन्म पर वेधसश चित तिरसि मनीषाम ||
4.6.e: PRIEST of our rite, stand up erect, O Agni, in the Gods’ service best of sacrificers,  For over evei y thought thou art the Ruler: thou furtherest e’en the wisdom of the pious.

4.6.d: अमूरो होता नय असादि विक्ष्व अग्निर मन्द्रो विदथेषु परचेताः | ऊर्ध्वम भानुं सवितेवाश्रेन मेतेव धूमं सतभायद उप दयाम ||
4.6.e: He was set down mid men as Priest unerring, Agni, wise, welcome in our holy synods.  Like Savitar he hath lifted up his splendour, and like a builder raised his smoke to heaven.

4.6.d: यता सुजूर्णी रातिनी घर्ताची परदक्षिणिद देवतातिम उराणः | उद उ सवरुर नवजा नाक्रः पश्वो अनक्ति सुधितः सुमेकः ||
4.6.e: The glowing ladle, filled with oil, is lifted; choosing Gods’ service to the right he circles.  Eager he rises like the new-wrought pillar which, firmly set and fixed, anoints the victims.

4.6.d: सतीर्णे बर्हिषि समिधाने अग्ना ऊर्ध्वो अध्वर्युर जुजुषाणो अस्थात | पर्य अग्निः पशुपा न होता तरिविष्ट्य एति परदिव उराणः ||
4.6.e: When sacred grass is strewn and Agni kindled, the Adhvaryu rises to, his task rejoicing.  Agni the Priest, like one who tends the cattle, goes three times round, as from of old he wills it.

4.6.d: परि तमना मितद्रुर एति होताग्निर मन्द्रो मधुवचा रतावा | दरवन्त्य अस्य वाजिनो न शोका भयन्ते विश्वा भुवना यद अभ्राट ||
4.6.e: Agni himself, the Priest, with measured motion, goes round, with sweet speech, cheerful, true to Order.  His fulgent flames run forth like vigorous horses; all creatures are affrighted when he blazes.

4.6.d: भद्रा ते अग्ने सवनीक संद्र्ग घोरस्य सतो विषुणस्य चारुः | न यत ते शोचिस तमसा वरन्त न धवस्मानस तन्व रेप आ धुः ||
4.6.e: Beautiful and auspicious is thine aspect, O lovely Agni, terrible when spreading.  Thy splendours are not covered by the darkness: detraction leaves no stain upon thy body.

4.6.d: न यस्य सातुर जनितोर अवारि न मातरापितरा नू चिद इष्टौ | अधा मित्रो न सुधितः पावको ऽगनिर दीदाय मानुषीषु विक्षु ||
4.6.e: Naught hindered his production, Bounteous Giver: his Mother and his Sire were free to send him.  Then as Friend benevolent, refulgent, Agni shone forth in human habitations.

4.6.d: दविर यम पञ्च जीजनन संवसानाः सवसारो अग्निम मानुषीषु विक्षु | उषर्बुधम अथर्यो न दन्तं शुक्रं सवासम परशुं न तिग्मम ||
4.6.e: He, Agni, whom the twice-five sisters, dwelling together, in the homes of men engendered,  Bright like a spear's tooth, wakened in the morning, with powerful mouth and like an axe well-sharpened.

4.6.d: तव तये अग्ने हरितो घर्तस्ना रोहितास रज्वञ्चः सवञ्चः | अरुषासो वर्षण रजुमुष्का आ देवतातिम अह्वन्त दस्माः ||
4.6.e: These thy Bay Coursers, Agni, dropping fatness, ruddy vigorous, speeding straightly forward,  And red steeds, wonderful, of mighty muscle, are to this service of the Gods invited:

4.6.d: ये ह तये ते सहमाना अयासस तवेषासो अग्ने अर्चयश चरन्ति | शयेनासो न दुवसनासो अर्थं तुविष्वणसो मारुतं न शर्धः ||
4.6.e: These brightly-shining games of thine, O Agni, that move for ever restless, all-subduing,  Like falcons hasting eagerly to the quarry, roar loudly like the army of the Maruts.

4.6.d: अकारि बरह्म समिधान तुभ्यं शंसात्य उक्थं यजते वय धाः | होतारम अग्निम मनुषो नि षेदुर नमस्यन्त उशिजः शंसम आयोः ||
4.6.e: To thee, O flaming God, hath prayer been offered. Let the priest laud thee: give to him who worships.  Men have established Agni as Invoker, fain to adore the glory of the living.

4.7.d: अयम इह परथमो धायि धात्र्भिर होता यजिष्ठो अध्वरेष्व ईड्यः | यम अप्नवानो भर्गवो विरुरुचुर वनेषु चित्रं विभ्वं विशे-विशे ||
4.7.e: HERE by ordainers was this God appointed first Invoker, best at worship, to be praised at rites:  Whom Apnavāna, and the Bhṛgus caused to shine bright-coloured in the wood, spreading from home to home.

4.7.d: अग्ने कदा त आनुषग भुवद देवस्य चेतनम | अधा हि तवा जग्र्भ्रिरे मर्तासो विक्ष्व ईड्यम ||
4.7.e: When shall thy glory as a God, Agni, be suddenly shown forth.  For mortal men have held thee fast, adorable in all their homes,

4.7.d: रतावानं विचेतसम पश्यन्तो दयाम इव सत्र्भिः | विश्वेषाम अध्वराणां हस्कर्तारं दमे-दमे ||
4.7.e: Seeing thee faithful to the Law, most sapient, like the starry heaven,  Illumining with cheerful ray each solemn rite in every house.

4.7.d: आशुं दूतं विवस्वतो विश्वा यश चर्षणीर अभि | आ जभ्रुः केतुम आयवो भर्गवाणं विशे-विशे ||
4.7.e: Vivasvān's envoy living men have taken as their ensign, swift,  The ruler over all mankind, moving like Bhṛgu in each home.

4.7.d: तम ईं होतारम आनुषक चिकित्वांसं नि षेदिरे | रण्वम पावकशोचिषं यजिष्ठं सप्त धामभिः ||
4.7.e: Him the intelligent have they placed duly as Invoking Priest,  Welcome, with sanctifying flame, best worshipper, with sevenfold might;

4.7.d: तं शश्वतीषु मात्र्षु वन आ वीतम अश्रितम | चित्रं सन्तं गुहा हितं सुवेदं कूचिदर्थिनम ||
4.7.e: In his Eternal Mothers, in the wood, concealed and unapproached,  Kept secret though his flames are bright seeking on all sides, quickly found.

4.7.d: ससस्य यद वियुता सस्मिन्न ऊधन्न रतस्य धामन रणयन्त देवाः | महां अग्निर नमसा रातहव्यो वेर अध्वराय सदम इद रतावा ||
4.7.e: That as food spreads forth in this earthly udder, Gods may rejoice them in the home of Order,  Great Agni, served with reverence and oblation, flies ever to the sacrifice, the Faithful.

4.7.d: वेर अध्वरस्य दूत्यानि विद्वान उभे अन्ता रोदसी संचिकित्वान | दूत ईयसे परदिव उराणो विदुष्टरो दिव आरोधनानि ||
4.7.e: Bird of each rite, skilled in an envoy's duties, knowing both worlds and that which lies between them,  Thou goest from of old a willing Herald, knowing full well heaven's innermost recesses.

4.7.d: कर्ष्णं त एम रुशतः पुरो भाश चरिष्ण्व अर्चिर वपुषाम इद एकम | यद अप्रवीता दधते ह गर्भं सद्यश चिज जातो भवसीद उ दूतः ||
4.7.e: Bright God, thy path is black: light is before thee: thy moving splendour is the chief of wonders.  When she, yet unimpregnate, hath conceived thee, even when newly born thou art an envoy.

4.7.d: सद्यो जातस्य दद्र्शानम ओजो यद अस्य वातो अनुवाति शोचिः | वर्णक्ति तिग्माम अतसेषु जिह्वां सथिरा चिद अन्ना दयते वि जम्भैः ||
4.7.e: Yet newly born, his vigour is apparent when the wind blows upon his fiery splendour,  His sharpened tongue he layeth on the brushwood, and with his teeth e’en solid food consumeth.

4.7.d: तर्षु यद अन्ना तर्षुणा ववक्ष तर्षुं दूतं कर्णुते यह्वो अग्निः | वातस्य मेळिं सचते निजूर्वन्न आशुं न वाजयते हिन्वे अर्वा ||
4.7.e: When he hath borne off food with swift flame swiftly, strong Agni makes himself a speedy envoy,  Follows the rustling of the wind, consuming, and courser-like, speeds, drives the swift horse onward.

4.8.d: दूतं वो विश्ववेदसं हव्यवाहम अमर्त्यम | यजिष्ठम रञ्जसे गिरा ||
4.8.e: YOUR envoy who possesses all, Immortal, bearer of your gifts,  Best worshipper, I woo with song.

4.8.d: स हि वेदा वसुधितिम महां आरोधनं दिवः | स देवां एह वक्षति ||
4.8.e: He, Mighty, knows the gift of wealth, he knows the deep recess of heaven:  He shall bring hitherward the Gods.

4.8.d: स वेद देव आनमं देवां रतायते दमे | दाति परियाणि चिद वसु ||
4.8.e: He knows, a God himself, to guide Gods to the righteous in his home:  He gives e’en treasures that we love.

4.8.d: स होता सेद उ दूत्यं चिकित्वां अन्तर ईयते | विद्वां आरोधनं दिवः ||
4.8.e: He is the Herald: well-informed, he doth his errand to and fro,  Knowing the deep recess of heaven.

4.8.d: ते सयाम ये अग्नये ददाशुर हव्यदातिभिः | य ईम पुष्यन्त इन्धते ||
4.8.e: May we be they who gratify Agni with sacrificial gifts,  Who cherish and enkindle him.

4.8.d: ते राया ते सुवीर्यैः ससवांसो वि शर्ण्विरे | ये अग्ना दधिरे दुवः ||
4.8.e: Illustrious for wealth are they, and hero deeds, victorious,  Who have served Agni reverently.
