4.8.d: अस्मे रायो दिवे-दिवे सं चरन्तु पुरुस्प्र्हः | अस्मे वाजास ईरताम ||
4.8.e: So unto us, day after day, may riches craved by many come,  And power and might spring up for us.

4.8.d: स विप्रश चर्षणीनां शवसा मानुषाणाम | अति कषिप्रेव विध्यति ||
4.8.e: That holy Singer in his strength shoots forth his arrows swifter than  The swift shafts of the tribes of men.

4.9.d: अग्ने मर्ळ महां असि य ईम आ देवयुं जनम | इयेथ बर्हिर आसदम ||
4.9.e: AGNI, show favour: great art thou who to this pious man art come,  To seat thee on the sacred grass.

4.9.d: स मानुषीषु दूळभो विक्षु परावीर अमर्त्यः | दूतो विश्वेषाम भुवत ||
4.9.e: May he the Immortal, Helper, bard to be deceived among mankind,  Become the messenger of all.

4.9.d: स सद्म परि णीयते होता मन्द्रो दिविष्टिषु | उत पोता नि षीदति ||
4.9.e: Around the altar is he led, welcome Chief Priest at solemn rites,  Or as the Potar sits him down.

4.9.d: उत गना अग्निर अध्वर उतो गर्हपतिर दमे | उत बरह्मा नि षीदति ||
4.9.e: Agni in fire at sacrifice, and in the house as Lord thereof,  And as a Brahman takes his seat.

4.9.d: वेषि हय अध्वरीयताम उपवक्ता जनानाम | हव्या च मानुषाणाम ||
4.9.e: Thou comest as the guide of folk who celebrate a sacrifice,  And to oblations brought by men.

4.9.d: वेषीद व अस्य दूत्यं यस्य जुजोषो अध्वरम | हव्यम मर्तस्य वोळ्हवे ||
4.9.e: Thou servest as his messenger whose sacrifice thou lovest well,  To bear the mortal's gifts to heaven.

4.9.d: अस्माकं जोष्य अध्वरम अस्माकं यज्ञम अङगिरः | अस्माकं शर्णुधी हवम ||
4.9.e: Accept our solemn rite; be pleased, Aṅgiras, with our sacrifice:  Give ear and listen to our call.

4.9.d: परि ते दूळभो रथो ऽसमां अश्नोतु विश्वतः | येन रक्षसि दाशुषः ||
4.9.e: May thine inviolable car, wherewith thou guardest those who give,  Come near to us from every side.

4.10.d: अग्ने तम अद्याश्वं न सतोमैः करतुं न भद्रं हर्दिस्प्र्शम | रध्यामा त ओहैः ||
4.10.e: This day with praises, Agni, we bring thee that which thou lovest.  Right judgment, like a horse, with our devotions.

4.10.d: अधा हय अग्ने करतोर भद्रस्य दक्षस्य साधोः | रथीर रतस्य बर्हतो बभूथ ||
4.10.e: For thou hast ever been the Car-driver, Agni, of noble  Strength, lofty sacrifice, and rightful judgment.

4.10.d: एभिर नो अर्कैर भवा नो अर्वाङ सवर ण जयोतिः | अग्ने विश्वेभिः सुमना अनीकैः ||
4.10.e: Through these our praises come thou to meet us, bright as the sunlight,  O Agni, well disposed, with all thine aspects.

4.10.d: आभिष टे अद्य गीर्भिर गर्णन्तो ऽगने दाशेम | पर ते दिवो न सतनयन्ति शुष्माः ||
4.10.e: Now may we serve thee singing these lauds this day to thee, Agni.  Loud as the voice of Heaven thy blasts are roaring.

4.10.d: तव सवादिष्ठाग्ने संद्र्ष्टिर इदा चिद अह्न इदा चिद अक्तोः | शरिये रुक्मो न रोचत उपाके ||
4.10.e: Just at this time of the day and the night thy look is the sweetest:  It shineth near us even as gold for glory.

4.10.d: घर्तं न पूतं तनूर अरेपाः शुचि हिरण्यम | तत ते रुक्मो न रोचत सवधावः ||
4.10.e: Spotless thy body, brilliant as gold, like clarified butter:  This gleams like gold on thee, O Self. dependent.

4.10.d: कर्तं चिद धि षमा सनेमि दवेषो ऽगन इनोषि मर्तात | इत्था यजमानाद रतावः ||
4.10.e: All hate and mischief, yea, if committed, Agni, thou turnest,  Holy One, from the man who rightly worships.

4.10.d: शिवा नः सख्या सन्तु भरात्राग्ने देवेषु युष्मे | सा नो नाभिः सदने सस्मिन्न ऊधन ||
4.10.e: Agni, with you Gods, prosperous be our friendships and kinships.  Be this our bond here by this place, thine altar.

4.11.d: भद्रं ते अग्ने सहसिन्न अनीकम उपाक आ रोचते सूर्यस्य | रुशद दर्शे दद्र्शे नक्तया चिद अरूक्षितं दर्श आ रूपे अन्नम ||
4.11.e: THY blessed majesty, victorious Agni, shines brightly in the neighbourhood of Sūrya.  Splendid to see, it shows even at nighttime, and food is fair to look on in thy beauty.

4.11.d: वि षाह्य अग्ने गर्णते मनीषां खं वेपसा तुविजात सतवानः | विश्वेभिर यद वावनः शुक्र देवैस तन नो रास्व सुमहो भूरि मन्म ||
4.11.e: Agni, disclose his thought for him who singeth, the well, Strong God! while thou art praised with fervour.  Vouchsafe to us that powerful hymn, O Mighty, which, Radiant One! with all the Gods thou lovest.

4.11.d: तवद अग्ने काव्या तवन मनीषास तवद उक्था जायन्ते राध्यानि | तवद एति दरविणं वीरपेशा इत्थाधिये दाशुषे मर्त्याय ||
4.11.e: From thee, O Agni, springs poetic wisdom, from thee come thoughts and hymns of praise that prosper;  From thee flows wealth, with heroes to adorn it, to the true-hearted man who gives oblation.

4.11.d: तवद वाजी वाजम्भरो विहाया अभिष्टिक्र्ज जायते सत्यशुष्मः | तवद रयिर देवजूतो मयोभुस तवद आशुर जूजुवां अग्ने अर्वा ||
4.11.e: From thee the hero springs who wins the booty, bringer of help, mighty, of real courage.  From thee comes wealth, sent by the Gods, bliss-giving; Agni, from thee the fleet impetuous charger.

4.11.d: तवाम अग्ने परथमं देवयन्तो देवम मर्ता अम्र्त मन्द्रजिह्वम | दवेषोयुतम आ विवासन्ति धीभिर दमूनसं गर्हपतिम अमूरम ||
4.11.e: Immortal Agni, thee whose voice is pleasant, as first in rank, as God, religious mortals  Invite with hymns; thee who removest hatred, Friend of the Home, the household's Lord, unerring.

4.11.d: आरे अस्मद अमतिम आरे अंह आरे विश्वां दुर्मतिं यन निपासि | दोषा शिवः सहसः सूनो अग्ने यं देव आ चित सचसे सवस्ति ||
4.11.e: Far from us thou removest want and sorrow, far from us all ill-will when thou protectest.  Son of Strength, Agni, blest is he at evening, whom thou as God attendest for his welfare.

4.12.d: यस तवाम अग्न इनधते यतस्रुक तरिस ते अन्नं कर्णवत सस्मिन्न अहन | स सु दयुम्नैर अभ्य अस्तु परसक्षत तव करत्वा जातवेदश चिकित्वान ||
4.12.e: WHOSO enkindles thee, with lifted ladle, and thrice this day offers thee food, O Agni,  May he excel, triumphant through thy splendours, wise through thy mental power, O Jātavedas.

4.12.d: इध्मं यस ते जभरच छश्रमाणो महो अग्ने अनीकम आ सपर्यन | स इधानः परति दोषाम उषासम पुष्यन रयिं सचते घनन्न अमित्रान ||
4.12.e: Whoso with toil and trouble brings thee fuel, serving the majesty of mighty Agni,  He, kindling thee at evening and at morning, prospers, and comes to wealth, and slays his foemen.

4.12.d: अग्निर ईशे बर्हतः कषत्रियस्याग्निर वाजस्य परमस्य रायः | दधाति रत्नं विधते यविष्ठो वय आनुषङ मर्त्याय सवधावान ||
4.12.e: Agni is Master of sublime dominion, Agni is Lord of strength and lofty riches.  Straightway the self-reliant God, Most Youthful, gives treasures to the mortal who adores him.

4.12.d: यच चिद धि ते पुरुषत्रा यविष्ठाचित्तिभिश चक्र्मा कच चिद आगः | कर्धी षव अस्मां अदितेर अनागान वय एनांसि शिश्रथो विष्वग अग्ने ||
4.12.e: Most Youthful God, whatever sin, through folly, we here, as human beings, have committed,  In sight of Aditi make thou us sinless remit, entirely, Agni, our offences.

4.12.d: महश चिद अग्न एनसो अभीक ऊर्वाद देवानाम उत मर्त्यानाम | मा ते सखायः सदम इद रिषाम यछा तोकाय तनयाय शं योः ||
4.12.e: Even in the presence of great sin, O Agni, free us from prison of the Gods or mortals.  Never may we who are thy friends be injured: grant health and strength unto our seed and offspring.

4.12.d: यथा ह तयद वसवो गौर्यं चित पदि षिताम अमुञ्चता यजत्राः | एवो षव अस्मन मुञ्चता वय अंहः पर तार्य अग्ने परतरं न आयुः ||
4.12.e: Even as ye here, Gods Excellent and Holy, have loosed the cow that by the foot was tethered,  So also set us free from this affliction long let our life, O Agni, be extended.

4.13.d: परत्य अग्निर उषसाम अग्रम अख्यद विभातीनां सुमना रत्नधेयम | यातम अश्विना सुक्र्तो दुरोणम उत सूर्यो जयोतिषा देव एति ||
4.13.e: AGNI hath looked, benevolently-minded, on the wealth-giving spring of radiant Mornings.  Come, Aśvins, to the dwelling of the pious: Sūrya the God is rising with his splendour.

4.13.d: ऊर्ध्वम भानुं सविता देवो अश्रेद दरप्सं दविध्वद गविषो न सत्वा | अनु वरतं वरुणो यन्ति मित्रो यत सूर्यं दिव्य आरोहयन्ति ||
4.13.e: Savitar, God, hath spread on high his lustre, waving his flag like a spoil-seeking hero.  Their stablished way go Varuṇa and Mitra, what time they make the Sun ascend the heaven.

4.13.d: यं सीम अक्र्ण्वन तमसे विप्र्चे धरुवक्षेमा अनवस्यन्तो अर्थम | तं सूर्यं हरितः सप्त यह्वी सपशं विश्वस्य जगतो वहन्ति ||
4.13.e: Him whom they made to drive away the darkness, Lords of sure mansions, constant to their object,  Him who beholds the universe, the Sun-God, seven strong and youthful Coursers carry onward.

4.13.d: वहिष्ठेभिर विहरन यासि तन्तुम अवव्ययन्न असितं देव वस्म | दविध्वतो रश्मयः सूर्यस्य चर्मेवावाधुस तमो अप्स्व अन्तः ||
4.13.e: Spreading thy web with mightiest Steeds thou comest, rending apart, thou God, the black-hued mantle.  The rays of Sūrya tremulously shining sink, like a hide, the darkness in the waters.

4.13.d: अनायतो अनिबद्धः कथायं नयङङ उत्तानो ऽव पद्यते न | कया याति स्वधया को ददर्श दिवः स्कम्भः समृतः पाति नाकम् ||
4.13.e: How is it that, unbound and not supported, he falleth not although directed downward?  By what self power moves he? Who hath seen it? He guards the vault of heaven, a close-set pillar.

4.14.d: परत्य अग्निर उषसो जातवेदा अख्यद देवो रोचमाना महोभिः | आ नासत्योरुगाया रथेनेमं यज्ञम उप नो यातम अछ ||
4.14.e: THE God hath looked, even Agni Jātavedas, to meet the Dawns refulgent in their glories.  Come on your chariot, ye who travel widely, come to this sacrifice of ours, Nāsatyas.

4.14.d: ऊर्ध्वं केतुं सविता देवो अश्रेज जयोतिर विश्वस्मै भुवनाय कर्ण्वन | आप्रा दयावाप्र्थिवी अन्तरिक्षं वि सूर्यो रश्मिभिश चेकितानः ||
4.14.e: Producing light for all the world of creatures, God Savitar hath raised aloft his banner.  Making his presence known by sunbeams, Sūrya hath filled the firmament and earth and heaven.

4.14.d: आवहन्त्य अरुणीर जयोतिषागान मही चित्रा रश्मिभिश चेकिताना | परबोधयन्ती सुविताय देव्य उषा ईयते सुयुजा रथेन ||
4.14.e: Red Dawn is come, riding with brightness onward, distinguished by her beams, gay-hued and mighty.  Dawn on her nobly-harnessed car, the Goddess, awaking men to happiness, approacheth.

4.14.d: आ वां वहिष्ठा इह ते वहन्तु रथा अश्वास उषसो वयुष्टौ | इमे हि वाम मधुपेयाय सोमा अस्मिन यज्ञे वर्षणा मादयेथाम ||
4.14.e: May those most powerful steeds and chariot bring you, O Aśvins, hither at the break of morning.  Here for your draught of meath are Soma juices: at this our sacrifice rejoice, ye Mighty.

4.14.d: अनायतो अनिबद्धः कथायं नयङङ उत्तानो ऽव पद्यते न | कया याति स्वधया को ददर्श दिवः स्कम्भः समृतः पाति नाकम् ||
4.14.e: How is it that, unbound and unsupported, he falleth not although directed downward?  By what self-power moves he? Who hath seen it? He guards the vault of heaven, a close-set pillar?

4.15.d: अग्निर होता नो अध्वरे वाजी सन परि णीयते | देवो देवेषु यज्ञियः ||
4.15.e: AGNI the Herald, like a horse, is led forth at our solemn rite,  God among Gods adorable.

4.15.d: परि तरिविष्ट्य अध्वरं यात्य अग्नी रथीर इव | आ देवेषु परयो दधत ||
4.15.e: Three times unto our solemn rite comes Agni like a charioteer,  Bearing the viands to the Gods.

4.15.d: परि वाजपतिः कविर अग्निर हव्यान्य अक्रमीत | दधद रत्नानि दाशुषे ||
4.15.e: Round the oblations hath he paced, Agni the Wise, the Lord of Strength,  Giving the offerer precious boons.

4.15.d: अयं यः सर्ञ्जये पुरो दैववाते समिध्यते | दयुमां अमित्रदम्भनः ||
4.15.e: He who is kindled eastward for Sṛñjaya, Devāvata's son,  Resplendent, tamer of the foe.

4.15.d: अस्य घा वीर ईवतो ऽगनेर ईशीत मर्त्यः | तिग्मजम्भस्य मीळ्हुषः ||
4.15.e: So mighty be the Agni whom the mortal hero shall command,  With sharpened teeth and bountiful.

4.15.d: तम अर्वन्तं न सानसिम अरुषं न दिवः शिशुम | मर्म्र्ज्यन्ते दिवे-दिवे ||
4.15.e: Day after day they dress him, as they clean a horse who wins the prize.  Dress the red Scion of the Sky.

4.15.d: बोधद यन मा हरिभ्यां कुमारः साहदेव्यः | अछा न हूत उद अरम ||
4.15.e: When Sahadeva's princely son with two bay horses thought of me,  Summoned by him I drew not back.

4.15.d: उत तया यजता हरी कुमारात साहदेव्यात | परयता सद्य आ ददे ||
4.15.e: And truly those two noble bays I straightway took when offered me,  From Sahadeva's princely son.

4.15.d: एष वां देवाव अश्विना कुमारः साहदेव्यः | दीर्घायुर अस्तु सोमकः ||
4.15.e: Long, O ye Aśvins, may he live, your care, ye Gods, the princely son.  Of Sahadeva, Somaka.

4.15.d: तं युवं देवाव अश्विना कुमारं साहदेव्यम | दीर्घायुषं कर्णोतन ||
4.15.e: Cause him the youthful prince, the son of Sahadeva, to enjoy  Long life, O Aśvins, O ye Gods.

4.16.d: आ सत्यो यातु मघवां रजीषी दरवन्त्व अस्य हरय उप नः | तस्मा इद अन्धः सुषुमा सुदक्षम इहाभिपित्वं करते गर्णानः ||
4.16.e: IMPETUOUS, true, let Maghavan come hither, and let his Tawny Coursers speed to reach us.  For him have we pressed juice exceeding potent: here, praised with song, let him effect his visit.

4.16.d: अव सय शूराध्वनो नान्ते ऽसमिन नो अद्य सवने मन्दध्यै | शंसात्य उक्थम उशनेव वेधाश चिकितुषे असुर्याय मन्म ||
4.16.e: Unyoke, as at thy journey's end, O Hero, to gladden thee today at this libation.  Like Uśanā, the priest a laud shall utter, a hymn to thee, the Lord Divine, who markest.

4.16.d: कविर न निण्यं विदथानि साधन वर्षा यत सेकं विपिपानो अर्चात | दिव इत्था जीजनत सप्त कारून अह्ना चिच चक्रुर वयुना गर्णन्तः ||
4.16.e: When the Bull, quaffing, praises our libation, as a sage paying holy rites in secret,  Seven singers here from heaven hath he begotten, who e’en by day have wrought their works while singing.

4.16.d: सवर यद वेदि सुद्र्शीकम अर्कैर महि जयोती रुरुचुर यद ध वस्तोः | अन्धा तमांसि दुधिता विचक्षे नर्भ्यश चकार नर्तमो अभिष्टौ ||
4.16.e: When heaven's fair light by hymns was made apparent (they made great splendour shine at break of morning),  He with his succour, best of Heroes, scattered the blinding darkness so that men saw clearly.

4.16.d: ववक्ष इन्द्रो अमितम रजीष्य उभे आ पप्रौ रोदसी महित्वा | अतश चिद अस्य महिमा वि रेच्य अभि यो विश्वा भुवना बभूव ||
4.16.e: Indra, Impetuous One, hath waxed immensely: he with his vastness hath filled earth and heaven.  E’en beyond this his majesty extendeth who hath exceeded all the worlds in greatness.

4.16.d: विश्वानि शक्रो नर्याणि विद्वान अपो रिरेच सखिभिर निकामैः | अश्मानं चिद ये बिभिदुर वचोभिर वरजं गोमन्तम उशिजो वि वव्रुः ||
4.16.e: Śakra who knoweth well all human actions hath with his eager Friends let loose the waters.  They with their songs cleft e’en the mountain open and willingly disclosed the stall of cattle.

4.16.d: अपो वर्त्रं वव्रिवांसम पराहन परावत ते वज्रम पर्थिवी सचेताः | परार्णांसि समुद्रियाण्य ऐनोः पतिर भवञ छवसा शूर धर्ष्णो ||
4.16.e: He smote away the floods' obstructer, Vṛtra; Earth, conscious, lent her aid to speed thy thunder.  Thou sentest forth the waters of the ocean, as Lord through power and might, O daring Hero.

4.16.d: अपो यद अद्रिम पुरुहूत दर्दर आविर भुवत सरमा पूर्व्यं ते | स नो नेता वाजम आ दर्षि भूरिं गोत्रा रुजन्न अङगिरोभिर गर्णानः ||
4.16.e: When, Much-invoked! the water's rock thou cleftest, Saramā showed herself and went before thee.  Hymned by Aṅgirases, bursting the cow-stalls, much strength thou foundest for us as our leader.

4.16.d: अछा कविं नर्मणो गा अभिष्टौ सवर्षाता मघवन नाधमानम | ऊतिभिस तम इषणो दयुम्नहूतौ नि मायावान अब्रह्मा दस्युर अर्त ||
4.16.e: Come, Maghavan, Friend of Man, to aid the singer imploring thee in battle for the sunlight.  Speed him with help in his inspired invokings: down sink the sorcerer, the prayerless Dasyu.

4.16.d: आ दस्युघ्ना मनसा याह्य अस्तम भुवत ते कुत्सः सख्ये निकामः | सवे योनौ नि षदतं सरूपा वि वां चिकित्सद रतचिद ध नारी ||
4.16.e: Come to our home resolved to slay the Dasyu: Kutsa longed eagerly to win thy friendship.  Alike in form ye both sate in his dwelling the faithful Lady was in doubt between you.

4.16.d: यासि कुत्सेन सरथम अवस्युस तोदो वातस्य हर्योर ईशानः | रज्रा वाजं न गध्यं युयूषन कविर यद अहन पार्याय भूषात ||
4.16.e: Thou comest, fain to succour him, with Kutsa,—a goad that masters both the Wind-God's horses,  That, holding the brown steeds like spoil for capture, the sage may on the final day be present.

4.16.d: कुत्साय शुष्णम अशुषं नि बर्हीः परपित्वे अह्नः कुयवं सहस्रा | सद्यो दस्यून पर मर्ण कुत्स्येन पर सूरश चक्रं वर्हताद अभीके ||
4.16.e: For Kutsa, with thy thousand, thou at day-break didst hurl down greedy Śuṣṇa, foe of harvest.  Quickly with Kutsa's friend destroy the Dasyus, and roll the chariot-wheel of Sūrya near us.

4.16.d: तवम पिप्रुम मर्गयं शूशुवांसम रजिश्वने वैदथिनाय रन्धीः | पञ्चाशत कर्ष्णा नि वपः सहस्रात्कं न पुरो जरिमा वि दर्दः ||
4.16.e: Thou to the son of Vidathin, Ṛjiśvan, gavest up mighty Mṛgaya and Pipru.  Thou smotest down the swarthy fifty thousand, and rentest forts as age consumes a garment.

4.16.d: सूर उपाके तन्वं दधानो वि यत ते चेत्य अम्र्तस्य वर्पः | मर्गो न हस्ती तविषीम उषाणः सिंहो न भीम आयुधानि बिभ्रत ||
4.16.e: What time thou settest near the Sun thy body, thy form, Immortal One, is seen expanding:  Thou a wild elephant with might invested. like a dread lion as thou wieldest weapons.

4.16.d: इन्द्रं कामा वसूयन्तो अग्मन सवर्मीळ्हे न सवने चकानाः | शरवस्यवः शशमानास उक्थैर ओको न रण्वा सुद्र्शीव पुष्टिः ||
4.16.e: Wishes for wealth have gone to Indra, longing for him in war for light and at libation,  Eager for glory, labouring with praisesongs: he is like home, like sweet and fair nutrition.

4.16.d: तम इद व इन्द्रं सुहवं हुवेम यस ता चकार नर्या पुरूणि | यो मावते जरित्रे गध्यं चिन मक्षू वाजम भरति सपार्हराधाः ||
4.16.e: Call we for you that Indra, prompt to listen, him who hath done so much for men's advantage;  Who, Lord of envied bounty, to a singer like me brings quickly booty worth the capture.

4.16.d: तिग्मा यद अन्तर अशनिः पताति कस्मिञ चिच छूर मुहुके जनानाम | घोरा यद अर्य सम्र्तिर भवात्य अध समा नस तन्वो बोधि गोपाः ||
4.16.e: When the sharp-pointed arrow, O thou Hero, flieth mid any conflict of the people,  When, Faithful One, the dread encounter cometh, then be thou the Protector of our body.

4.16.d: भुवो ऽविता वामदेवस्य धीनाम भुवः सखाव्र्को वाजसातौ | तवाम अनु परमतिम आ जगन्मोरुशंसो जरित्रे विश्वध सयाः ||
4.16.e: Further the holy thoughts of Vamadeva be thou a guileless Friend in fight for booty.  We come to thee whose providence protects us: wide be thy sway for ever for thy singer.

4.16.d: एभिर नर्भिर इन्द्र तवायुभिष टवा मघवद्भिर मघवन विश्व आजौ | दयावो न दयुम्नैर अभि सन्तो अर्यः कषपो मदेम शरदश च पूर्वीः ||
4.16.e: O Indra, with these men who love thee truly, free givers, Maghavan, in every battle,  May we rejoice through many autumns, quelling our foes, as days subdue the nights with splendour.

4.16.d: एवेद इन्द्राय वर्षभाय वर्ष्णे बरह्माकर्म भर्गवो न रथम | नू चिद यथा नः सख्या वियोषद असन न उग्रो ऽविता तनूपाः ||
4.16.e: Now, as the Bhṛgus wrought a car, for Indra the Strong, the Mighty, we our prayer have fashioned,  That he may, ne’er withdraw from us his friendship, but be our bodies' guard and strong defender.

4.16.d: नू षटुत इन्द्र नू गर्णान इषं जरित्रे नद्यो न पीपेः | अकारि ते हरिवो बरह्म नव्यं धिया सयाम रथ्यः सदासाः ||
4.16.e: Now, Indra! lauded, glorified with praises, let power swell. high like rivers for the singer.  For thee a new hymn, Lord of Bays, is fashioned. May we, car-borne, through song be victors ever.

4.17.d: तवम महां इन्द्र तुभ्यं ह कषा अनु कषत्रम मंहना मन्यत दयौः | तवं वर्त्रं शवसा जघन्वान सर्जः सिन्धूंर अहिना जग्रसानान ||
4.17.e: GREAT art thou, Indra; yea, the earth, with gladness, and heaven confess to thee thine high dominion.  Thou in thy vigour having slaughtered Vṛtra didst free the floods arrested by the Dragon.

4.17.d: तव तविषो जनिमन रेजत दयौ रेजद भूमिर भियसा सवस्य मन्योः | रघायन्त सुभ्वः पर्वतास आर्दन धन्वानि सरयन्त आपः ||
4.17.e: Heaven trembled at the birth of thine effulgence; Earth trembled at the fear of thy displeasure.  The stedfast mountains shook in agitation . the waters flowed, and desert spots were flooded.

4.17.d: भिनद गिरिं शवसा वज्रम इष्णन्न आविष्क्र्ण्वानः सहसान ओजः | वधीद वर्त्रं वज्रेण मन्दसानः सरन्न आपो जवसा हतव्र्ष्णीः ||
4.17.e: Hurling his bolt with might he cleft the mountain, while, putting forth his strength, he showed his vigour.  He slaughtered Vṛtra with his bolt, exulting, and, their lord slain, forth flowed the waters swiftly.

4.17.d: सुवीरस ते जनिता मन्यत दयौर इन्द्रस्य कर्ता सवपस्तमो भूत | य ईं जजान सवर्यं सुवज्रम अनपच्युतं सदसो न भूम ||
4.17.e: Thy Father Dyaus esteemed himself a hero: most noble was the work of Indra's Maker,  His who begat the strong bolt's Lord who roareth, immovable like earth from her foundation.

4.17.d: य एक इच चयावयति पर भूमा राजा कर्ष्टीनाम पुरुहूत इन्द्रः | सत्यम एनम अनु विश्वे मदन्ति रातिं देवस्य गर्णतो मघोनः ||
4.17.e: He who alone o’erthrows the world of creatures, Indra the peoples' King, invoked of many-  Verily all rejoice in him, extolling the boons which Maghavan the God hath sent them.

4.17.d: सत्रा सोमा अभवन्न अस्य विश्वे सत्रा मदासो बर्हतो मदिष्ठाः | सत्राभवो वसुपतिर वसूनां दत्रे विश्वा अधिथा इन्द्र कर्ष्टीः ||
4.17.e: All Soma juices are his own for ever, most gladdening draughts are ever his, the Mighty,  Thou ever wast the Treasure-Lord of treasures: Indra, thou lettest all folk share thy bounty.

4.17.d: तवम अध परथमं जायमानो ऽमे विश्वा अधिथा इन्द्र कर्ष्टीः | तवम परति परवत आशयानम अहिं वज्रेण मघवन वि वर्श्चः ||
4.17.e: Moreover, when thou first wast born, O Indra, thou struckest terror into all the people.  Thou, Maghavan, rentest with thy bolt the Dragon who lay against the waterfloods of heaven.

4.17.d: सत्राहणं दाध्र्षिं तुम्रम इन्द्रम महाम अपारं वर्षभं सुवज्रम | हन्ता यो वर्त्रं सनितोत वाजं दाता मघानि मघवा सुराधाः ||
4.17.e: The ever-slaying, bold and furious Indra, the bright bolt's Lord, infinite, strong and mighty,  Who slayeth Vṛtra and acquireth booty, giver of blessings, Maghavan the bounteous:

4.17.d: अयं वर्तश चातयते समीचीर य आजिषु मघवा शर्ण्व एकः | अयं वाजम भरति यं सनोत्य अस्य परियासः सख्ये सयाम ||
4.17.e: Alone renowned as Maghavan in battles, he frighteneth away assembled armies.  He bringeth us the booty that he winneth may we, well-loved, continue in his friendship.

4.17.d: अयं शर्ण्वे अध जयन्न उत घनन्न अयम उत पर कर्णुते युधा गाः | यदा सत्यं कर्णुते मन्युम इन्द्रो विश्वं दर्ळ्हम भयत एजद अस्मात ||
4.17.e: Renowned is he when conquering and when slaying: 'fis he who winneth cattle in the combat.  When Indra hardeneth his indignation all that is fixed and all that moveth fear him.

4.17.d: सम इन्द्रो गा अजयत सं हिरण्या सम अश्विया मघवा यो ह पूर्वीः | एभिर नर्भिर नर्तमो अस्य शाकै रायो विभक्ता सम्भरश च वस्वः ||
4.17.e: Indra hath won all kine, all gold, all horses,—Maghavan, he who breaketh forts in pieces;  Most manly with these men of his who help him, dealing out wealth and gathering the treasure.

4.17.d: कियत सविद इन्द्रो अध्य एति मातुः कियत पितुर जनितुर यो जजान | यो अस्य शुष्मम मुहुकैर इयर्ति वातो न जूत सतनयद्भिर अभ्रैः ||
4.17.e: What is the care of Indra for his Mother, what cares he for the Father who begat him?  His care is that which speeds his might in conflicts, like wind borne onward by the clouds that thunder.

4.17.d: कषियन्तं तवम अक्षियन्तं कर्णोतीयर्ति रेणुम मघवा समोहम | विभञ्जनुर अशनिमां इव दयौर उत सतोतारम मघवा वसौ धात ||
4.17.e: Maghavan makes the settled man unsettled: he scatters dust that he hath swept together,  Breaking in pieces like Heaven armed with lightning: Maghavan shall enrich the man who lauds h;m.

4.17.d: अयं चक्रम इषणत सूर्यस्य नय एतशं रीरमत सस्र्माणम | आ कर्ष्ण ईं जुहुराणो जिघर्ति तवचो बुध्ने रजसो अस्य योनौ ||
4.17.e: He urged the chariot-wheel of Sūrya forward: Etaśa, speeding on his way, he rested.  Him the black undulating cloud bedeweth, in this mid-air's depth, at the base of darkness,

4.17.d: असिक्न्यां यजमानो न होता ||
4.17.e: As in the night the sacrificing priest.

4.17.d: गव्यन्त इन्द्रं सख्याय विप्रा अश्वायन्तो वर्षणं वाजयन्तः | जनीयन्तो जनिदाम अक्षितोतिम आ चयावयामो ऽवते न कोशम ||
4.17.e: Eager for booty, craving strength and horses, we-singers stir Indra, the strong, for friendship,  Who gives the wives we seek, whose succour fails not, to hasten, like a pitcher to the fountain.

4.17.d: तराता नो बोधि दद्र्शान आपिर अभिख्याता मर्डिता सोम्यानाम | सखा पिता पित्र्तमः पित्णां कर्तेम उलोकम उशते वयोधाः ||
4.17.e: Be thou our guardian, show thyself our kinsman, watching and blessing those who pour the Soma;  As Friend, as Sire, most fatherly of fathers giving the suppliant vital strength and freedom.

4.17.d: सखीयताम अविता बोधि सखा गर्णान इन्द्र सतुवते वयो धाः | वयं हय आ ते चक्र्मा सबाध आभिः शमीभिर महयन्त इन्द्र ||
4.17.e: Be helping Friend of those who seek thy friendship . give life, when lauded, Indra, to the singer.  For, Indra, we the priests have paid thee worship, exalting thee with these our sacrifices.

4.17.d: सतुत इन्द्रो मघवा यद ध वर्त्रा भूरीण्य एको अप्रतीनि हन्ति | अस्य परियो जरिता यस्य शर्मन नकिर देवा वारयन्ते न मर्ताः ||
4.17.e: Alone, when Indra Maghavan is lauded, he slayeth many ne’er-resisted Vṛtras.  Him in whose keeping is the well-loved singer never do Gods or mortals stay or hinder.

4.17.d: एवा न इन्द्रो मघवा विरप्शी करत सत्या चर्षणीध्र्द अनर्वा | तवं राजा जनुषां धेह्य अस्मे अधि शरवो माहिनं यज जरित्रे ||
4.17.e: E’en so let Maghavan, the loud-voiced Indra, give us true blessings, foeless, men's upholder.  King of all creatures, give us glory amply, exalted glory due to him who lauds thee.

4.17.d: नू षटुत इन्द्र नू गर्णान इषं जरित्रे नद्यो न पीपेः | अकारि ते हरिवो बरह्म नव्यं धिया सयाम रथ्यः सदासाः ||
4.17.e: Now, Indra! lauded, glorified with praises, let power swell high like rivers for the singer.  For thee a new hymn, Lord of Bays! is fashioned. May we, car-borne, through song be victors ever.

4.18.d: अयम पन्था अनुवित्तः पुराणो यतो देवा उदजायन्त विश्वे | अतश चिद आ जनिषीष्ट परव्र्द्धो मा मातरम अमुया पत्तवे कः ||
4.18.e: THIS is the ancient and accepted pathway by which all Gods have come into existence.  Hereby could one be born though waxen mighty. Let him not, otherwise, destroy his Mother.

4.18.d: नाहम अतो निर अया दुर्गहैतत तिरश्चता पार्श्वान निर गमाणि | बहूनि मे अक्र्ता कर्त्वानि युध्यै तवेन सं तवेन पर्छै ||
4.18.e: Not this way go I forth: hard is the passage. Forth from the side obliquely will I issue.  Much that is yet undone must I accomplish; one must I combat and the other question.

4.18.d: परायतीम मातरम अन्व अचष्ट न नानु गान्य अनु नू गमानि | तवष्टुर गर्हे अपिबत सोमम इन्द्रः शतधन्यं चम्वोः सुतस्य ||
4.18.e: He bent his eye upon the dying Mother: My word I now withdraw. That way I follow.  In Tvaṣṭar's dwelling India drank the Soma, a hundredworth of juice pressed from the mortar.

4.18.d: किं स रधक कर्णवद यं सहस्रम मासो जभार शरदश च पूर्वीः | नही नव अस्य परतिमानम अस्त्य अन्तर जातेषूत ये जनित्वाः ||
4.18.e: What strange act shall he do, he whom his Mother bore for a thousand months and many autumns?  No peer hath he among those born already, nor among those who shall be born hereafter.

4.18.d: अवद्यम इव मन्यमाना गुहाकर इन्द्रम माता वीर्येणा नयॄष्टम | अथोद अस्थात सवयम अत्कं वसान आ रोदसी अप्र्णाज जायमानः ||
4.18.e: Deeming him a reproach, his mother hid him, Indra, endowed with all heroic valour.  Then up he sprang himself, assumed his vesture, and filled, as soon as born, the earth and heaven.

4.18.d: एता अर्षन्त्य अललाभवन्तीर रतावरीर इव संक्रोशमानाः | एता वि पर्छ किम इदम भनन्ति कम आपो अद्रिम परिधिं रुजन्ति ||
4.18.e: With lively motion onward flow these waters, the Holy Ones, shouting, as ’twere, together.  Ask them to. tell thee what the floods are saying, what girdling rock the waters burst asunder.

4.18.d: किम उ षविद अस्मै निविदो भनन्तेन्द्रस्यावद्यं दिधिषन्त आपः | ममैतान पुत्रो महता वधेन वर्त्रं जघन्वां अस्र्जद वि सिन्धून ||
4.18.e: Are they addressing him with words of welcome? Will the floods take on them the shame of Indra?  With his great thunderbolt my Son hath slaughtered Vṛtra, and set these rivers free to wander.

4.18.d: ममच चन तवा युवतिः परास ममच चन तवा कुषवा जगार | ममच चिद आपः शिशवे मम्र्ड्युर ममच चिद इन्द्रः सहसोद अतिष्ठत ||
4.18.e: I cast thee from me, mine,—thy youthful mother: thee, mine own offspring, Kusava hath swallowed.  To him, mine infant, were the waters gracious. Indra, my Son, rose up in conquering vigour.

4.18.d: ममच चन ते मघवन वयंसो निविविध्वां अप हनू जघान | अधा निविद्ध उत्तरो बभूवाञ छिरो दासस्य सम पिणक वधेन ||
4.18.e: Thou art mine own, O Maghavan, whom Vyaṁsa struck to the ground and smote thy jaws in pieces.  But, smitten through, the mastery thou wonnest, and with thy bolt the Dāsa's head thou crushedst.

4.18.d: गर्ष्टिः ससूव सथविरं तवागाम अनाध्र्ष्यं वर्षभं तुम्रम इन्द्रम | अरीळ्हं वत्सं चरथाय माता सवयं गातुं तन्व इछमानम ||
4.18.e: The Heifer hath brought forth the Strong, the Mighty, the unconquerable Bull, the furious Indra.  The Mother left her unlicked Calf to wander, seeking himself, the path that he would follow.

4.18.d: उत माता महिषम अन्व अवेनद अमी तवा जहति पुत्र देवाः | अथाब्रवीद वर्त्रम इन्द्रो हनिष्यन सखे विष्णो वितरं वि करमस्व ||
4.18.e: Then to her mighty Child the Mother turned her, saying, My son, these Deities forsake thee.  Then Indra said, about to slaughter Vṛtra, O my friend Vṛtra, stride full boldly forward.

4.18.d: कस ते मातरं विधवाम अचक्रच छयुं कस तवाम अजिघांसच चरन्तम | कस ते देवो अधि मार्डीक आसीद यत पराक्षिणाः पितरम पादग्र्ह्य ||
4.18.e: Who was he then who made thy Mother widow? Who sought to stay thee lying still or moving?  What God, when by the foot thy Sire thou tookest and slewest, was at hand to give thee comfort?

4.18.d: अवर्त्या शुन आन्त्राणि पेचे न देवेषु विविदे मर्डितारम | अपश्यं जायाम अमहीयमानाम अधा मे शयेनो मध्व आ जभार ||
4.18.e: In deep distress I cooked a dog's intestines. Among the Gods I found not one to comfort.  My consort I beheld in degradation. The Falcon then brought me the pleasant Soma.

4.19.d: एवा तवाम इन्द्र वज्रिन्न अत्र विश्वे देवासः सुहवास ऊमाः | महाम उभे रोदसी वर्द्धम रष्वं निर एकम इद वर्णते वर्त्रहत्ये ||
4.19.e: THEE, verily, O Thunder-wielding Indra, all the Gods here, the Helpers swift to listen,  And both the worlds elected, thee the Mighty, High, waxen strong, alone to slaughter Vṛtra.

4.19.d: अवास्र्जन्त जिव्रयो न देवा भुवः सम्राळ इन्द्र सत्ययोनिः | अहन्न अहिम परिशयानम अर्णः पर वर्तनीर अरदो विश्वधेनाः ||
4.19.e: The Gods, as worn witheld, relaxed their efforts: thou, Indra, born of truth, wast Sovran Ruler.  Thou slewest Ahi who besieged the waters, and duggest out their all-supporting channels.

4.19.d: अत्र्प्णुवन्तं वियतम अबुध्यम अबुध्यमानं सुषुपाणम इन्द्र | सप्त परति परवत आशयानम अहिं वज्रेण वि रिणा अपर्वन ||
4.19.e: The insatiate one, extended, hard to waken, who slumbered in perpetual sleep, O Indra,—  The Dragon stretched against the seven prone rivers, where no joint was, thou rentest with thy thunder.

4.19.d: अक्षोदयच छवसा कषाम बुध्नं वार ण वातस तविषीभिर इन्द्रः | दर्ळ्हान्य औभ्नाद उशमान ओजो ऽवाभिनत ककुभः पर्वतानाम ||
4.19.e: Indra with might shook earth and her foundation as the wind stirs the water with its fury.  Striving, with strength he burst the firm asunder, and tore away the summits of the mountains.

4.19.d: अभि पर दद्रुर जनयो न गर्भं रथा इव पर ययुः साकम अद्रयः | अतर्पयो विस्र्त उब्ज ऊर्मीन तवं वर्तां अरिणा इन्द्र सिन्धून ||
4.19.e: They ran to thee as mothers to their offspring: the clouds, like chariots, hastened forth together.  Thou didst refresh the streams and force the billows: thou, Indra, settest free obstructed rivers.

4.19.d: तवम महीम अवनिं विश्वधेनां तुर्वीतये वय्याय कषरन्तीम | अरमयो नमसैजद अर्णः सुतरणां अक्र्णोर इन्द्र सिन्धून ||
4.19.e: Thou for the sake of Vayya and Turvīti didst stay the great stream, flowing, all-sustaining:  Yea, at their prayer didst check the rushing river and make the floods easy to cross, O Indra.

4.19.d: पराग्रुवो नभन्वो न वक्वा धवस्रा अपिन्वद युवतीर रतज्ञाः | धन्वान्य अज्रां अप्र्णक तर्षाणां अधोग इन्द्र सतर्यो दंसुपत्नीः ||
4.19.e: He let the young Maids skilled in Law, unwedded, like fountains, bubbling, flow forth streaming onward.  He inundated thirsty plains and deserts, and milked the dry Cows of the mighty master.

4.19.d: पूर्वीर उषसः शरदश च गूर्ता वर्त्रं जघन्वां अस्र्जद वि सिन्धून | परिष्ठिता अत्र्णद बद्बधानाः सीरा इन्द्रः सरवितवे पर्थिव्या ||
4.19.e: Through many a morn and many a lovely autumn, having slain Vṛtra, he set free the rivers.  Indra hath set at liberty to wander on earth the streams encompassed pressed together.

4.19.d: वम्रीभिः पुत्रम अग्रुवो अदानं निवेशनाद धरिव आ जभर्थ | वय अन्धो अख्यद अहिम आददानो निर भूद उखछित सम अरन्त पर्व ||
4.19.e: Lord of Bay Steeds, thou broughtest from the ant-hill the unwedded damsel's son whom ants were eating.  The blind saw clearly, as he grasped the serpent, rose, brake the jar: his joints again united.

4.19.d: पर ते पूर्वाणि करणानि विप्राविद्वां आह विदुषे करांसि | यथा-यथा वर्ष्ण्यानि सवगूर्तापांसि राजन नर्याविवेषीः ||
4.19.e: To the wise man, O Sage and Sovran Ruler, the man who knoweth all thine ancient exploits.  Hath told these deeds of might as thou hast wrought them, great acts, spontaneous, and to man's advantage.

4.19.d: नू षटुत इन्द्र नू गर्णान इषं जरित्रे नद्यो न पीपेः | अकारि ते हरिवो बरह्म नव्यं धिया सयाम रथ्यः सदासाः ||
4.19.e: Now, Indra! lauded, glorified with praises, let powers swell high, like rivers, for the singer.  For thee a new hymn, Lord of Bays! is fashioned. May we, car-borne, through song be victors ever.

4.20.d: आ न इन्द्रो दूराद आ न आसाद अभिष्टिक्र्द अवसे यासद उग्रः | ओजिष्ठेभिर नर्पतिर वज्रबाहुः संगे समत्सु तुर्वणिः पर्तन्यून ||
4.20.e: FROM near or far away may mighty Indra giver of succour, come for our protection  Lord of men, armed with thunder, with the Strongest, slaying his foes in conflict, in the battles.

4.20.d: आ न इन्द्रो हरिभिर यात्व अछार्वाचीनो ऽवसे राधसे च | तिष्ठाति वज्री मघवा विरप्शीमं यज्ञम अनु नो वाजसातौ ||
4.20.e: May Indra come to us with Tawny Coursers, inclined to us, to favour and enrich us.  May Maghavan, loud-voiced and wielding thunder, stand by us at this sacrifice, in combat.

4.20.d: इमं यज्ञं तवम अस्माकम इन्द्र पुरो दधत सनिष्यसि करतुं नः | शवघ्नीव वज्रिन सनये धनानां तवया वयम अर्य आजिं जयेम ||
4.20.e: Thou, honouring this our sacrifice, O Indra, shalt give us strength and fill us full of courage.  To win the booty, Thunder-armed! like hunters may we with thee subdue in fight our foemen.

4.20.d: उशन्न उ षु णः सुमना उपाके सोमस्य नु सुषुतस्य सवधावः | पा इन्द्र परतिभ्र्तस्य मध्वः सम अन्धसा ममदः पर्ष्ठ्येन ||
4.20.e: Loving us well, benevolent, close beside us, drink, Godlike Indra, of the well-pressed Soma.  Drink of the meath we offer, and delight thee with food that cometh from the mountain ridges.

4.20.d: वि यो ररप्श रषिभिर नवेभिर वर्क्षो न पक्वः सर्ण्यो न जेता | मर्यो न योषाम अभि मन्यमानो ऽछा विवक्मि पुरुहूतम इन्द्रम ||
4.20.e: Him who is sung aloud by recent sages, like a ripe-fruited tree, a scythe-armed victor,—  I, like a bridegroom thinking of his consort, call hither Indra, him invoked of many;

4.20.d: गिरिर न यः सवतवां रष्व इन्द्रः सनाद एव सहसे जात उग्रः | आदर्ता वज्रं सथविरं न भीम उद्नेव कोशं वसुना नयॄष्टम ||
4.20.e: Him who in native strength is like a mountain, the lofty Indra born or old for conquest,  Terrific wielder of the ancient thunder. filled full with splendour as a jar with water.

4.20.d: न यस्य वर्ता जनुषा नव अस्ति न राधस आमरीता मघस्य | उद्वाव्र्षाणस तविषीव उग्रास्मभ्यं दद्धि पुरुहूत रायः ||
4.20.e: Whom from of old there is not one to hinder, none to curtail the riches of his bounty.  Pouring forth freely, O thou Strong and Mighty, vouchsafe us riches, God invoked of many!

4.20.d: ईक्षे रायः कषयस्य चर्षणीनाम उत वरजम अपवर्तासि गोनाम | शिक्षानरः समिथेषु परहावान वस्वो राशिम अभिनेतासि भूरिम ||
4.20.e: Of wealth and homes of men thou art the ruler, and opener of the stable of the cattle.  Helper of men, winner of spoil in combats, thou leadest to an ample heap of riches.

4.20.d: कया तच छर्ण्वे शच्या शचिष्ठो यया कर्णोति मुहु का चिद रष्वः | पुरु दाशुषे विचयिष्ठो अंहो ऽथा दधाति दरविणं जरित्रे ||
4.20.e: By what great might is he renowned as strongest, wherewith the Lofty One stirs up wild battles?  Best soother of the worshipper's great sorrow, he gives possessions to the man who lauds him.

4.20.d: मा नो मर्धीर आ भरा दद्धि तन नः पर दाशुषे दातवे भूरि यत ते | नव्ये देष्णे शस्ते अस्मिन त उक्थे पर बरवाम वयम इन्द्र सतुवन्तः ||
4.20.e: Slay us not; bring, bestow onus the ample gift which thou hast to give to him who offers.  At this new gift, with this laud sung before thee, extolling thee, we, Indra, will declare it.

4.20.d: नू षटुत इन्द्र नू गर्णान इषं जरित्रे नद्यो न पीपेः | अकारि ते हरिवो बरह्म नव्यं धिया सयाम रथ्यः सदासाः ||
4.20.e: Now, Indra! lauded, glorified with praises, let power swell high, like rivers, for the singer.  A new hymn, Lord of Bays! for thee is fashioned. May we, car-born, through song be victors ever.

4.21.d: आ यात्व इन्द्रो ऽवस उप न इह सतुतः सधमाद अस्तु शूरः | वाव्र्धानस तविषीर यस्य पूर्वीर दयौर न कषत्रम अभिभूति पुष्यात ||
4.21.e: MAY Indra come to us for our protection; here be the Hero, praised, our feast-companion.  May he whose powers are many, waxen mighty, cherish, like Dyaus, his own supreme dominion.

4.21.d: तस्येद इह सतवथ वर्ष्ण्यानि तुविद्युम्नस्य तुविराधसो नॄन | यस्य करतुर विदथ्यो न सम्राट साह्वान तरुत्रो अभ्य अस्ति कर्ष्टीः ||
4.21.e: Here magnify his great heroic exploits, most glorious One, enriching men with bounties,  Whose will is like a Sovran in assembly, who rules the people, Conqueror, all-surpassing.

4.21.d: आ यात्व इन्द्रो दिव आ पर्थिव्या मक्षू समुद्राद उत वा पुरीषात | सवर्णराद अवसे नो मरुत्वान परावतो वा सदनाद रतस्य ||
4.21.e: Hither let Indra come from earth or heaven, hither with speech from firmament or ocean;  With Maruts, from the realm of light to aid us, or from a distance, from the seat of Order.

4.21.d: सथूरस्य रायो बर्हतो य ईशे तम उ षटवाम विदथेष्व इन्द्रम | यो वायुना जयति गोमतीषु पर धर्ष्णुया नयति वस्यो अछ ||
4.21.e: That Indra will we laud in our assemblies, him who is Lord of great and lasting riches,  Victor with Vāyu where the herds are gathered, who leads with boldness on to higher fortune.

4.21.d: उप यो नमो नमसि सतभायन्न इयर्ति वाचं जनयन यजध्यै | रञ्जसानः पुरुवार उक्थैर एन्द्रं कर्ण्वीत सदनेषु होता ||
4.21.e: May the Priest, Lord of many blessings, striving,—who fixing reverence on reverence, giving  Vent to his voice, inciteth men to worship—with lauds bring Indra hither to our dwellings.

4.21.d: धिषा यदि धिषण्यन्तः सरण्यान सदन्तो अद्रिम औशिजस्य गोहे | आ दुरोषाः पास्त्यस्य होता यो नो महान संवरणेषु वह्निः ||
4.21.e: When sitting pondering in deep devotion in Auśija's abode they ply the press-stone,  May he whose wrath is fierce, the mighty bearer, come as the house-lord's priest within our chambers.

4.21.d: सत्रा यद ईम भार्वरस्य वर्ष्णः सिषक्ति शुष्म सतुवते भराय | गुहा यद ईम औशिजस्य गोहे पर यद धिये परायसे मदाय ||
4.21.e: Surely the power of Bhārvara the mighty for ever helpeth to support the singer;  That which in Auśija's abode lies hidden, to come forth for delight and for devotion.

4.21.d: वि यद वरांसि पर्वतस्य वर्ण्वे पयोभिर जिन्वे अपां जवांसि | विदद गौरस्य गवयस्य गोहे यदी वाजाय सुध्यो वहन्ति ||
4.21.e: When he unbars the spaces of the mountains, and quickens with his floods the water-torrents,  He finds in lair the buffalo and wild-ox when the wise lead him on to vigorous exploit.

4.21.d: भद्रा ते हस्ता सुक्र्तोत पाणी परयन्तारा सतुवते राध इन्द्र | का ते निषत्तिः किम उ नो ममत्सि किं नोद-उद उ हर्षसे दातवा उ ||
4.21.e: Auspicious are thy hands, thine arms well-fashioned which proffer bounty, Indra, to thy praiser.  What sloth is this? Why dost thou not rejoice thee? Why dost thou not delight thyself with giving?

4.21.d: एवा वस्व इन्द्रः सत्यः सम्राड ढन्ता वर्त्रं वरिवः पूरवे कः | पुरुष्टुत करत्वा नः शग्धि रायो भक्षीय ते ऽवसो दैव्यस्य ||
4.21.e: So Indra is the truthful Lord of treasure. Freedom he gave to man by slaying Vṛtra.  Much-lauded! help us with thy power to riches: may I be sharer of thy Godlike favour.

4.21.d: नू षटुत इन्द्र नू गर्णान इषं जरित्रे नद्यो न पीपेः | अकारि ते हरिवो बरह्म नव्यं धिया सयाम रथ्यः सदासाः ||
4.21.e: Now, Indra! lauded, glorified with praises, let power swell high, like rivers, for the singer.  For thee a new hymn, Lord of Bays! is fashioned. May we, care-borne, through song be victors ever.

4.22.d: यन न इन्द्रो जुजुषे यच च वष्टि तन नो महान करति शुष्म्य आ चित | बरह्म सतोमम मघवा सोमम उक्था यो अश्मानं शवसा बिभ्रद एति ||
4.22.e: THAT gift of ours which Indra loves and welcomes, even that he makes for us, the Great and Strong One.  He who comes wielding in his might the thunder, Maghavan, gives prayer, praise, and laud, and Soma.

4.22.d: वर्षा वर्षन्धिं चतुरश्रिम अस्यन्न उग्रो बाहुभ्यां नर्तमः शचीवान | शरिये परुष्णीम उषमाण ऊर्णां यस्याः पर्वाणि सख्याय विव्ये ||
4.22.e: Bull, hurler of the four-edged rain-producer with both his arms, strong, mighty, most heroic;  Wearing as wool Paruṣṇī for adornment, whose joints for sake of friendship he hath covered.

4.22.d: यो देवो देवतमो जायमानो महो वाजेभिर महद्भिश च शुष्मैः | दधानो वज्रम बाह्वोर उशन्तं दयाम अमेन रेजयत पर भूम ||
4.22.e: God who of all the Gods was born divinest, endowed with ample strength and mighty powers,  And bearing in his arms the yearning thunder, with violent rush caused heaven and earth to tremble.

4.22.d: विश्वा रोधांसि परवतश च पूर्वीर दयौर रष्वाज जनिमन रेजत कषाः | आ मातरा भरति शुष्म्य आ गोर नर्वत परिज्मन नोनुवन्त वाताः ||
4.22.e: Before the High God, at his birth, heaven trembled, earth, many floods and all the precipices.  The Strong One bringeth nigh the Bull's two Parents: loud sing the winds, like men, in air's mid-region.

4.22.d: ता तू त इन्द्र महतो महानि विश्वेष्व इत सवनेषु परवाच्या | यच छूर धर्ष्णो धर्षता दध्र्ष्वान अहिं वज्रेण शवसाविवेषीः ||
4.22.e: These are thy great deeds, Indra, thine, the Mighty, deeds to be told aloud at all libations,  That thou, O Hero, bold and boldly daring, didst with thy bolt, by strength, destroy the Dragon.

4.22.d: ता तू ते सत्या तुविन्र्म्ण विश्वा पर धेनवः सिस्रते वर्ष्ण ऊध्नः | अधा ह तवद वर्षमणो भियानाः पर सिन्धवो जवसा चक्रमन्त ||
4.22.e: True are all these thy deeds, O Most Heroic. The Milch-kine issued from the streaming udder.  In fear of thee, O thou of manly spirit, the rivers swiftly set themselves in motion.

4.22.d: अत्राह ते हरिवस ता उ देवीर अवोभिर इन्द्र सतवन्त सवसारः | यत सीम अनु पर मुचो बद्बधाना दीर्घाम अनु परसितिं सयन्दयध्यै ||
4.22.e: With joy, O Indra, Lord of Tawny Coursers, the Sisters then, these Goddesses, extolled thee,  When thou didst give the prisoned ones their freedom to wander at their will in long succession.

4.22.d: पिपीळे अंशुर मद्यो न सिन्धुर आ तवा शमी शशमानस्य शक्तिः | अस्मद्र्यक छुशुचानस्य यम्या आशुर न रश्मिं तुव्योजसं गोः ||
4.22.e: Pressed is the gladdening stalk as ’twere a river: so let the rite, the toiler's power, attract thee  To us-ward, of the Bright One, as the courser strains his. exceedingly strong leather bridle.

4.22.d: अस्मे वर्षिष्ठा कर्णुहि जयेष्ठा नर्म्णानि सत्रा सहुरे सहांसि | अस्मभ्यं वर्त्रा सुहनानि रन्धि जहि वधर वनुषो मर्त्यस्य ||
4.22.e: Ever by us perform thy most heroic, thine highest, best victorious deeds, O Victor.  For us make Vṛtras easy to be conquered: destroy the weapon of our mortal foeman.

4.22.d: अस्माकम इत सु शर्णुहि तवम इन्द्रास्मभ्यं चित्रां उप माहि वाजान | अस्मभ्यं विश्वा इषणः पुरंधीर अस्माकं सु मघवन बोधि गोदाः ||
4.22.e: Graciously listen to our prayer, O Indra, and strength of varied sort bestow thou on us.  Send to us all intelligence arid wisdom O Maghavan, be he who gives us cattle.

4.22.d: नू षटुत इन्द्र नू गर्णान इषं जरित्रे नद्यो न पीपेः | अकारि ते हरिवो बरह्म नव्यं धिया सयाम रथ्यः सदासाः ||
4.22.e: Now, Indra! lauded, glorified with praises, let wealth swell high like rivers to the singer.  For thee a new hymn, Lord of Bays, is fashioned. May we, car-borne, through song be victors ever.

4.23.d: कथा महाम अव्र्धत कस्य होतुर यज्ञं जुषाणो अभि सोमम ऊधः | पिबन्न उशानो जुषमाणो अन्धो ववक्ष रष्वः शुचते धनाय ||
4.23.e: How, what priest's sacrifice hath he made mighty, rejoicing in the Soma and its fountain?  Delighting in juice, eagerly drinking, the Lofty One hath waxed for splendid riches.

4.23.d: को अस्य वीरः सधमादम आप सम आनंश सुमतिभिः को अस्य | कद अस्य चित्रं चिकिते कद ऊती वर्धे भुवच छशमानस्य यज्योः ||
4.23.e: What hero hath been made his feast-companion? Who hath been partner in his loving-kindness?  What know we of his wondrous acts? How often comes he to aid and speed the pious toiler?

4.23.d: कथा शर्णोति हूयमानम इन्द्रः कथा शर्ण्वन्न अवसाम अस्य वेद | का अस्य पूर्वीर उपमातयो ह कथैनम आहुः पपुरिं जरित्रे ||
4.23.e: How heareth Indra offered invocation? How, hearing, marketh he the invoker's wishes?  What are his ancient acts of bounty? Wherefore call they him One who filleth full the singer?

4.23.d: कथा सबाधः शशमानो अस्य नशद अभि दरविणं दीध्यानः | देवो भुवन नवेदा म रतानां नमो जग्र्भ्वां अभि यज जुजोषत ||
4.23.e: How doth the priest who laboureth, ever longing, win for himself the wealth which he possesseth?  May he, the God, mark well my truthful praises, having received the homage which he loveth.

4.23.d: कथा कद अस्या उषसो वयुष्टौ देवो मर्तस्य सख्यं जुजोष | कथा कद अस्य सख्यं सखिभ्यो ये अस्मिन कामं सुयुजं ततस्रे ||
4.23.e: How, and what bond of friendship with a mortal hath the God chosen as this morn is breaking?  How, and what love hath he for those who love him, who have entwined in him their firm affection?

4.23.d: किम आद अमत्रं सख्यं सखिभ्यः कदा नु ते भरात्रम पर बरवाम | शरिये सुद्र्शो वपुर अस्य सर्गाः सवर ण चित्रतमम इष आ गोः ||
4.23.e: Is then thy friendship with thy friends most mighty? Thy brotherhood with us,—when may we tell it?  The streams of milk move, as most wondrous sunlight, the beauty of the Lovely One for glory.

4.23.d: दरुहं जिघांसन धवरसम अनिन्द्रां तेतिक्ते तिग्मा तुजसे अनीका | रणा चिद यत्र रणया न उग्रो दूरे अज्ञाता उषसो बबाधे ||
4.23.e: About to stay the Indra-less destructive spirit he sharpens his keen arms to strike her.  Whereby the Strong, although our debts’ exactor, drives in the distant mornings that we know not.

4.23.d: रतस्य हि शुरुधः सन्ति पूर्वीर रतस्य धीतिर वर्जिनानि हन्ति | रतस्य शलोको बधिरा ततर्द कर्णा बुधानः शुचमान आयोः ||
4.23.e: Eternal Law hath varied food that strengthens; thought of eternal Law, removes transgressions.  The praise-hymn of eternal Law, arousing, glowing, hath oped the deaf ears of the living.

4.23.d: रतस्य दर्ळ्हा धरुणानि सन्ति पुरूणि चन्द्रा वपुषे वपूंषि | रतेन दीर्घम इषणन्त पर्क्ष रतेन गाव रतम आ विवेशुः ||
4.23.e: Firm-seated are eternal Law's foundations in its fair form are many splendid beauties.  By holy Law long lasting food they bring us; by holy Law have cows come to our worship.

4.23.d: रतं येमान रतम इद वनोत्य रतस्य शुष्मस तुरया उ गव्युः | रताय पर्थ्वी बहुले गभीरे रताय धेनू परमे दुहाते ||
4.23.e: Fixing eternal Law he, too, upholds it swift moves the might of Law and wins the booty.  To Law belong the vast deep Earth and Heaven: Milch-kine supreme, to Law their milk they render.

4.23.d: नू षटुत इन्द्र नू गर्णान इषं जरित्रे नद्यो न पीपेः | अकारि ते हरिवो बरह्म नव्यं धिया सयाम रथ्यः सदासाः ||
4.23.e: Now, Indra! lauded,—glorified with praises, let power swell high like rivers to the singer.  For thee a new hymn, Lord of Bays, is fashioned. May we, car-borne, through song be victors ever.

4.24.d: का सुष्टुतिः शवसः सूनुम इन्द्रम अर्वाचीनं राधस आ ववर्तत | ददिर हि वीरो गर्णते वसूनि स गोपतिर निष्षिधां नो जनासः ||
4.24.e: WHAT worthy praise will bring before us Indra, the Son of Strength, that he may grant us riches;  For he the Hero, gives the singer treasures: he is the Lord who sends us gifts, ye people.

4.24.d: स वर्त्रहत्ये हव्यः स ईड्यः स सुष्टुत इन्द्रः सत्यराधाः | स यामन्न आ मघवा मर्त्याय बरह्मण्यते सुष्वये वरिवो धात ||
4.24.e: To be invoked and hymned in fight with Vṛtra, that well-praised Indra gives us real bounties.  That Maghavan brings comfort in the foray to the religious man who pours libations.

4.24.d: तम इन नरो वि हवयन्ते समीके रिरिक्वांसस तन्वः कर्ण्वत तराम | मिथो यत तयागम उभयासो अग्मन नरस तोकस्य तनयस्य सातौ ||
4.24.e: Him, verily, the men invoke in combat; risking their lives they make him their protector,  When heroes, foe to foe, give up their bodies, fighting, each side, for children and their offspring.

4.24.d: करतूयन्ति कषितयो योग उग्राशुषाणासो मिथो अर्णसातौ | सं यद विशो ऽवव्र्त्रन्त युध्मा आद इन नेम इन्द्रयन्ते अभीके ||
4.24.e: Strong God! the folk at need put forth their vigour, striving together in the whirl of battle.  When warrior bands encounter one another some in the grapple quit themselves like Indra.

4.24.d: आद इद ध नेम इन्द्रियं यजन्त आद इत पक्तिः पुरोळाशं रिरिच्यात | आद इत सोमो वि पप्र्च्याद असुष्वीन आद इज जुजोष वर्षभं यजध्यै ||
4.24.e: Hence many a one worships the might of Indra: hence let the brew succeed the meal-oblation.  Hence let the Soma banish those who pour not: even hence I joy to pay the Strong One worship.

4.24.d: कर्णोत्य अस्मै वरिवो य इत्थेन्द्राय सोमम उशते सुनोति | सध्रीचीनेन मनसाविवेनन तम इत सखायं कर्णुते समत्सु ||
4.24.e: Indra gives comfort to the man who truly presses, for him who longs  for  it, the Soma,  Not disaffected, with devoted spirit this man he takes to be his friend in battles.

4.24.d: य इन्द्राय सुनवत सोमम अद्य पचात पक्तीर उत भर्ज्जाति धानाः | परति मनायोर उचथानि हर्यन तस्मिन दधद वर्षणं शुष्मम इन्द्रः ||
4.24.e: He who this day for Indra presses Soma, prepares the brew and fries the grains of barley—  Loving the hymns of that devoted servant, to him may Indra give heroic vigour.

4.24.d: यदा समर्यं वय अचेद रघावा दीर्घं यद आजिम अभ्य अख्यद अर्यः | अचिक्रदद वर्षणम पत्न्य अछा दुरोण आ निशितं सोमसुद्भिः ||
4.24.e: When the impetuous chief hath sought the  conflict  , and the lord looked upon the long-drawn battle,  The matron calls to the Strong God whom pressers of Soma have encouraged in the dwelling.

4.24.d: भूयसा वस्नम अचरत कनीयो ऽविक्रीतो अकानिषम पुनर यन | स भूयसा कनीयो नारिरेचीद दीना दक्षा वि दुहन्ति पर वाणम ||
4.24.e: He bid a small price for a thing of value: I was content, returning, still unpurchased.  He heightened not his insufficient offer. Simple and clever, both milk out the udder.

4.24.d: क इमं दशभिर ममेन्द्रं करीणाति धेनुभिः | यदा वर्त्राणि जङघनद अथैनम मे पुनर ददत ||
4.24.e: Who for ten milch-kine purchaseth from me this Indra who is mine?  When he hath slain the Vṛtras let the buyer give him back to me.

4.24.d: नू षटुत इन्द्र नू गर्णान इषं जरित्रे नद्यो न पीपेः | अकारि ते हरिवो बरह्म नव्यं धिया सयाम रथ्यः सदासाः ||
4.24.e: Now, Indra! lauded, glorified with praises, let wealth swell high like rivers for the singer.  For thee a new hymn, Lord of Bays, is fashioned. May we, car-borne, through song be victors ever.

4.25.d: को अद्य नर्यो देवकाम उशन्न इन्द्रस्य सख्यं जुजोष | को वा महे ऽवसे पार्याय समिद्धे अग्नौ सुतसोम ईट्टे ||
4.25.e: WHAT friend of man, God-loving, hath delighted, yearning therefor, this day in Indra's friendship?  Who with enkindled flame and flowing Soma laudeth him for his great protecting favour?

4.25.d: को नानाम वचसा सोम्याय मनायुर वा भवति वस्त उस्राः | क इन्द्रस्य युज्यं कः सखित्वं को भरात्रं वष्टि कवये क ऊती ||
4.25.e: Who hath with prayer bowed to the Soma-lover? What pious man endues the beams of morning?  Who seeks bond, friendship, brotherhood with Indra? Who hath recourse unto the Sage for succour?

4.25.d: को देवानाम अवो अद्या वर्णीते क आदित्यां अदितिं जयोतिर ईट्टे | कस्याश्विनाव इन्द्रो अग्निः सुतस्यांशोः पिबन्ति मनसाविवेनम ||
4.25.e: Who claims to-day the Deities' protection, asks Aditi for light, or the Ādityas?  Of whose pressed stalk of Soma drink the Aśvins, Indra, and Agni, well-inclined in spirit?

4.25.d: तस्मा अग्निर भारतः शर्म यंसज जयोक पश्यात सूर्यम उच्चरन्तम | य इन्द्राय सुनवामेत्य आह नरे नर्याय नर्तमाय नर्णाम ||
4.25.e: To him shall Agni Bhārata give shelter: long shall he look upon the Sun up-rising,  Who sayeth, Let us press the juice for Indra, man's Friend, the Hero manliest of heroes.

4.25.d: न तं जिनन्ति बहवो न दभ्रा उर्व अस्मा अदितिः शर्म यंसत | परियः सुक्र्त परिय इन्द्रे मनायुः परियः सुप्रावीः परियो अस्य सोमी ||
4.25.e: Him neither few men overcome, nor many to him shall Aditi give spacious shelter.  Dear is the pious, the devout, to Indra dear is the zealous, dear the Soma-bringer.

4.25.d: सुप्राव्यः पराशुषाळ एष वीरः सुष्वेः पक्तिं कर्णुते केवलेन्द्रः | नासुष्वेर आपिर न सखा न जामिर दुष्प्राव्यो ऽवहन्तेद अवाचः ||
4.25.e: This Hero curbs the mighty for the zealous: the presser's brew Indra possesses solely:  No brother, kin, or friend to him who pours not, destroyer of the dumb who would resist him.

4.25.d: न रेवता पणिना सख्यम इन्द्रो ऽसुन्वता सुतपाः सं गर्णीते | आस्य वेदः खिदति हन्ति नग्नं वि सुष्वये पक्तये केवलो भूत ||
4.25.e: Not with the wealthy churl who pours no Soma doth Indra, Soma-drinker, bind alliance.  He draws away his wealth and slays him naked, own Friend to him who offers, for oblation.

4.25.d: इन्द्रम परे ऽवरे मध्यमास इन्द्रं यान्तो ऽवसितास इन्द्रम | इन्द्रं कषियन्त उत युध्यमाना इन्द्रं नरो वाजयन्तो हवन्ते ||
4.25.e: Highest and lowest, men who stand between diem, going, returning, dwelling in contentment,  Those who show forth their strength when urged to battle-these are the men who call for aid on Indra.

4.26.d: अहम मनुर अभवं सूर्यश चाहं कक्षीवां रषिर अस्मि विप्रः | अहं कुत्सम आर्जुनेयं नय ॠञ्जे ऽहं कविर उशना पश्यता मा ||
4.26.e: I WAS aforetime Manu, I was Sūrya: I am the sage Kakṣīvān, holy singer.  Kutsa the son of Ārjuni I master. I am the sapient Uśanā behold me.

4.26.d: अहम भूमिम अददाम आर्यायाहं वर्ष्टिं दाशुषे मर्त्याय | अहम अपो अनयं वावशाना मम देवासो अनु केतम आयन ||
4.26.e: I have bestowed the earth upon the Ārya, and rain upon the man who brings oblation.  I guided forth the loudly-roaring waters, and the Gods moved according to my pleasure.

4.26.d: अहम पुरो मन्दसानो वय ऐरं नव साकं नवतीः शम्बरस्य | शततमं वेश्यं सर्वताता दिवोदासम अतिथिग्वं यद आवम ||
4.26.e: In the wild joy of Soma I demolished Śambara's forts, ninety-and-nine, together;  And, utterly, the hundredth habitation, when helping Divodāsa Atithigva.

4.26.d: पर सु ष विभ्यो मरुतो विर अस्तु पर शयेनः शयेनेभ्य आशुपत्वा | अचक्रया यत सवधया सुपर्णो हव्यम भरन मनवे देवजुष्टम ||
4.26.e: Before all birds be ranked this Bird, O Maruts; supreme of falcons be this fleet-winged Falcon,  Because, strong- pinioned, with no car to bear him, he brought to Manu the Godloved oblation.

4.26.d: भरद यदि विर अतो वेविजानः पथोरुणा मनोजवा असर्जि | तूयं ययौ मधुना सोम्येनोत शरवो विविदे शयेनो अत्र ||
4.26.e: When the Bird brought it, hence in rapid motion sent on the wide path fleet as thought he hurried.  Swift he returned with sweetness of the Soma, and hence the Falcon hath acquired his glory.

4.26.d: रजीपी शयेनो ददमानो अंशुम परावतः शकुनो मन्द्रम मदम | सोमम भरद दाद्र्हाणो देवावान दिवो अमुष्माद उत्तराद आदाय ||
4.26.e: Bearing the stalk, the Falcon speeding onward, Bird bringing from afar the draught that gladdens,  Friend of the Gods, brought, grasping fast, the Soma which be bad taken from yon loftiest heaven.

4.26.d: आदाय शयेनो अभरत सोमं सहस्रं सवां अयुतं च साकम | अत्रा पुरंधिर अजहाद अरातीर मदे सोमस्य मूरा अमूरः ||
4.26.e: The Falcon took and brought the Soma, bearing thousand libations with him, yea, ten thousand.  The Bold One left Malignities behind him, wise, in wild joy of Soma, left the foolish.

4.27.d: गर्भे नु सन्न अन्व एषाम अवेदम अहं देवानां जनिमानि विश्वा | शतम मा पुर आयसीर अरक्षन्न अध शयेनो जवसा निर अदीयम ||
4.27.e: I, As I lay within the womb, considered all generations of these Gods in order.  A hundred iron fortresses confined me but forth I flew with rapid speed a Falcon.

4.27.d: न घा स माम अप जोषं जभाराभीम आस तवक्षसा वीर्येण | ईर्मा पुरंधिर अजहाद अरातीर उत वातां अतरच छूशुवानः ||
4.27.e: Not at his own free pleasure did he bear me: he conquered with his strength and manly courage.  Straightway the Bold One left the fiends behind him and passed the winds as he grew yet more mighty.

4.27.d: अव यच छयेनो अस्वनीद अध दयोर वि यद यदि वात ऊहुः पुरंधिम | सर्जद यद अस्मा अव ह कषिपज जयां कर्शानुर अस्ता मनसा भुरण्यन ||
4.27.e: When with loud cry from heaven down sped the Falcon, thence hasting like the wind he bore the Bold One.  Then, wildly raging in his mind, the archer Kṛśānu aimed and loosed the string to strike him.

4.27.d: रजिप्य ईम इन्द्रावतो न भुज्युं शयेनो जभार बर्हतो अधि षणोः | अन्तः पतत पतत्र्य अस्य पर्णम अध यामनि परसितस्य तद वेः ||
4.27.e: The Falcon bore him from heaven's lofty summit as the swift car of Indra's Friend bore Bhujyu.  Then downward hither fell a flying feather of the Bird hasting forward in his journey.

4.27.d: अध शवेतं कलशं गोभिर अक्तम आपिप्यानम मघवा शुक्रम अन्धः | अध्वर्युभिः परयतम मध्वो अग्रम इन्द्रो मदाय परति धत पिबध्यै शूरो मदाय परति धत पिबध्यै ||
4.27.e: And now let Maghavan accept the beaker, white, filled with milk, filled with the shining liquid;  The best of sweet meath which the priests have offered: that Indra to his joy may drink, the Hero, that he may take and drink it to his rapture.

4.28.d: तवा युजा तव तत सोम सख्य इन्द्रो अपो मनवे सस्रुतस कः | अहन्न अहिम अरिणात सप्त सिन्धून अपाव्र्णोद अपिहितेव खानि ||
4.28.e: ALLIED with thee, in this thy friendship, Soma, Indra for man made waters flow together,  Slew Ahi, and sent forth the Seven Rivers, and opened as it were obstructed fountains.

4.28.d: तवा युजा नि खिदत सूर्यस्येन्द्रश चक्रं सहसा सद्य इन्दो | अधि षणुना बर्हता वर्तमानम महो दरुहो अप विश्वायु धायि ||
4.28.e: Indu, with thee for his confederate, Indra swiftly with might pressed down the wheel of Sūrya.  What rolled, all life's support, on heaven's high summit was separated from the great oppressor.

4.28.d: अहन्न इन्द्रो अदहद अग्निर इन्दो पुरा दस्यून मध्यंदिनाद अभीके | दुर्गे दुरोणे करत्वा न याताम पुरू सहस्रा शर्वा नि बर्हीत ||
4.28.e: Indra smote down, Agni consumed, O Indu, the Dasyus ere the noontide in the conflict.  Of those who gladly sought a hard-won dwelling he cast down many a thousand with his arrow.

4.28.d: विश्वस्मात सीम अधमां इन्द्र दस्यून विशो दासीर अक्र्णोर अप्रशस्ताः | अबाधेथाम अम्र्णतं नि शत्रून अविन्देथाम अपचितिं वधत्रैः ||
4.28.e: Lower than all besides hast thou, O Indra, cast down the Dasyus, abject tribes of Dāsas.  Ye drave away, ye put to death the foemen, and took great vengeance with your murdering weapons.

4.28.d: एवा सत्यम मघवाना युवं तद इन्द्रश च सोमोर्वम अश्व्यं गोः | आदर्द्र्तम अपिहितान्य अश्ना रिरिचथुः कषाश चित तत्र्दाना ||
4.28.e: So, of a truth, Indra and Soma, Heroes, ye burst the stable of the kine and horses,  The stable which the bar or stone obstructed; and piercing through set free the habitations.

4.29.d: आ न सतुत उप वाजेभिर ऊती इन्द्र याहि हरिभिर मन्दसानः | तिरश चिद अर्यः सवना पुरूण्य आङगूषेभिर गर्णानः सत्यराधाः ||
4.29.e: COME, lauded, unto us with powers and succours, O Indra, with thy Tawny Steeds; exulting,  Past even the foeman's manifold libations, glorified with our hymns, true Wealth-bestower.

4.29.d: आ हि षमा याति नर्यश चिकित्वान हूयमानः सोत्र्भिर उप यज्ञम | सवश्वो यो अभीरुर मन्यमानः सुष्वाणेभिर मदति सं ह वीरैः ||
4.29.e: Man's Friend, to this our sacrifice he cometh marking how he is called by Soma-pressers.  Fearless, and conscious that his Steeds are noble, he joyeth with the Soma-pouring heroes.

4.29.d: शरावयेद अस्य कर्णा वाजयध्यै जुष्टाम अनु पर दिशम मन्दयध्यै | उद्वाव्र्षाणो राधसे तुविष्मान करन न इन्द्रः सुतीर्थाभयं च ||
4.29.e: Make his cars hear, that he may show his vigour and may be joyful in the way he loveth.  May mighty Indra pouring forth in bounty bestow on us good roads and perfect safety;

4.29.d: अछा यो गन्ता नाधमानम ऊती इत्था विप्रं हवमानं गर्णन्तम | उप तमनि दधानो धुर्य आशून सहस्राणि शतानि वज्रबाहुः ||
4.29.e: He who with succour comes to his implorer, the singer here who with his song invites him;  He who himself sets to the pole swift Coursers, he who hath hundreds, thousands, Thunder-wielder.

4.29.d: तवोतासो मघवन्न इन्द्र विप्रा वयं ते सयाम सूरयो गर्णन्तः | भेजानासो बर्हद्दिवस्य राय आकाय्यस्य दावने पुरुक्षोः ||
4.29.e: O Indra Maghavan, by thee protected may we be thine, princes and priests and singers,  Sharing the riches sent from lofty heaven which yields much food, and all desire its bounty.

4.30.d: नकिर इन्द्र तवद उत्तरो न जयायां अस्ति वर्त्रहन | नकिर एवा यथा तवम ||
4.30.e: O INDRA, Vṛtra-slayer, none is better, mightier than thou:  Verily there is none like thee.

4.30.d: सत्रा ते अनु कर्ष्टयो विश्वा चक्रेव वाव्र्तुः | सत्रा महां असि शरुतः ||
4.30.e: Like chariot-wheels these people all together follow after thee:  Thou ever art renowned as Great.

4.30.d: विश्वे चनेद अना तवा देवास इन्द्र युयुधुः | यद अहा नक्तम आतिरः ||
4.30.e: Not even all the gathered Gods conquered thee, Indra, in the war,  When thou didst lengthen days by night.

4.30.d: यत्रोत बाधितेभ्यश चक्रं कुत्साय युध्यते | मुषाय इन्द्र सूर्यम ||
4.30.e: When for the sake of those oppressed, and Kutsa as he battled,  Thou stolest away the Sun's car-wheel.

4.30.d: यत्र देवां रघायतो विश्वां अयुध्य एक इत | तवम इन्द्र वनूंर अहन ||
4.30.e: When, fighting singly, Indra. thou o’ercamest all the furious Gods, thou slewest those who strove with thee.

4.30.d: यत्रोत मर्त्याय कम अरिणा इन्द्र सूर्यम | परावः शचीभिर एतशम ||
4.30.e: When also for a mortal man, Indra, thou speddest forth the Sun,  And holpest Etaśa with might.

4.30.d: किम आद उतासि वर्त्रहन मघवन मन्युमत्तमः | अत्राह दानुम आतिरः ||
4.30.e: What? Vṛtra-slayer, art not thou, Maghavan, fiercest in thy wrath?  So hast thou quelled the demon too.

4.30.d: एतद घेद उत वीर्यम इन्द्र चकर्थ पौंस्यम | सत्रियं यद दुर्हणायुवं वधीर दुहितरं दिवः ||
4.30.e: And this heroic deed of might thou, Indra, also hast achieved,  That thou didst smite to death the Dame, Heaven's Daughter, meditating ill.

4.30.d: दिवश चिद घा दुहितरम महान महीयमानाम | उषासम इन्द्र सम पिणक ||
4.30.e: Thou, Indra, Mighty One, didst crush Uṣas, though Daughter of the Sky.  When lifting up herself in pride.

4.30.d: अपोषा अनसः सरत सम्पिष्टाद अह बिभ्युषी | नि यत सीं शिश्नथद वर्षा ||
4.30.e: Then from her chariot Uṣas fled, affrighted, from her ruined car.  When the strong God had shattered it.

4.30.d: एतद अस्या अनः शये सुसम्पिष्टं विपाश्य आ | ससार सीम परावतः ||
4.30.e: So there this car of Uṣas lay, broken to pieces, in Vipāś,  And she herself fled far away.

4.30.d: उत सिन्धुं विबाल्यं वितस्थानाम अधि कषमि | परि षठा इन्द्र मायया ||
4.30.e: Thou, Indra, didst. with magic power resist the overflowing stream  Who spread her waters o’er the land.

4.30.d: उत शुष्णस्य धर्ष्णुया पर मर्क्षो अभि वेदनम | पुरो यद अस्य सम्पिणक ||
4.30.e: Valiantly didst thou seize and take the store which Śuṣṇa had amassed,  When thou didst crush his fortresses.

4.30.d: उत दासं कौलितरम बर्हतः पर्वताद अधि | अवाहन्न इन्द्र शम्बरम ||
4.30.e: Thou, Indra, also smotest down Kulitara's son Śambara,  The Dāsa, from the lofty hill.

4.30.d: उत दासस्य वर्चिनः सहस्राणि शतावधीः | अधि पञ्च परधींर इव ||
4.30.e: Of Dāsa Varcin's thou didst slay the hundred thousand and the five,  Crushed like the fellies, of a car.

4.30.d: उत तयम पुत्रम अग्रुवः पराव्र्क्तं शतक्रतुः | उक्थेष्व इन्द्र आभजत ||
4.30.e: So Indra, Lord of Heroes, Powers, caused the unwedded damsel's son,  The castaway, to share the lauds.

4.30.d: उत तया तुर्वशायदू अस्नातारा शचीपतिः | इन्द्रो विद्वां अपारयत ||
4.30.e: So sapient Indra, Lord of Might, brought Turvaśa and Yadu, those  Who feared the flood, in safety o’er.

4.30.d: उत तया सद्य आर्या सरयोर इन्द्र पारतः | अर्णाचित्ररथावधीः ||
4.30.e: Arṇa and Citraratha, both Āryas, thou, Indra, slewest swift,  On yonder side of Sarayu,

4.30.d: अनु दवा जहिता नयो ऽनधं शरोणं च वर्त्रहन | न तत ते सुम्नम अष्टवे ||
4.30.e: Thou, Vṛtra-slayer, didst conduct those two forlorn, the blind, the lame.  None may attain this bliss of thine.

4.30.d: शतम अश्मन्मयीनाम पुराम इन्द्रो वय आस्यत | दिवोदासाय दाशुषे ||
4.30.e: For Divodāsa, him who brought oblations, Indra overthrew  A hundred fortresses of stone.

4.30.d: अस्वापयद दभीतये सहस्रा तरिंशतं हथैः | दासानाम इन्द्रो मायया ||
4.30.e: The thirty thousand Dāsas he with magic power and weapons sent  To slumber, for Dabhīti's sake.

4.30.d: स घेद उतासि वर्त्रहन समान इन्द्र गोपतिः | यस ता विश्वानि चिच्युषे ||
4.30.e: As such, O Vṛtra-slayer, thou art general Lord of kine for all,  Thou Shaker of all things that be.

4.30.d: उत नूनं यद इन्द्रियं करिष्या इन्द्र पौंस्यम | अद्या नकिष टद आ मिनत ||
4.30.e: Indra, whatever deed of might thou hast this day to execute,  None be there now to hinder it.

4.30.d: वामं-वामं त आदुरे देवो ददात्व अर्यमा | वामम पूषा वामम भगो वामं देवः करूळती ||
4.30.e: O Watchful One, may Aryaman the God give thee all goodly things.  May Pūṣan, Bhaga, and the God Karūḷatī give all things fair.

4.31.d: कया नश चित्र आ भुवद ऊती सदाव्र्धः सखा | कया शचिष्ठया वर्ता ||
4.31.e: WITH what help will he come to us, wonderful, ever-waxing Friend;  With what most mighty company?

4.31.d: कस तवा सत्यो मदानाम मंहिष्ठो मत्सद अन्धसः | दर्ळ्हा चिद आरुजे वसु ||
4.31.e: What genuine and most liberal draught will spirit thee with juice to burst  Open e’en strongly-guarded wealth?

4.31.d: अभी षु णः सखीनाम अविता जरित्णाम | शतम भवास्य ऊतिभिः ||
4.31.e: Do thou who art Protector of us thy friends who praise thee  With hundred aids approach us.

4.31.d: अभी न आ वव्र्त्स्व चक्रं न वर्त्तम अर्वतः | नियुद्भिश चर्षणीनाम ||
4.31.e: Like as a courser's circling wheel, so turn thee hitherward to us,  Attracted by the hymns of men.

4.31.d: परवता हि करतूनाम आ हा पदेव गछसि | अभक्षि सूर्ये सचा ||
4.31.e: Thou seekest as it were thine own stations with swift descent of powers:  I share thee even with the Sun.

4.31.d: सं यत त इन्द्र मन्यवः सं चक्राणि दधन्विरे | अध तवे अध सूर्ये ||
4.31.e: What time thy courage and his wheels together, Indra, run their course  With thee and with the Sun alike,

4.31.d: उत समा हि तवाम आहुर इन मघवानं शचीपते | दातारम अविदीधयुम ||
4.31.e: So even, Lord of Power and Might, the people call thee Maghavan,  Giver, who pauses not to think.

4.31.d: उत समा सद्य इत परि शशमानाय सुन्वते | पुरू चिन मंहसे वसु ||
4.31.e: And verily to him who toils and presses Soma juice for thee  Thou quickly givest ample wealth.

4.31.d: नहि षमा ते शतं चन राधो वरन्त आमुरः | न चयौत्नानि करिष्यतः ||
4.31.e: No, not a hundred hinderers can check thy gracious bounty's flow,  Nor thy great deeds when thou wilt act.

4.31.d: अस्मां अवन्तु ते शतम अस्मान सहस्रम ऊतयः | अस्मान विश्वा अभिष्टयः ||
4.31.e: May thine assistance keep us safe, thy hundred and thy thousand aids:  May all thy favours strengthen us.

4.31.d: अस्मां इहा वर्णीष्व सख्याय सवस्तये | महो राये दिवित्मते ||
4.31.e: Do thou elect us this place for friendship and prosperity,  And great celestial opulence.

4.31.d: अस्मां अविड्ढि विश्वहेन्द्र राया परीणसा | अस्मान विश्वाभिर ऊतिभिः ||
4.31.e: Favour us, Indra, evermore with overflowing store of wealth:  With all thy succours aid thou us.

4.31.d: अस्मभ्यं तां अपा वर्धि वरजां अस्तेव गोमतः | नवाभिर इन्द्रोतिभिः ||
4.31.e: With new protections, Indra, like an archer, open thou for us  The stables that are filled with kine.

4.31.d: अस्माकं धर्ष्णुया रथो दयुमां इन्द्रानपच्युतः | गव्युर अश्वयुर ईयते ||
4.31.e: Our chariot, Indra, boldly moves endued with splendour, ne’er repulsed,  Winning for us both kine and steeds.

4.31.d: अस्माकम उत्तमं कर्धि शरवो देवेषु सूर्य | वर्षिष्ठं दयाम इवोपरि ||
4.31.e: O Sūrya, make our fame to be most excellent among the Gods,  Most lofty as the heaven on high.

4.32.d: आ तू न इन्द्र वर्त्रहन्न अस्माकम अर्धम आ गहि | महान महीभिर ऊतिभिः ||
4.32.e: O THOU who slewest Vṛtra, come, O Indra, hither to our side,  Mighty One with thy mighty aids.

4.32.d: भर्मिश चिद घासि तूतुजिर आ चित्र चित्रिणीष्व आ | चित्रं कर्णोष्य ऊतये ||
4.32.e: Swift and impetuous art thou, wondrous amid the well-dressed folk:  Thou doest marvels for our help.

4.32.d: दभ्रेभिश चिच छशीयांसं हंसि वराधन्तम ओजसा | सखिभिर ये तवे सचा ||
4.32.e: Even with the weak thou smitest down him  who is stronger, with thy strength  The mighty, with the Friends thou hast.

4.32.d: वयम इन्द्र तवे सचा वयं तवाभि नोनुमः | अस्मां-अस्मां इद उद अव ||
4.32.e: O Indra, we are close to thee; to thee we sing aloud our songs:  Help and defend us, even us.

4.32.d: स नश चित्राभिर अद्रिवो ऽनवद्याभिर ऊतिभिः | अनाध्र्ष्टाभिर आ गहि ||
4.32.e: As such, O Caster of the Stone, come with thy succours wonderful,  Blameless, and irresistible.

4.32.d: भूयामो षु तवावतः सखाय इन्द्र गोमतः | युजो वाजाय घर्ष्वये ||
4.32.e: May we be friends of one like thee, O Indra, with the wealth of kine,  Comrades for lively energy.

4.32.d: तवं हय एक ईशिष इन्द्र वाजस्य गोमतः | स नो यन्धि महीम इषम ||
4.32.e: For thou, O Indra, art alone the Lord of strength that comes from kine  So grant thou us abundant food.

4.32.d: न तवा वरन्ते अन्यथा यद दित्ससि सतुतो मघम | सतोत्र्भ्य इन्द्र गिर्वणः ||
4.32.e: They turn thee not another way, when, lauded, Lover of the Song,  Thou wilt give wealth to those who praise.

4.32.d: अभि तवा गोतमा गिरानूषत पर दावने | इन्द्र वाजाय घर्ष्वये ||
4.32.e: The Gotamas have sung their song of praise to thee that thou mayst give,  Indra, for lively energy.

4.32.d: पर ते वोचाम वीर्या या मन्दसान आरुजः | पुरो दासीर अभीत्य ||
4.32.e: We will declare thy hero deeds, what Dāsa forts thou brakest down,  Attacking them in rapturous joy.

4.32.d: ता ते गर्णन्ति वेधसो यानि चकर्थ पौंस्या | सुतेष्व इन्द्र गिर्वणः ||
4.32.e: The sages sing those manly deeds which, Indra, Lover of the Song,  Thou wroughtest when the Soma flowed.

4.32.d: अवीव्र्धन्त गोतमा इन्द्र तवे सतोमवाहसः | ऐषु धा वीरवद यशः ||
4.32.e: Indra, the Gotamas who bring thee praises have grown strong by thee.  Give them renown with hero sons.

4.32.d: यच चिद धि शश्वताम असीन्द्र साधारणस तवम | तं तवा वयं हवामहे ||
4.32.e: For, Indra, verily thou art the general treasure even of all .  Thee, therefore, do we invocate.

4.32.d: अर्वाचीनो वसो भवास्मे सु मत्स्वान्धसः | सोमानाम इन्द्र सोमपाः ||
4.32.e: Excellent Indra, turn to us: glad thee among us with the juice  Of Somas, Soma-drinker thou.

4.32.d: अस्माकं तवा मतीनाम आ सतोम इन्द्र यछतु | अर्वाग आ वर्तया हरी ||
4.32.e: May praise from us who think Qn thee, O Indra, bring thee near to us.  Turn thy two Bay Steeds hitherward.

4.32.d: पुरोळाशं च नो घसो जोषयासे गिरश च नः | वधूयुर इव योषणाम ||
4.32.e: Eat of our sacrificial cake: rejoice thee in the songs we sing.  Even as a lover in his bride.

4.32.d: सहस्रं वयतीनां युक्तानाम इन्द्रम ईमहे | शतं सोमस्य खार्यः ||
4.32.e: To India for a thousand steeds well-trained and fleet of foot we pray,  And hundred jars of Soma juice.

4.32.d: सहस्रा ते शता वयं गवाम आ चयावयामसि | अस्मत्रा राध एतु ते ||
4.32.e: We make a hundred of thy kine, yea, and a thousand, hasten nigh:  So let thy bounty come to us.

4.32.d: दश ते कलशानां हिरण्यानाम अधीमहि | भूरिदा असि वर्त्रहन ||
4.32.e: We have obtained, a gift from thee, ten water-ewers wrought of gold:  Thou, Vṛtra-slayer, givest much.

4.32.d: भूरिदा भूरि देहि नो मा दभ्रम भूर्य आ भर | भूरि घेद इन्द्र दित्ससि ||
4.32.e: A bounteous Giver, give us much, bring much and not a trifling gift:  Much, Indra, wilt thou fain bestow.

4.32.d: भूरिदा हय असि शरुतः पुरुत्रा शूर वर्त्रहन | आ नो भजस्व राधसि ||
4.32.e: O Vṛtra-slayer, thou art famed in many a place as bountiful  Hero, thy bounty let us share.

4.32.d: पर ते बभ्रू विचक्षण शंसामि गोषणो नपात | माभ्यां गा अनु शिश्रथः ||
4.32.e: I praise thy pair of Tawny Steeds, wise Son of him who giveth kine  Terrify not the cows with these.

4.32.d: कनीनकेव विद्रधे नवे दरुपदे अर्भके | बभ्रू यामेषु शोभेते ||
4.32.e: Like two slight images of girls, unrobed, upon a new-wrought post,  So shine the Bay Steeds in their course.

4.32.d: अरम म उस्रयाम्णे ऽरम अनुस्रयाम्णे | बभ्रू यामेष्व अस्रिधा ||
4.32.e: For me the Bays are ready when I start, or start not, with the dawn, Innocuous in the ways they take.

4.33.d: पर रभुभ्यो दूतम इव वाचम इष्य उपस्तिरे शवैतरीं धेनुम ईळे | ये वातजूतास तरणिभिर एवैः परि दयां सद्यो अपसो बभूवुः ||
4.33.e: I SEND my voice as herald to the Ṛbhus; I crave the white cow for the overspreading.  Wind-sped, the Skillful Ones in rapid motion have in an instant compassed round the heaven.

4.33.d: यदारम अक्रन्न रभवः पित्र्भ्याम परिविष्टी वेषणा दंसनाभिः | आद इद देवानाम उप सख्यम आयन धीरासः पुष्टिम अवहन मनायै ||
4.33.e: What time the Rbus had with care and marvels done proper service to assist their Parents,  They won the friendship of the Gods; the Sages carried away the fruit of their devotion.

4.33.d: पुनर ये चक्रुः पितरा युवाना सना यूपेव जरणा शयाना | ते वाजो विभ्वां रभुर इन्द्रवन्तो मधुप्सरसो नो ऽवन्तु यज्ञम ||
4.33.e: May they who made their Parents, who were lying like posts that moulder, young again for ever,—  May Vāja, Vibhvan, Ṛbhu, joined with Indra , protect our sacrifice, the Soma-lovers.

4.33.d: यत संवत्सम रभवो गाम अरक्षन यत संवत्सम रभवो मा अपिंशन | यत संवत्सम अभरन भासो अस्यास ताभिः शमीभिर अम्र्तत्वम आशुः ||
4.33.e: As for a year the Ṛbhus kept the Milch-cow, throughout a year fashioned and formed her body,  And through a year's space still sustained her brightness, through these their labours they were made immortal.

4.33.d: जयेष्ठ आह चमसा दवा करेति कनीयान तरीन कर्णवामेत्य आह | कनिष्ठ आह चतुरस करेति तवष्ट रभवस तत पनयद वचो वः ||
4.33.e: Two beakers let us make,—thus said the eldest. Let us make three,—this was the younger's sentence.  Four beakers let us make,—thus spoke the youngest. Tvaṣṭar approved this rede of yours, O Ṛbhus.

4.33.d: सत्यम ऊचुर नर एवा हि चक्रुर अनु सवधाम रभवो जग्मुर एताम | विभ्राजमानांश चमसां अहेवावेनत तवष्टा चतुरो दद्र्श्वान ||
4.33.e: The men spake truth and even so they acted: this Godlike way of theirs the Ṛbhus followed.  And Tvaṣṭar, when he looked on the four beakers resplendent as the day, was moved with envy.

4.33.d: दवादश दयून यद अगोह्यस्यातिथ्ये रणन्न रभवः ससन्तः | सुक्षेत्राक्र्ण्वन्न अनयन्त सिन्धून धन्वातिष्ठन्न ओषधीर निम्नम आपः ||
4.33.e: When for twelve days the Ṛbhus joyed reposing as guests of him who never may be hidden,  They made fair fertile fields, they brought the rivers. Plants spread o’er deserts, waters filled the hollows.

4.33.d: रथं ये चक्रुः सुव्र्तं नरेष्ठां ये धेनुं विश्वजुवं विश्वरूपाम | त आ तक्षन्त्व रभवो रयिं नः सववसः सवपसः सुहस्ताः ||
4.33.e: May they who formed the swift car, bearing Heroes, and the Cow omniform and all-impelling,  Even may they form wealth for us,—the Ṛbhus, dexterous-handed, deft in work and gracious.

4.33.d: अपो हय एषाम अजुषन्त देवा अभि करत्वा मनसा दीध्यानाः | वाजो देवानाम अभवत सुकर्मेन्द्रस्य रभुक्षा वरुणस्य विभ्वा ||
4.33.e: So in their work the Gods had satisfaction, pondering it with thought and mental insight.  The Gods’ expert artificer was Vāja, Indra's Ṛbhukṣan, Varuṇa's was Vibhvan.

4.33.d: ये हरी मेधयोक्था मदन्त इन्द्राय चक्रुः सुयुजा ये अश्वा | ते रायस पोषं दरविणान्य अस्मे धत्त रभवः कषेमयन्तो न मित्रम ||
4.33.e: They who made glad with sacrifice and praises, wrought the two Bays, his docile Steeds, for Indra,—  Ṛbhus, as those who wish a friend to prosper, bestow upon us gear and growth of riches.

4.33.d: इदाह्नः पीतिम उत वो मदं धुर न रते शरान्तस्य सख्याय देवाः | ते नूनम अस्मे रभवो वसूनि तर्तीये अस्मिन सवने दधात ||
4.33.e: This day have they set gladdening drink before you. Not without toil are Gods inclined to friendship.  Therefore do ye who are so great, O Ṛbhus, vouchsafe us treasures at this third libation.

4.34.d: रभुर विभ्वा वाज इन्द्रो नो अछेमं यज्ञं रत्नधेयोप यात | इदा हि वो धिषणा देव्य अह्नाम अधात पीतिं सम मदा अग्मता वः ||
4.34.e: To this our sacrifice come Ṛbhu, Vibhvan, Vāja, and Indra with the gift of riches,  Because this day hath Dhiṣaṇā the Goddess set drink for you: the gladdening draughts have reached you.

4.34.d: विदानासो जन्मनो वाजरत्ना उत रतुभिर रभवो मादयध्वम | सं वो मदा अग्मत सम पुरंधिः सुवीराम अस्मे रयिम एरयध्वम ||
4.34.e: Knowing your birth and rich in gathered treasure, Ṛbhus, rejoice together with the Ṛtus.  The gladdening draughts and wisdom have approached you: send ye us riches with good store of heroes.

4.34.d: अयं वो यज्ञ रभवो ऽकारि यम आ मनुष्वत परदिवो दधिध्वे | पर वो ऽछा जुजुषाणासो अस्थुर अभूत विश्वे अग्रियोत वाजाः ||
4.34.e: For you was made this sacrifice, O Ṛbhus, which ye, like men, won for yourselves aforetime.  To you come all who find in you their pleasure: ye all were—even the two elder—Vājas.

4.34.d: अभूद उ वो विधते रत्नधेयम इदा नरो दाशुषे मर्त्याय | पिबत वाजा रभवो ददे वो महि तर्तीयं सवनम मदाय ||
4.34.e: Now for the mortal worshipper, O Heroes, for him who served you, was the gift of riches.  Drink, Vājas, Ṛbhus! unto you is offered, to gladden you, the third and great libation.

4.34.d: आ वाजा यातोप न रभुक्षा महो नरो दरविणसो गर्णानाः | आ वः पीतयो ऽभिपित्वे अह्नाम इमा अस्तं नवस्व इव गमन ||
4.34.e: Come to us, Heroes, Vājas and Ṛbhukṣans, glorified for the sake of mighty treasure.  These draughts approach you as the day is closing, as cows, whose calves are newly-born, their stable.

4.34.d: आ नपातः शवसो यातनोपेमं यज्ञं नमसा हूयमानाः | सजोषसः सूरयो यस्य च सथ मध्वः पात रत्नधा इन्द्रवन्तः ||
4.34.e: Come to this sacrifice of ours, ye Children of Strength, invoked with humble adoration.  Drink of this meath, Wealth-givers, joined with Indra with whom ye are in full accord, ye Princes.

4.34.d: सजोषा इन्द्र वरुणेन सोमं सजोषाः पाहि गिर्वणो मरुद्भिः | अग्रेपाभिर रतुपाभिः सजोषा गनास्पत्नीभी रत्नधाभिः सजोषाः ||
4.34.e: Close knit with Varuṇa drink the Soma, Indra; close-knit, Hymn-lover! with the Maruts drink it:  Close-knit with drinkers first, who drink in season; close-knit with heavenly Dames who give us treasures.

4.34.d: सजोषस आदित्यैर मादयध्वं सजोषस रभवः पर्वतेभिः | सजोषसो दैव्येना सवित्रा सजोषसः सिन्धुभी रत्नधेभिः ||
4.34.e: Rejoice in full accord with the Ādityas, in concord with the Parvatas, O Ṛbhus;  In full accord with Savitar, Divine One; in full accord with floods that pour forth riches.

4.34.d: ये अश्विना ये पितरा य ऊती धेनुं ततक्षुर रभवो ये अश्वा | ये अंसत्रा य रधग रोदसी ये विभ्वो नरः सवपत्यानि चक्रुः ||
4.34.e: Ṛbhus, who helped their Parents and the Aśvins, who formed the Milch-cow and the pair of horses,  Made armour, set the heaven and earth asunder,—far- reaching Heroes, they have made good offspring.

4.34.d: ये गोमन्तं वाजवन्तं सुवीरं रयिं धत्थ वसुमन्तम पुरुक्षुम | ते अग्रेपा रभवो मन्दसाना अस्मे धत्त ये च रातिं गर्णन्ति ||
4.34.e: Ye who have wealth in cattle and in booty, in heroes, in rich sustenance and treasure,  Such, O ye Ṛbhus, first to drink, rejoicing, give unto us and those who laud our present.

4.34.d: नापाभूत न वो ऽतीत्र्षामानिःशस्ता रभवो यज्ञे अस्मिन | सम इन्द्रेण मदथ सम मरुद्भिः सं राजभी रत्नधेयाय देवाः ||
4.34.e: Ye were not far: we have not left you thirsting, blameless in this our sacrifice, O Ṛbhus.  Rejoice you with the Maruts and with Indra, with the Kings, Gods! that ye may give us riches.

4.35.d: इहोप यात शवसो नपातः सौधन्वना रभवो माप भूत | अस्मिन हि वः सवने रत्नधेयं गमन्त्व इन्द्रम अनु वो मदासः ||
4.35.e: Come hither, O ye Sons of Strength, ye Ṛbhus; stay not afar, ye Children of Sudhanvan.  At this libation is your gift of treasure. Let gladdening draughts approach you after Indra's.

4.35.d: आगन्न रभूणाम इह रत्नधेयम अभूत सोमस्य सुषुतस्य पीतिः | सुक्र्त्यया यत सवपस्यया चं एकं विचक्र चमसं चतुर्धा ||
4.35.e: Hither is come the Ṛbhus' gift of riches; here was the drinking of the well-pressed Soma,  Since by dexterity and skill as craftsmen ye made the single chalice to be fourfold

4.35.d: वय अक्र्णोत चमसं चतुर्धा सखे वि शिक्षेत्य अब्रवीत | अथैत वाजा अम्र्तस्य पन्थां गणं देवानाम रभवः सुहस्ताः ||
4.35.e: Ye made fourfold the chalice that wag single: ye spake these words and said, O Friend, assist us;  Then, Vājas! gained the path of life eternal, deft-handed Ṛbhus, to the Gods’ assembly.

4.35.d: किम्मयः सविच चमस एष आस यं काव्येन चतुरो विचक्र | अथा सुनुध्वं सवनम मदाय पात रभवो मधुनः सोम्यस्य ||
4.35.e: Out of what substance was that chalice fashioned which ye made fourfold by your art and wisdom?  Now for the gladdening draught press out the liquor, and drink, O Ṛbhus, of die meath of Soma.

4.35.d: शच्याकर्त पितरा युवाना शच्याकर्त चमसं देवपानम | शच्या हरी धनुतराव अतष्टेन्द्रवाहाव रभवो वाजरत्नाः ||
4.35.e: Ye with your cunning made your Parents youthful; the cup, for Gods to drink, ye formed with cunning;  With cunning, Ṛbhus, rich in treasure, fashioned the two swift Tawny Steeds who carry Indra.

4.35.d: यो वः सुनोत्य अभिपित्वे अह्नां तीव्रं वाजासः सवनम मदाय | तस्मै रयिम रभवः सर्ववीरम आ तक्षत वर्षणो मन्दसानाः ||
4.35.e: Whoso pours out for you, when days are closing, the sharp libation for your joy, O Vājas,  For him, O mighty Ṛbhus, ye, rejoicing, have fashioned wealth with plenteous store of heroes.

4.35.d: परातः सुतम अपिबो हर्यश्व माध्यंदिनं सवनं केवलं ते | सम रभुभिः पिबस्व रत्नधेभिः सखींर यां इन्द्र चक्र्षे सुक्र्त्या ||
4.35.e: Lord of Bay Steeds, at dawn the juice thou drankest: thine, only thine, is the noonday libation.  Now drink thou with the wealth-bestowing Ṛbhus, whom for their skill thou madest friends, O Indra.

4.35.d: ये देवासो अभवता सुक्र्त्या शयेना इवेद अधि दिवि निषेद | ते रत्नं धात शवसो नपातः सौधन्वना अभवताम्र्तासः ||
4.35.e: Ye, whom your artist skill hath raised to Godhead have set you down above in heaven like falcons.  So give us riches, Children of Sudhanvan, O Sons of Strength; ye have become immortal.

4.35.d: यत तर्तीयं सवनं रत्नधेयम अक्र्णुध्वं सवपस्या सुहस्ताः | तद रभवः परिषिक्तं व एतत सम मदेभिर इन्द्रियेभिः पिबध्वम ||
4.35.e: The third libation, that bestoweth treasure, which ye have won by skill, ye dexterous-handed,—  This drink hath been effused for you, O Ṛbhus . drink it with high delight, with joy like Indra's.

4.36.d: अनश्वो जातो अनभीशुर उक्थ्यो रथस तरिचक्रः परि वर्तते रजः | महत तद वो देव्यस्य परवाचनं दयाम रभवः पर्थिवीं यच च पुष्यथ ||
4.36.e: THE car that was not made for horses or for reins, three-wheeled, worthy of lauds, rolls round the firmament.  That is the great announcement of your Deity, that, O ye Ṛbhus, ye sustain the earth and heaven.

4.36.d: रथं ये चक्रुः सुव्र्तं सुचेतसो ऽविह्वरन्तम मनसस परि धयया | तां ऊ नव अस्य सवनस्य पीतय आ वो वाजा रभवो वेदयामसि ||
4.36.e: Ye Sapient Ones who made the lightly-rolling car out of your mind, by thought, the car that never errs,  You, being such, to drink of this drink-offering, you, O ye Vājas, and ye Ṛbhus, we invoke.

4.36.d: तद वो वाजा रभवः सुप्रवाचनं देवेषु विभ्वो अभवन महित्वनम | जिव्री यत सन्ता पितरा सनाजुरा पुनर युवाना चरथाय तक्षथ ||
4.36.e: O Vājas, Ṛbhus, reaching far, among the Gods this was your exaltation gloriously declared,  In that your aged Parents, worn with length of days, ye wrought again to youth so that they moved at will.

4.36.d: एकं वि चक्र चमसं चतुर्वयं निश चर्मणो गाम अरिणीत धीतिभिः | अथा देवेष्व अम्र्तत्वम आनश शरुष्टी वाजा रभवस तद व उक्थ्यम ||
4.36.e: The chalice that wag single ye have made fourfold, and by your wisdom brought the Cow forth from the hide.  So quickly, mid the Gods, ye gained immortal life. Vājas and Ṛbhus, your great work must be extolled.

4.36.d: रभुतो रयिः परथमश्रवस्तमो वाजश्रुतासो यम अजीजनन नरः | विभ्वतष्टो विदथेषु परवाच्यो यं देवासो ऽवथा स विचर्षणिः ||
4.36.e: Wealth from the Ṛbhus is most glorious in renown, that which the Heroes, famed for vigour, have produced.  In synods must be sung the car which Vibhvan wrought: that which ye favour, Gods! is famed among mankind.

4.36.d: स वाज्य अर्वा स रषिर वचस्यया स शूरो अस्ता पर्तनासु दुष्टरः | स रायस पोषं स सुवीर्यं दधे यं वाजो विभ्वां रभवो यम आविषुः ||
4.36.e: Strong is the steed, the man a sage in eloquence, the bowman is a hero hard to beat in fight,  Great store of wealth and manly power hath he obtained whom Vāja, Vibhvan, Ṛbhus have looked kindly on.

4.36.d: शरेष्ठं वः पेशो अधि धायि दर्शतं सतोमो वाजा रभवस तं जुजुष्टन | धीरासो हि षठा कवयो विपश्चितस तान व एना बरह्मणा वेदयामसि ||
4.36.e: To you hath been assigned the fairest ornament, the hymn of praise: Vājas and Ṛbhus, joy therein;  For ye have lore and wisdom and poetic skill: as such, with this our prayer we call on you to come.

4.36.d: यूयम अस्मभ्यं धिषणाभ्यस परि विद्वांसो विश्वा नर्याणि भोजना | दयुमन्तं वाजं वर्षशुष्मम उत्तमम आ नो रयिम रभवस तक्षता वयः ||
4.36.e: According to the wishes of our hearts may ye, who have full knowledge of all the delights of men,  Fashion for us, O Ṛbhus, power and splendid wealth, rich in high courage, excellent, and vital strength.

4.36.d: इह परजाम इह रयिं रराणा इह शरवो वीरवत तक्षता नः | येन वयं चितयेमात्य अन्यान तं वाजं चित्रम रभवो ददा नः ||
4.36.e: Bestowing on us here riches and offspring, here fashion fame for us befitting heroes.  Vouchsafe us wealth of splendid sort, O Ṛbhus, that we may make us more renowned than others.
